question: The length of the common chord of two circles of radii 15 cm and 13 cm, whose centres are 14 cm apart, is:
solution:
Given:

Radii of circles are 13 cm and 15 cm 

Distance between centres = 14 cm 

Concept Used:

The line joining the centers of two circles is the perpendicular bisector of the common chord of the two circles.

⇒ AB = 2AM

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6008f37fd7b12402914c8a9d494de1501df6065c15024a36901891c01373a2bd.png] 

From the figure, P and Q are the centers of two circles of radius 15 cm and 13cm respectively and AB is the common chord

In ΔAMP, PA = 15 cm

By Pythagoras theorem,

AM² = PA² - PM²

⇒ AM2 = 152 - PM2

⇒ AM2 = 225 - PM2 -----(1)

In ΔAMQ, QA = 13 cm

By Pythagoras theorem,

AM2 = QA2 - MQ2

⇒ AM2 = 132 - MQ2

⇒ AM2 = 169 - MQ2 -----(2)

From (1) and (2)

225 - PM2 = 169 - MQ2 

⇒ PM2 - MQ2 = 56

⇒ (PM + MQ) (PM - MQ) = 56

According to the question,

(PM + MQ) = PQ = Distance between centres = 14 cm ----(3)

⇒ 14 (PM - MQ) = 56

⇒ (PM - MQ) = 56/14 = 4 ----(4)

From (3) and (4)

PM = 9 cm

Putting value of PM in (1)

AM2 = 225 - 92

⇒ AM2 = 225 - 81

⇒ AM2 = 144

⇒ AM = 12 cm

Thus, length of common chord = AB = 2AM = 24 cm

**∴ The length of the common chord is 24 cm.**

question: Let O be the centre of the circle and AB and CD are two parallel chords on the same side of the radius. OP is perpendicular to AB and OQ is perpendicular to CD. If AB = 10 cm, CD = 24 cm and PQ = 7 cm, then the diameter (in cm) of the circle is equal to:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The half-lengths of the parallel chords are 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm and 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm.

Notice the common Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13) where 13 represents the hypotenuse (radius).

The distances from the centre for these chords would be 12 cm and 5 cm.

Difference in perpendicular distances = 12 − 5 = 7 cm, which perfectly matches the given PQ.

Thus, the radius is 13 cm, meaning the diameter is 2 × 13 = 26 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 26 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

AB = 10 cm, CD = 24 cm, PQ = 7 cm

OP ⊥ AB and OQ ⊥ CD

**Formula Used:**

A perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord into two equal halves.

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

**Calculations:**

⇒ AP = AB ÷ 2 = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm

⇒ CQ = CD ÷ 2 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm

⇒ Let the radius of the circle be r and the distance OQ = x.

⇒ Since chords are on the same side of the centre, OP = OQ + PQ = x + 7

⇒ In right-angled ΔOQC: r² = OQ² + CQ²

⇒ r² = x² + 12² = x² + 144 --- (i)

⇒ In right-angled ΔOPA: r² = OP² + AP²

⇒ r² = (x + 7)² + 5² = x² + 14x + 49 + 25 = x² + 14x + 74 --- (ii)

⇒ Equating (i) and (ii): x² + 144 = x² + 14x + 74

⇒ 14x = 144 − 74 = 70

⇒ x = 5 cm

⇒ Substitute the value of x in (i):

⇒ r² = 5² + 144 = 25 + 144 = 169

⇒ r = √169 = 13 cm

⇒ Diameter of the circle = 2 × 13 = 26 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 26 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular from Centre to Chord

A perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to any chord bisects the chord into two equal halves. This forms a right-angled triangle where the radius is the hypotenuse.

Distance Between Parallel Chords

If two parallel chords lie on the same side of the centre, the distance between them is the difference of their perpendicular distances from the centre (d = |d₁ − d₂|). If they lie on opposite sides, the distance is the sum (d = d₁ + d₂).

Pythagorean Triplets in Circle Geometry

Commonly repeating triplets like (3, 4, 5) or (5, 12, 13) or (8, 15, 17) very frequently satisfy the values of the radius, half-chord, and perpendicular distance. Spotting them saves calculation time.
</p

question: P and Q are centres of two circles whose radii are 7 cm and 3 cm, respectively. If the direct common tangents to the circles meet PQ extended at A, then A divides PQ ________.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the properties of common tangents to circles, the point of intersection of the direct common tangents divides the line joining their centres externally in the ratio of their radii.

⇒ Ratio = r₁ : r₂

⇒ Ratio = 7 : 3

Since the direct common tangents meet outside the segment connecting the centres, the division is external.

**∴ The correct answer is externally in the ratio 7 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the circle with centre P, r₁ = 7 cm

Radius of the circle with centre Q, r₂ = 3 cm

A is the point of intersection of the direct common tangents on PQ extended.

**Formula Used:**

For similar triangles, the ratio of their corresponding sides is always equal.

**Calculations:**

Let T₁ and T₂ be the points of contact of the direct common tangent on the two circles.

In ΔAPT₁ and ΔAQT₂,

⇒ ∠A = ∠A (Common angle)

⇒ ∠PT₁A = ∠QT₂A = 90° (The radius is always perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact)

⇒ ΔAPT₁ ∼ ΔAQT₂ (By AA similarity criterion)

Therefore, the ratio of their corresponding sides will be equal:

⇒ AP / AQ = PT₁ / QT₂

⇒ AP / AQ = 7 / 3

⇒ AP : AQ = 7 : 3

Since the direct common tangents meet on the line joining the centres extended beyond Q, point A lies completely outside the segment PQ.

⇒ A divides the line segment PQ externally in the ratio 7 : 3.

**∴ The correct answer is externally in the ratio 7 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Common Tangent (DCT) Intersection

The intersection point of the direct common tangents divides the line segment joining the centres of the two circles externally in the ratio of their radii (r₁ : r₂).

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT) Intersection

The intersection point of the transverse common tangents divides the line segment joining the centres of the two circles internally in the ratio of their radii (r₁ : r₂).

Length of Direct Common Tangent

The length of the DCT between two circles with centres separated by a distance d is given by: √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²).

Length of Transverse Common Tangent

The length of the TCT between two circles with centres separated by a distance d is given by: √(d² − (r₁ + r₂)²).

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two circles touch each other externally, the distance between their centers is (R + r).

The formula for the length of the Direct Common Tangent (DCT) simplifies directly to: DCT = 2√(R × r)

Given the radii R = 16 cm and r = 8 cm:

⇒ DCT = 2√(16 × 8)

⇒ DCT = 2√(128) = 2 × 8√2 = 16√2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 16√2 cm.**

**Given:**

Radius of first circle (R) = 16 cm

Radius of second circle (r) = 8 cm

Since the circles touch externally, the distance between their centers (d) is the sum of their radii.

⇒ d = R + r = 16 + 8 = 24 cm

**Formula Used:**

Length of Direct Common Tangent (DCT) = √[d² − (R − r)²]

**Calculation:**

⇒ R − r = 16 − 8 = 8 cm

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

The general formula for the length of a direct common tangent is √[d² − (r₁ − r₂)²], where d is the distance between the centers. They do not cross the line segment connecting the centers.

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

The formula for the length of a transverse common tangent is √[d² − (r₁ + r₂)²]. A TCT always crosses the line segment joining the centers of the two circles.

Number of Common Tangents

Two completely separate circles have 4 common tangents (2 DCT, 2 TCT). If they touch externally, they have 3. Intersecting circles have 2. Circles touching internally have 1, and one inside the other has 0.

question: From a point T, the length of the tangent to a circle is 32 cm and the distance of T from the centre is 40 cm. The diameter (in cm) of the circle is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The radius, tangent, and distance to the centre form a right-angled triangle.

The ratio of Tangent to Hypotenuse (distance from centre) is 32 : 40 = 4 : 5.

This strictly follows the 3-4-5 Pythagorean triplet.

⇒ Radius = 3 parts = 3 × 8 = 24 cm.

⇒ Diameter = 2 × 24 = 48 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of external point T from centre (OT) = 40 cm

Length of the tangent (PT) = 32 cm

**Formula Used:**

A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency.

Using Pythagoras theorem in right-angled ΔOPT:

OP² + PT² = OT²

•

**Calculations:**

⇒ OP² + 32² = 40²

⇒ OP² + 1024 = 1600

⇒ OP² = 1600 − 1024

⇒ OP² = 576

⇒ OP = √576 = 24 cm

⇒ Diameter = 2 × Radius = 2 × 24 = 48 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

Tangent Theorem

A tangent to a circle is always perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency, creating a 90° angle.

Tangents from an External Point

The lengths of the two tangents drawn from a single external point to a circle are strictly equal in length.

Secant-Tangent Theorem

If a tangent segment (PT) and a secant segment (PAB) are drawn to a circle from an exterior point, then PT² = PA × PB.

question: A and B are centres of two circles with radii 2 cm and 1 cm respectively, where AB = 5 cm. C is the centre of another circle of radius r cm, which touches each of the above two circles externally. Iftriangle ACB = 90circ, then the value of r is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If angle ACB = 90°, ΔACB forms a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse AB = 5 cm.

The standard Pythagorean triplet with hypotenuse 5 is (3, 4, 5), so the perpendicular legs must be 3 cm and 4 cm.

The distance between externally touching circles is the sum of their radii, giving AC = r + 2 and BC = r + 1.

By comparing the lengths, setting r = 2 cm directly gives AC = 4 cm and BC = 3 cm.

This perfectly satisfies the right-angled triangle condition without needing to solve quadratic equations.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of circle with centre A = 2 cm

Radius of circle with centre B = 1 cm

Distance between centres A and B (AB) = 5 cm

Circle with centre C touches both circles externally with radius r.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
•

**Formula Used:**

When two circles touch externally, distance between their centres = r₁ + r₂

Pythagoras Theorem: (Hypotenuse)² = (Base)² + (Perpendicular)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance AC = r + 2 cm

⇒ Distance BC = r + 1 cm

Since angle ACB = 90°, ΔACB is a right-angled triangle with AB as the hypotenuse.

⇒ AC² + BC² = AB²

⇒ (r + 2)² + (r + 1)² = 5²

⇒ r² + 4r + 4 + r² + 2r + 1 = 25

⇒ 2r² + 6r + 5 = 25

⇒ 2r² + 6r − 20 = 0

Dividing the entire equation by 2:

⇒ r² + 3r − 10 = 0

⇒ r² + 5r − 2r − 10 = 0

⇒ r(r + 5) − 2(r + 5) = 0

⇒ (r + 5)(r − 2) = 0

⇒ r = −5 or r = 2

Since the radius of a circle cannot be negative, r = 2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circles Touching Externally

When two circles touch each other externally, the distance between their centres is equal to the sum of their radii: d = r₁ + r₂.

Circles Touching Internally

When two circles touch each other internally, the distance between their centres is equal to the absolute difference of their radii: d = |r₁ − r₂|.

Pythagorean Triplets

A set of three positive integers that fit the rule a² + b² = c². Common triplets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13) and (8, 15, 17) help solve right-angled triangle problems quickly.
</p

Two circles, centred at P and Q intersect at two points C and D. AB is tangent to the two circles at A and B. If ∠ADB = 68°, then ∠ACB = ________.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two intersecting circles with a common tangent AB, and intersection points C and D:

The sum of the angles subtended by the common tangent at the intersection points is always 180°.

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠ADB = 180°

⇒ ∠ACB + 68° = 180°

⇒ ∠ACB = 112°

**∴ The correct answer is 112°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠ADB = 68°

**Formula Used:**

Alternate Segment Theorem: The angle between a tangent and a chord is equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the alternate segment.

Sum of interior angles of a triangle is 180°.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let AB be the common tangent touching the circles at A and B.

⇒ By the Alternate Segment Theorem for the first circle, the angle between tangent AB and chord AC is equal to the angle in the alternate segment.

⇒ ∠BAC = ∠ADC

⇒ Similarly, for the second circle, the angle between tangent AB and chord BC is equal to the angle in the alternate segment.

⇒ ∠ABC = ∠BDC

⇒ In ΔABC, the sum of all interior angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠BAC + ∠ABC = 180°

⇒ Substituting the corresponding alternate angles into the equation:

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠ADC + ∠BDC = 180°

⇒ We know from the figure that ∠ADC + ∠BDC = ∠ADB.

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠ADB = 180°

⇒ ∠ACB + 68° = 180°

⇒ ∠ACB = 180° − 68°

⇒ ∠ACB = 112°

**∴ The correct answer is 112°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Segment Theorem

The angle between a tangent and a chord through the point of contact is strictly equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the alternate segment.

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

Length of DCT = √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²), where d is the distance between the centres and r₁, r₂ are the radii.

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

Length of TCT = √(d² − (r₁ + r₂)²), applicable when circles are strictly disjoint.

Common Chord of Intersecting Circles

The line joining the centres of two intersecting circles acts as the perpendicular bisector of their common chord.

The half-lengths of the two chords are 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm and 18 ÷ 2 = 9 cm.

We observe that the distance between the parallel chords is exactly the sum of their half-lengths (12 + 9 = 21 cm).

This implies the perpendicular distances from the centre to the chords are 9 cm and 12 cm.

Using the Pythagorean theorem, the radius r = √(12² + 9²).

r = √(144 + 81) = √225 = 15 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Length of chord AB = 24 cm

⇒ Length of chord CD = 18 cm

⇒ Distance between the chords = 21 cm

**Formula and Concept Used:**

⇒ The perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

⇒ Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the radius of the circle be r.

⇒ Let O be the centre, and OM and ON be the perpendiculars drawn from O to the chords AB and CD respectively.

⇒ AM = AB ÷ 2 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm

⇒ CN = CD ÷ 2 = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 cm

⇒ Let OM = x, then ON = 21 − x (since the total distance is 21 cm).

⇒ In right-angled ΔOMA: r² = x² + 12² ... (Equation 1)

⇒ In right-angled ΔONC: r² = (21 − x)² + 9² ... (Equation 2)

⇒ Equating Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ x² + 144 = (21 − x)² + 81

⇒ x² + 144 = 441 + x² − 42x + 81

⇒ 144 = 522 − 42x

⇒ 42x = 522 − 144 = 378

⇒ x = 378 ÷ 42 = 9 cm

⇒ Substituting x = 9 in Equation 1:

⇒ r² = 9² + 12²

⇒ r² = 81 + 144 = 225

⇒ r = √225 = 15 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Bisector Theorem

The perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord always bisects the chord into two equal halves.

Distance Between Parallel Chords

If two parallel chords of lengths 2a and 2b are on the opposite sides of the centre, the distance between them is √(r² − a²) + √(r² − b²).

Pythagorean Triplets

A set of three positive integers a, b, and c that satisfy a² + b² = c². The numbers 9, 12, and 15 form a common Pythagorean triplet, representing the sides of a right-angled triangle.
</p

question: If we extend a chord infinitely on both sides, then the chord becomes a __________.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A chord is a finite line segment connecting two points on the circumference of a circle.

When any finite line segment is extended infinitely on both sides, it becomes a straight line.

A straight line that passes through and intersects a circle at exactly two distinct points is defined as a secant.

**∴ The correct answer is secant.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A chord of a circle extended infinitely on both sides.

**Definitions Used:**

⇒ **Chord:** A line segment whose endpoints lie on the circle.

⇒ **Secant:** A line that intersects a circle at two distinct points.

**Analysis:**

⇒ Let AB be a chord of a circle with center O.

⇒ The chord AB itself is a finite line segment entirely inside the boundaries of the circle.

⇒ When we extend the line segment AB infinitely on both sides, it loses its bounded endpoints and becomes a straight continuous line.

⇒ Because this straight line intersects the circle at exactly two points (A and B) and goes beyond them, it directly satisfies the geometrical definition of a secant.

**∴ The correct answer is secant.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent

A line that touches the circle at exactly one single point is called a tangent. The tangent is always perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

Diameter

The longest chord of a circle that passes through its geometric center is called a diameter. Its length is exactly twice the radius (d = 2 × r).

Secant vs Chord Difference

A chord is a finite line segment contained entirely inside the circle, while a secant is an infinitely extending line that crosses through the circle, containing the chord within it.
</p

Angle in a Semicircle

Let O be the center of the circle, then OA = OB = OC = radius (r).

Given BC = r, ΔOBC becomes an equilateral triangle with all sides equal to r.

Since ΔOBC is equilateral, ∠ABC = ∠OBC = 60° and the center angle ∠BOC = 60°.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the radius of the circle be r. Then, OA = OB = OC = r.

⇒ In ΔOBC, the radii OB = OC = r, and it is given that the chord BC = r.

⇒ Since all three sides are equal, ΔOBC is an equilateral triangle.

⇒ Therefore, the angle at the center ∠BOC = 60° and ∠OBC = 60°.

A line drawn from the center of a circle perpendicular to a chord always bisects the chord into two equal segments.

Area of Annulus (Ring)

The region bounded between two concentric circles is called an annulus. Its area is calculated by subtracting the inner circle area from the outer circle area: Area = π(R² − r²).

Concentric Circles

Circles that share the same center point but have different radii are known as concentric circles. Any line intersecting both circles forms segments that are symmetrical around the perpendicular from the center.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. For ΔTQP, the exterior angle at Q is ∠PQR.

By the Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle between the tangent TP and chord PQ equals the angle in the alternate segment: ∠PRQ = ∠TPQ = 55°.

In ΔPQR, ∠QPR = 180° − (∠PQR + ∠PRQ) = 180° − (82° + 55°) = 43°.

The central angle ∠ROQ is twice the angle subtended at the circumference by the same arc: ∠ROQ = 2 × ∠QPR = 2 × 43° = 86°.

**∴ The correct answer is 86°.**

question: From a point A, which is at a distance of 17 cm from the centre C of a circle with radius 8 cm, the pair of tangents AB and AD to the circle are drawn. The area of the quadrilateral ABCD is ____ cm².
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a circle, length of a tangent = √(distance from centre² − radius²).

Length of tangent AB = √(17² − 8²) = √(289 − 64) = √225 = 15 cm.

The quadrilateral ABCD consists of two congruent right-angled triangles (ΔABC and ΔADC).

Total Area = 2 × Area of ΔABC = 2 × (1/2 × Base × Height).

Area of Quadrilateral ABCD = 15 × 8 = 120 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 120 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
 
• A B C D 17 cm 8 cm 8 cm 15 cm 15 cm 

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (r) = BC = CD = 8 cm

Distance of external point A from centre C (AC) = 17 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of a right-angled triangle = (1/2) × base × height

**Calculations:**

⇒ In a circle, a tangent is always perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

⇒ Therefore, ∠ABC = 90° and ∠ADC = 90°

⇒ Using Pythagoras theorem in right-angled ΔABC:

⇒ AB² + BC² = AC²

⇒ AB² + 8² = 17²

⇒ AB² = 289 − 64 = 225

⇒ AB = 15 cm

⇒ Area of right-angled ΔABC = (1/2) × 15 × 8 = 60 cm²

⇒ Due to symmetry, the tangents drawn from an external point are equal in length, making ΔABC ≅ ΔADC.

⇒ Area of ΔADC = 60 cm²

⇒ Total Area of Quadrilateral ABCD = Area of ΔABC + Area of ΔADC

⇒ Total Area = 60 + 60 = 120 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 120 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Tangents

Tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length. Hence, the tangent segments AB and AD are completely identical.

Tangent-Radius Theorem

A tangent to a circle is fundamentally perpendicular to the radius drawn to the exact point of tangency, creating a perfect 90° angle.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of integers satisfying the condition a² + b² = c² speed up calculations immensely. Common triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and naturally (8, 15, 17).

question: The angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are in the ratio 1:2:3:4. What is the measure of the smallest angle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The sum of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral is exactly 180°.

The given ratio of angles is 1 : 2 : 3 : 4. Let the angles be x, 2x, 3x, and 4x.

Since the sum of opposite angle pairs must be equal, we must pair them as (x, 4x) and (2x, 3x) because x + 4x = 5x and 2x + 3x = 5x.

Equating the sum to 180°: 5x = 180° ⇒ x = 36°.

The smallest angle in the ratio is x, which is 36°.

**∴ The correct answer is 36°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are in the ratio of 1 : 2 : 3 : 4.

**Formula Used:**

The sum of the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is always 180°.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the four angles of the cyclic quadrilateral be x, 2x, 3x, and 4x.

⇒ In a valid cyclic quadrilateral, the pairs of opposite angles must sum to the same value (180°).

⇒ Grouping the angles to find equal sums: (x + 4x) = 5x and (2x + 3x) = 5x.

⇒ Therefore, the opposite angle pairs are (x, 4x) and (2x, 3x).

⇒ Summing either opposite pair gives: 5x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° ÷ 5 = 36°

⇒ The measures of the four angles are 36°, 72°, 108°, and 144°.

⇒ Smallest angle = x = 36°

**∴ The correct answer is 36°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cyclic Quadrilateral

A quadrilateral is called cyclic if all four of its vertices lie on the circumference of a circle. The sum of either pair of opposite angles is exactly 180°.

Exterior Angle Property

If any side of a cyclic quadrilateral is extended, the exterior angle formed is equal to the interior opposite angle.

Ptolemy's Theorem

For any cyclic quadrilateral with side lengths a, b, c, d and diagonals p, q, the product of the diagonals equals the sum of the products of opposite sides: p × q = (a × c) + (b × d).

Brahmagupta's Formula

The area of a cyclic quadrilateral is given by Area = √(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)(s − d), where s is the semi-perimeter calculated as s = (a + b + c + d) ÷ 2.
</p

A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency. By proving the two triangles formed by the tangents, radii, and the line connecting the external point to the center are congruent, we can establish that the tangent lengths are equal.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Consider △OAP and △OBP:

⇒ OA = OB (Radii of the same circle)

⇒ OP = OP (Common hypotenuse)

⇒ ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° (Tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact)

⇒ By RHS (Right angle - Hypotenuse - Side) congruence criterion, △OAP ≅ △OBP.

⇒ Therefore, PA = PB (Corresponding parts of congruent triangles)

⇒ Since PA = 12 cm, it follows that PB = 12 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

When two circles do not intersect, the length of their direct common tangent is given by √(d² − (R − r)²), where d is the distance between their centers and R, r are their radii.

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

The length of the transverse common tangent (which crosses the line segment joining the centers) is calculated using the formula √(d² − (R + r)²).

Tangent-Secant Theorem

If a tangent segment and a secant segment are drawn to a circle from an exterior point, the square of the length of the tangent is equal to the product of the external secant part and the entire secant length (PT² = PA × PB).

Number of Tangents Rule

From an external point, exactly two tangents can be drawn to a circle. From a point on the circle, exactly one tangent can be drawn, and from a point inside the circle, zero tangents can be drawn.
</p

For a Transverse Common Tangent, the distance (d), TCT length, and sum of radii (R + r) form a right-angled triangle.

Given TCT = 9 cm and d = 15 cm, this perfectly forms a 9-12-15 right triangle triplet.

Therefore, R + r = 12 cm.

Since R = 8 cm, r = 12 − 8 = 4 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.**

Angles subtended by the same arc (Arc AD) are always equal: ∠ABD = ∠ACD = 40°.

Angle formed in a semicircle by the diameter AB is a right angle, meaning ∠ADB = 90°.

In ΔABD, the sum of all interior angles must be 180°.

⇒ ∠BAD = 180° − (90° + 40°) = 50°.

**∴ The correct answer is 50°.**

⇒ AB is the diameter of the circle.

⇒ ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral.

⇒ ∠ACD = 40°.

**Formulas & Properties Used:**

⇒ Angles subtended by the same arc at the circumference are equal.

⇒ The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is 90°.

⇒ The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is always 180°.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Notice that both ∠ACD and ∠ABD are formed by joining the points A and D to the circumference.

⇒ Thus, they are in the same segment of the circle, making them equal.

⇒ ∠ABD = ∠ACD = 40°.

⇒ Since AB is the diameter passing through the center O, the angle it makes at the boundary is 90°.

⇒ Therefore, ∠ADB = 90°.

⇒ Now, in right-angled ΔABD, apply the angle sum property:

⇒ ∠BAD + ∠ABD + ∠ADB = 180°

⇒ ∠BAD + 40° + 90° = 180°

⇒ ∠BAD + 130° = 180°

⇒ ∠BAD = 180° − 130° = 50°.

**∴ The correct answer is 50°.**

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

A quadrilateral is called a cyclic quadrilateral if all four of its vertices lie on the circumference of a single circle. The sum of any pair of opposite angles is exactly 180° (e.g., ∠A + ∠C = 180° and ∠B + ∠D = 180°).

Angle in a Semicircle

A foundational circle theorem dictates that the angle subtended by the diameter at any point on the boundary of the circle is always a right angle (90°).

Angles in the Same Segment

When two or more angles are subtended by the exact same arc at any point on the remaining part of the circle, those angles are completely identical in measure.
</p

The length of a Direct Common Tangent (DCT) is defined by the relation DCT² = d² − (r₁ − r₂)².

We are given that the length of the tangent is equal to the distance between the centers, which means DCT = d.

For DCT² to be equal to d², the subtracted term (r₁ − r₂)² must be exactly zero.

⇒ r₁ − r₂ = 0 ⇒ r₁ = r₂

**∴ The correct answer is r₁ = r₂.**

Distance between their centers = d

Length of the Direct Common Tangent (L) = d

⇒ d = √[d² − (r₁ − r₂)²]

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

The length of a Transverse Common Tangent is given by TCT = √[d² − (r₁ + r₂)²]. This tangent completely crosses the line segment joining the centers of the two circles.

Number of Common Tangents

When two circles do not touch or intersect (d > r₁ + r₂), they have exactly 4 common tangents (2 direct and 2 transverse). If they touch externally (d = r₁ + r₂), there are exactly 3 common tangents.

Tangent Perpendicularity Theorem

A line drawn from the center of a circle to the point of tangency makes a perpendicular angle (90 degrees) with the tangent line at that exact point.

Angle subtended by a chord at the centre is always double the angle subtended at the major arc.

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°.

⇒ Let the centre of the circle be O and the radius be r.

⇒ Angle at the centre ∠AOB = 2 × ∠ACB

Direct formula for sector area (when angle is in radians):

⇒ θ = π/4 = 180° ÷ 4 = 45°

⇒ Area = (1 ÷ 8) × π × 64

By the central angle theorem, the angle subtended by an arc at the center is exactly double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

The major arc subtends an angle of 110° at the circumference (minor arc).

Central angle = 2 × Angle at circumference

Central angle = 2 × 110° = 220°

**∴ The correct answer is 220°.**

 220° 110° O P A B Major Arc AB Minor Arc AB 

**Given:**

Angle subtended by the major arc at the circumference = 110°.

**Formula Used:**

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the circle have center O and chord AB.

⇒ The chord divides the circle into a major arc and a minor arc.

⇒ Let P be a point on the minor arc. The angle subtended by the major arc at point P is ∠APB = 110°.

⇒ The central angle subtended by the major arc is the reflex angle ∠AOB.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

question: A line from the center of a circle bisects a chord. What is the angle between this line and the chord?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the standard circle theorem, a line drawn through the center of a circle to bisect a chord is always perpendicular to that chord.

Therefore, the angle formed between the bisecting line and the chord is exactly a right angle.

**∴ The correct answer is 90°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
• 
 
• 
• 
• 
• O A B M 

**Given:**

A circle with center O and chord AB.

A line OM drawn from the center bisects the chord AB, meaning AM = MB.

**Concept Used:**

Congruency of triangles using the SSS (Side-Side-Side) criterion.

**Calculations:**

⇒ In ΔOMA and ΔOMB:

⇒ OA = OB (Radii of the same circle)

⇒ AM = MB (Given that OM bisects the chord)

⇒ OM = OM (Common side)

⇒ By SSS congruence criterion, ΔOMA ≅ ΔOMB.

⇒ Therefore, their corresponding angles are equal: ∠OMA = ∠OMB.

⇒ Since AMB is a straight line, the sum of angles on the line is 180°.

⇒ ∠OMA + ∠OMB = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠OMA = 180°

⇒ ∠OMA = 90°

**∴ The correct answer is 90°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular from Center Theorem

The converse is also universally true: A perpendicular dropped from the center of a circle to a chord will always bisect the chord into two equal halves.

Equal Chords and Distance

Equal chords of a circle are always equidistant from the center. Conversely, chords that are equidistant from the center are equal in length.

Angle at the Center

The angle subtended by an arc at the center of a circle is double the angle subtended by it at any remaining part of the circle's circumference.

question: A tangent is drawn from a point 17 cm from the center of a circle of radius 8 cm. Find the length of the tangent.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The radius, tangent, and the distance from the center form a right-angled triangle.

In this triangle, the distance from the center is the hypotenuse.

We know the standard Pythagorean triplet **(8, 15, 17)**.

Since the radius is 8 cm and the hypotenuse is 17 cm, the tangent must be 15 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (OT) = 8 cm

Distance from the center to external point P (OP) = 17 cm

**Formula Used:**

In a circle, the tangent is always perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency.

Using Pythagoras theorem in right-angled ΔOTP: OP² = OT² + PT²

 
 
 O P T 17 cm 8 cm ? (Tangent) 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In right-angled ΔOTP, OP is the hypotenuse.

⇒ 17² = 8² + PT²

⇒ 289 = 64 + PT²

⇒ PT² = 289 − 64

⇒ PT² = 225

⇒ PT = √225 = 15 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent Perpendicularity Property

The radius of a circle drawn to the point of tangency is always perpendicular (90°) to the tangent line.

Equal Tangents Theorem

If two tangent segments are drawn to a single circle from an external point, then those segments are strictly equal in length.

Secant-Tangent Theorem

If a tangent segment (PT) and a secant segment (PAB) are drawn to a circle from an exterior point, then PT² = PA × PB.

Important Pythagorean Triplets

Memorizing common triplets speeds up geometry calculations: (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), (8, 15, 17), and (9, 40, 41).

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a circle, the radius, the perpendicular distance to the chord, and half the chord always form a right-angled triangle.

We can directly use the standard Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13).

Since the hypotenuse (radius) is 13 cm and one side is 5 cm, the other side (half the chord) must be 12 cm.

Length of the full chord = 2 × 12 cm = 24 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (OA) = 13 cm

Perpendicular distance from the center to the chord (OM) = 5 cm

**Formula Used:**

According to Pythagoras theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

The perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

 
• 
• 
• 
 O A B M 13 cm 5 cm x Chord AB = 2 × AM = 24 cm 

**Calculations:**

In right-angled triangle OMA:

⇒ OA² = OM² + AM²

⇒ 13² = 5² + AM²

⇒ 169 = 25 + AM²

⇒ AM² = 169 − 25

⇒ AM² = 144

⇒ AM = √144 = 12 cm

Since the perpendicular from the center bisects the chord, full chord AB = 2 × AM

⇒ Length of chord AB = 2 × 12 = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to any chord bisects the chord into two equal halves.

Memorizing integer sets that satisfy a² + b² = c² saves critical calculation time. Important triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25) along with their multiples.

Intersecting Chords Theorem

If two chords AB and CD intersect internally at point P, then the products of their segments are always equal: PA × PB = PC × PD.

Angle in a Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of a circle is exactly 90°.

solution:
**Given:**

In Δ PQR,

PQ = 15 cm, QR = 11 cm and RP = 13 cm.

A circle is inscribed in Δ PQR, such that it touches the sides PQ, QR and RP at points D, E, F, respectively.

**Concept Used:**

Tangents drawn from a point to the circle are equal in length.

**Calculation:**

A circle is inscribed in Δ PQR, such that it touches the sides PQ, QR and RP at points D, E, F, respectively.

⇒ PD = PF = x 

⇒ QD = QE = y

⇒ RE = RF = z

All are tangents,

⇒ PD + PF + QD + QE + RE + RF = PQ + QR + RP

⇒ x + x + y + y + z + z = 39

⇒ 2x + 2(y + z) = 39

Here,

y + z = QE + ER = RQ

And we have RQ = 11

⇒ 2x + 2(11) = 39

⇒ 2x + 22 = 39

⇒ 2x = 17

⇒ x = 8.5

⇒ PD = 8.5 cm

**∴ Option 4 is the correct answer.**

question: X, Y, and Z are three points on a plane with XY = 11 cm, YZ = 13 cm, and XZ = 24 cm. The number of circles that travel through points X, Y, and Z is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the sum of the two smaller distances: XY + YZ = 11 + 13 = 24 cm.

The largest distance is XZ = 24 cm.

Since XY + YZ = XZ, the three points X, Y, and Z lie on a straight line (they are collinear).

A circle can only pass through three non-collinear points.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Concept Used:**

For any three points to form a triangle (non-collinear), the sum of the distances between any two pairs of points must be strictly greater than the third distance.

A circle can uniquely pass through three non-collinear points, but zero circles can pass through three collinear points.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of two smaller distances = XY + YZ

⇒ Sum = 11 cm + 13 cm = 24 cm

⇒ The given largest distance XZ = 24 cm

⇒ Since XY + YZ = XZ, the point Y perfectly lies on the straight line segment connecting X and Z.

⇒ Therefore, points X, Y, and Z are collinear.

⇒ Because no circle can pass through three points lying on a single straight line, the number of such circles is zero.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Triangle Inequality Theorem

For any three points to form a valid triangle, the sum of the lengths of any two sides must be strictly greater than the length of the third side (a + b > c).

Circumcircle

A circumcircle is a unique circle that passes through all three non-collinear vertices of a triangle. The intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of the sides acts as its center.

Collinear Points

When three or more points lie entirely on the same straight line, they are known as collinear points. They cannot form a closed geometrical 2D figure like a circle or a triangle.

question: Point P is at an equal distance from the three vertices of a triangle with coordinates A(0, 0), B(4, 0), and C(0, 3). What are the coordinates of point P?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The given points A(0, 0), B(4, 0), and C(0, 3) lie on the axes, forming a right-angled triangle with the right angle at the origin A(0, 0).

A point equidistant from all three vertices of a triangle is known as its circumcenter.

For any right-angled triangle, the circumcenter always lies exactly at the midpoint of its hypotenuse.

The hypotenuse connects the points B(4, 0) and C(0, 3).

Coordinates of P = ((4 + 0) ÷ 2, (0 + 3) ÷ 2) = (2, 1.5).

**∴ The correct answer is (2, 1.5).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Vertices of the triangle are A(0, 0), B(4, 0), and C(0, 3).

Let the coordinates of point P be (x, y).

Point P is equidistant from all three vertices, meaning PA = PB = PC.

**Formula Used:**

Distance formula d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²)

 
• 
• 
 
 
• 
• 
• A(0, 0) B(4, 0) C(0, 3) P(2, 1.5) 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Equating PA² = PB²

⇒ (x − 0)² + (y − 0)² = (x − 4)² + (y − 0)²

⇒ x² + y² = x² − 8x + 16 + y²

⇒ 8x = 16

⇒ x = 2

⇒ Similarly, evaluating PA² = PC²

⇒ (x − 0)² + (y − 0)² = (x − 0)² + (y − 3)²

⇒ x² + y² = x² + y² − 6y + 9

⇒ 6y = 9

⇒ y = 1.5

⇒ The coordinates of point P are (2, 1.5).

**∴ The correct answer is (2, 1.5).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circumcenter of a Right-Angled Triangle

In any right-angled triangle, the circumcenter is precisely the midpoint of its hypotenuse. The length of the circumradius is equal to half the length of the hypotenuse.

Centroid of a Triangle

The centroid is the point of intersection of the three medians. For vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), and (x₃, y₃), the coordinates are derived as ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃) ÷ 3, (y₁ + y₂ + y₃) ÷ 3).

Circumcenter Position based on Triangle Type

The location of the circumcenter varies distinctively: it lies strictly inside an acute triangle, exactly on the midpoint of the hypotenuse for a right-angled triangle, and entirely outside an obtuse triangle.

question: Sides AB and DC of a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD are produced to meet at E and sides AD and BC are produced to meet at F. If ∠ADC = 78° and ∠BEC = 52°, then the measure of ∠AFB is:
solution:
**Given:**

∠ADC = 78° and ∠BEC = 52°

**Concept:**

The sum of a pair of opposite angles is 180° of a cyclic quadrilateral. 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5ecdc1e4af8b0eea06b16d09b5ef95bddb170d40b5eb76ab11785ff5b6ecda84.png] 

Now, In quadrilateral ABCD,

∠ADC + ∠ABC = 180° (Sum of opposite angles are 180°)

⇒ ∠ABC = 180° - 78° = 102° 

∠EBC = 180° - 102° = 78° [Linear Pair]

In ΔBEC,

∠BEC + ∠EBC + ∠BCE = 180° 

⇒ 52° + 78° + ∠BCE = 180° 

⇒ ∠BCE = 180° - 130° = 50°

⇒ ∠BCE = ∠DCF = 50° (Vertically opposite angle)

∠ADE + ∠FDC = 180° [Linear Pair]

⇒ ∠FDC = 180° - ∠ADE = 180° - 78° = 102°

In ΔDCF,

∠FDC + ∠DCF + ∠DFC = 180° 

102 + 50 + ∠DFC = 180° 

∠DFC = 180° - 152° = 28° 

∠DFC = ∠AFB = 28° 

**∴ The measure of ∠AFB is 28°.**

question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, the bisectors of ∠C and ∠D meet at point E. If ∠CED = 57° and ∠A = 47°, then the measure of ∠B is:
solution:
**Given:**

∠CED = 57° and ∠A = 47°

**Concept used:**

The sum of the all angles of a triangle = 180°

The sum of the all angles of a quadrilateral = 360°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30c0f85882aa49c6023fd21a7713b9da51260db1254e1dced67f52eace08da42.png] 

In ΔCED, ∠CDE + ∠DCE + ∠CED = 180°

⇒ ∠D/2 + ∠C/2 + 57° = 180°

⇒ ∠D/2 + ∠C/2 = 180° - 57° = 123°

⇒ (∠D + ∠C)/2 = 123°

⇒ ∠D + ∠C = 123° × 2 = 246°

Also, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ 47° + ∠B + 246° = 360° [∵ ∠D + ∠C = 246°]

⇒ ∠B = 360° - 246° - 47° = 67°

**∴ The measure of ∠B is 67°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** ∠CED = 57° and ∠A = 47°

The bisectors of *∠C* and *∠D *meet at point E

∠A + ∠B = 2 ∠CED

⇒ 47° + ∠B = 2 × 57°

⇒ ∠B = 114° - 47° = 67°

∴ The measure of ∠B is 67°

question: In a rhombus ABCD, O is any interior point such that OA = OC. What is five-ninths of the degree measure of ∠DOB?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a rhombus, diagonals act as perpendicular bisectors for each other.

Any point equidistant from vertices A and C (OA = OC) must lie on the perpendicular bisector of AC.

Hence, the interior point O must exclusively lie on the diagonal segment BD.

This makes D, O, and B collinear, forming a straight angle ∠DOB = 180º.

Required value = ⁵/₉ × 180º = 100º.

**∴ The correct answer is 100º.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ABCD is a rhombus.

O is an interior point such that OA = OC.

**Formula Used:**

The locus of all points equidistant from two points A and C is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment AC.

 
 

 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
• 
 
•

 C
 B
 D
 O
 
 
 

 
 
 
• 
 
• 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In rhombus ABCD, the diagonal BD functions strictly as the perpendicular bisector of the diagonal AC.

⇒ Because OA = OC, the interior point O is geometrically bounded to lie on this specific perpendicular bisector.

⇒ Consequently, O must lie on the interior line segment connecting points B and D.

⇒ With O positioned directly between B and D, the points D, O, and B become entirely collinear.

⇒ A collinear line visually forms a completely straight angle, meaning ∠DOB = 180º.

⇒ Required measure = ⁵/₉ × ∠DOB

⇒ Required measure = ⁵/₉ × 180º = 100º

**∴ The correct answer is 100º.**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

A rhombus is a type of quadrilateral where all four sides possess an equal length. Its unique diagonal property dictates that diagonals perpendicularly bisect each other at a 90º intersection while also actively bisecting opposite interior angles.

Locus of Equidistant Points

Any generic point mapping an identical and equal distance dynamically relative to two fixed stationary points A and B will fundamentally form an invisible tracing line representing their shared perpendicular bisector.

Straight Angle

Whenever three sequential points are geometrically aligned collinear on a straight plane path, the resulting primary inner vertex translates dynamically into a strict unbent straight angle measuring precisely 180º.
</p

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The locus of a point equidistant from two vertices (P and R) is their perpendicular bisector.

In a rhombus, the diagonal SQ is the perpendicular bisector of the diagonal PR.

Since OP = OR, the point O must lie exactly on the diagonal SQ.

Because O is an interior point, S, O, and Q lie on the same straight line.

A straight line always forms an angle of 180°.

**∴ The correct answer is 180°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

PQRS is a rhombus.

O is an interior point such that OP = OR.

**Formula / Concept Used:**

The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at 90°.

The set of all points equidistant from two given points forms the perpendicular bisector of the segment connecting them.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the diagonals PR and SQ intersect at point M.

⇒ In rhombus PQRS, SQ ⊥ PR and PM = MR.

⇒ This implies that the diagonal SQ acts as the perpendicular bisector of the diagonal PR.

⇒ We are given that OP = OR, which means O is perfectly equidistant from the endpoints P and R.

⇒ By the locus theorem, any point equidistant from P and R must lie exactly on the perpendicular bisector of PR.

⇒ Therefore, the point O must lie completely on the line segment SQ.

⇒ Since O is placed strictly inside the rhombus on the diagonal SQ, the points S, O, and Q are collinear.

⇒ A collinear arrangement forms a straight angle.

⇒ ∠SOQ = 180°

**∴ The correct answer is 180°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

All four sides are equal in length. The diagonals bisect each other at right angles (90°) and also perfectly bisect the opposite interior angles.

Locus of Equidistant Point

The locus of a point that is completely equidistant from two given points A and B is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment AB.

Collinear Points

Three or more points that lie directly on the same straight line are termed collinear points. The angle formed by three collinear points with the middle point acting as the vertex is exactly 180°.
</p

question: In a kite ABCD, the longer diagonal BD is drawn. If ∠ABD = 54° and ∠ADB = 50°, then what is the measure (in degrees) of the ∠DCB ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a kite, if a diagonal splits unequal adjacent angles (∠ABD ≠ ∠ADB), it must be the axis of symmetry.

This means the diagonal BD divides the kite into two identical triangles, making ∠C = ∠A.

In ΔABD, the sum of all angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠A = 180° − (54° + 50°) = 76°

⇒ ∠C = 76°

**∴ The correct answer is 76°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ABCD is a kite.

∠ABD = 54°

∠ADB = 50°

**Method Used:**

A kite has two pairs of equal adjacent sides, and its main diagonal divides it into two congruent triangles.

The sum of all interior angles in any triangle is always 180°.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5df2020eaca75367f4ac4cbf7c9fae51ee9639caa0161506738769cd0f5eee5c.png] 

⇒ For the given kite ABCD, if AB were equal to AD, ΔABD would be an isosceles triangle, making ∠ABD = ∠ADB.

⇒ However, given ∠ABD (54°) ≠ ∠ADB (50°), we conclude that AB ≠ AD.

⇒ Therefore, the adjacent equal sides must be AB = BC and AD = CD.

⇒ In this configuration, the diagonal BD acts as the axis of symmetry.

⇒ Because BD is the axis of symmetry, it divides the kite into two congruent triangles: ΔABD ≅ ΔCBD.

⇒ In ΔABD, the sum of internal angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠DAB + ∠ABD + ∠ADB = 180°

⇒ ∠DAB + 54° + 50° = 180°

⇒ ∠DAB + 104° = 180°

⇒ ∠DAB = 180° − 104° = 76°

⇒ Due to the exact congruence of ΔABD and ΔCBD, the corresponding angles are perfectly equal, meaning ∠DCB = ∠DAB.

⇒ ∠DCB = 76°

**∴ The correct answer is 76°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Kite

A kite is a quadrilateral with two distinct pairs of equal-length sides that are adjacent to each other. The opposite angles where the unequal sides meet are always equal.

Diagonals of a Kite

The diagonals of a kite are always perpendicular to each other, intersecting at exactly 90°. The main diagonal (axis of symmetry) acts as the perpendicular bisector of the other diagonal.

Axis of Symmetry

The diagonal connecting the common vertices of the equal sides acts as the axis of symmetry. It bisects the angles at its endpoints and cleanly divides the kite into two identical congruent triangles.

question: If two straight lines are coinciding with each other, then the number of points of intersection is/are:

options.text: finite number of point of intersection

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Coinciding lines are two straight lines that lie perfectly on top of each other.

Since a single line is made up of a continuous, infinite series of points, two overlapping lines share every single point.

Thus, they intersect at every point along their entire length.

**∴ The correct answer is infinitely many points of intersection.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two straight lines are coinciding with each other.

**Concept Used:**

If two linear equations L₁: a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and L₂: a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 represent coinciding lines, their coefficients are strictly proportional: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Intersecting
 (1 point)

 
 
• 
 
• 
 Parallel
 (0 points)

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
 Coinciding
 (Infinite points)

**Calculations:**

⇒ When the equations are proportional, they mathematically represent the exact same straight line.

⇒ A straight line contains an infinitely large set of coordinate points (x, y).

⇒ Because the lines perfectly overlap, every point present on the first line also acts as a point on the second line.

⇒ Therefore, the number of shared (intersecting) points between them is strictly infinite.

**∴ The correct answer is infinitely many points of intersection.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Intersecting Lines

When two lines have completely different slopes (a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂), they will intersect at exactly one unique point, resulting in a single solution.

Parallel Lines

When two lines have the same slope but different intercepts (a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂), they never meet each other at any point, resulting in 0 solutions.

Coincident Lines

When two lines share both the same slope and same intercept (a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂), they overlap perfectly, resulting in infinitely many solutions.
</p

question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, AB = BC, AD = DC. ∠ABD = 68º, ∠ADB = (2y-7)º, ∠BDC = 33º, ∠DBC = (3x+2)º. Then the value of 2x+3y is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A quadrilateral with two distinct pairs of equal adjacent sides is a kite.

The main diagonal of a kite bisects the opposite interior angles.

⇒ ∠ABD = ∠DBC ⇒ 68 = 3x + 2 ⇒ x = 22

⇒ ∠ADB = ∠BDC ⇒ 2y − 7 = 33 ⇒ y = 20

⇒ 2x + 3y = 2 × 22 + 3 × 20 = 44 + 60 = 104

**∴ The correct answer is 104.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
• 
 
 
 
 B D A C 68° (3x+2)° (2y−7)° 33° 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 

**Given:**

In quadrilateral ABCD:

⇒ AB = BC

⇒ AD = DC

⇒ ∠ABD = 68º

⇒ ∠ADB = (2y−7)º

⇒ ∠BDC = 33º

⇒ ∠DBC = (3x+2)º

**Method:**

Since the adjacent sides are equal, ABCD is a kite. The diagonal BD divides the kite into two congruent triangles, ΔABD and ΔCBD.

In ΔABD and ΔCBD:

⇒ AB = CB (Given)

⇒ AD = CD (Given)

⇒ BD = BD (Common Side)

⇒ By SSS congruence criterion, ΔABD ≅ ΔCBD.

Corresponding angles of congruent triangles are equal (CPCT):

⇒ ∠ABD = ∠CBD

⇒ 68 = 3x + 2

⇒ 3x = 66 ⇒ x = 22

Also,

⇒ ∠ADB = ∠CDB

⇒ 2y − 7 = 33

⇒ 2y = 40 ⇒ y = 20

Now, calculate the value of 2x + 3y:

⇒ 2x + 3y = 2 × 22 + 3 × 20

⇒ 44 + 60 = 104

**∴ The correct answer is 104.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Kite

A kite is a quadrilateral with two distinct pairs of equal-length sides that are adjacent to each other. Its diagonals intersect at right angles (90º).

Congruence in Kite

The main diagonal (connecting the vertices where the equal sides meet) divides the kite into two congruent triangles via the SSS rule.

Area of a Kite

The area of a kite is half the product of the lengths of its diagonals: Area = ½ × d₁ × d₂.

question: In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, if angle A is 100°, what is the measure of angle C?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The sum of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral is always 180°.

Angle A and Angle C are opposite angles in the cyclic quadrilateral ABCD.

∠C = 180° − ∠A

∠C = 180° − 100° = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 100°

 ∠A + ∠C = 180°

**Given:**

∠A = 100°

ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral.

**Formula Used:**

In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of a pair of opposite interior angles is equal to 180°.

**Calculation:**

⇒ ∠A + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 100° + ∠C = 180°

⇒ ∠C = 180° − 100°

⇒ ∠C = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cyclic Quadrilateral

A quadrilateral is called cyclic if all its four vertices lie on the circumference of a single circle. The primary property of a cyclic quadrilateral is that the sum of its opposite interior angles is always 180°.

Exterior Angle Property

If any one side of a cyclic quadrilateral is extended outwardly, the exterior angle formed is strictly equal to the interior opposite angle.

Ptolemy's Theorem

For a cyclic quadrilateral, the product of the lengths of the diagonals is equal to the sum of the products of the lengths of its opposite sides (AC × BD = AB × CD + AD × BC).
</p

question: If the perimeter of a regular octagon is 80 cm, what is the side length?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A regular octagon has 8 equal sides.

Side length = Total Perimeter ÷ Number of sides

Side length = 80 ÷ 8 = 10 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 

 Side = a
 Regular Octagon
 Perimeter = 8a

**Given:**

Perimeter of the regular octagon = 80 cm

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a regular polygon = Number of sides × Length of one side

For a regular octagon, Perimeter = 8 × a (where a is the side length)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 8 × a = 80

⇒ a = 80 ÷ 8

⇒ a = 10 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon is given by (n − 2) × 180°. For an octagon, it is (8 − 2) × 180° = 1080°.

Interior and Exterior Angle

Each interior angle of a regular octagon is 1080° ÷ 8 = 135°. Each exterior angle is 360° ÷ 8 = 45°.

Number of Diagonals

The total number of diagonals in an n-sided polygon is n(n − 3) ÷ 2. For an octagon, it is 8(8 − 3) ÷ 2 = 20 diagonals.

Area of Regular Octagon

The area of a regular octagon with side a is 2a²(1 + √2).
</p

question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, AB is parallel to CD, and AC is a diagonal. If AB=CD, which of the following is true?

options.text: The triangles are similar, but not necessarily congruen

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In quadrilateral ABCD, we are given AB is parallel to CD and AB = CD.

Since the alternate interior angles formed by transversal AC are equal, ∠BAC = ∠DCA.

For ΔABC and ΔCDA, we evaluate the known equal parts:

⇒ AB = CD (Given) | ∠BAC = ∠DCA (Alternate angles) | AC = CA (Common side)

Since two sides and their included angle are equal, the triangles are congruent by the Side-Angle-Side rule.

**∴ The correct answer is ΔABC ≅ ΔCDA by SAS.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal AC.

⇒ AB is parallel to CD.

⇒ AB = CD.

**Concept Used:**

⇒ If two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, their alternate interior angles are equal.

⇒ SAS Congruence Rule: If two sides and the included angle of one triangle are equal to the corresponding parts of another triangle, they are congruent.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Consider ΔABC and ΔCDA.

⇒ Since AB is parallel to CD and AC acts as the transversal, the alternate interior angles are exactly equal.

⇒ ∠BAC = ∠DCA

⇒ We are already given that side AB = side CD.

⇒ The diagonal AC is a common side to both triangles, so AC = CA.

⇒ We now have two sides and the included angle equal for both triangles.

Two triangles are congruent if two sides and the included angle of one are identically equal to the corresponding parts of the other.

SSS (Side-Side-Side) Congruence

Two triangles are completely congruent if all three sides of one triangle are equal to the corresponding three sides of the other.

ASA (Angle-Side-Angle) Congruence

If two angles and the included side of one triangle are equal to the corresponding parts of another triangle, they are completely congruent.

A fundamental property of any convex polygon is that a full trip around its perimeter involves exactly one complete rotation.

Therefore, the total sum of all exterior angles, taking one at each vertex, is equivalent to one full circle.

One complete circle rotation is always equal to 360°.

**∴ The correct answer is 360°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Sum of exterior angles = n × 180° − (n − 2) × 180°

question: A parallelogram is a quadrilateral in which:

options.text: Only one pair of opposite sides is parallel.
Opposite sides are parallel and of equal length.

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By basic geometric definitions, the term parallelogram explicitly means a quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel opposite sides.

A direct geometric consequence of opposite sides being parallel is that they must also be equal in length.

Statements defining only one parallel pair describe a trapezium, while perpendicular diagonals describe a rhombus.

**∴ The correct answer is Opposite sides are parallel and of equal length.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Four statements describing the properties of quadrilaterals.

 

 
 A
 B
 C
 D
 
 

 

 
 

 

 

 

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
• 
 
• 

**Analysis of each option:**

⇒ **Statement 1:** Only one pair of opposite sides is parallel. This defines a **Trapezium**.

⇒ **Statement 2:** All four interior angles are 90°. This defines a **Rectangle** or a Square.

⇒ **Statement 3:** Opposite sides are parallel and of equal length. This is the exact definition and core property of a **Parallelogram**.

⇒ **Statement 4:** The diagonals are perpendicular. This is a special property found in a **Rhombus** or a Square, but not in all standard parallelograms.

⇒ Therefore, the only universally true statement for any general parallelogram is that its opposite sides are parallel and equal.

**∴ The correct answer is Opposite sides are parallel and of equal length.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rhombus

A parallelogram in which all four sides are equal. The diagonals of a rhombus always bisect each other at exactly 90°.

Rectangle

A parallelogram where all four interior angles are exactly 90°. Its diagonals are equal in length and bisect each other.

Trapezium

A quadrilateral with strictly only one pair of parallel opposite sides. The parallel sides are called bases.

Square

A regular quadrilateral satisfying properties of both a rectangle and a rhombus. All sides are equal, all angles are 90°, and diagonals intersect at 90°.
</p

question: A large regular polygon is made by combining 6 regular hexagons around a common center. What is the ratio of area of the combined shape to one hexagon?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the area of a single regular hexagon be 1 unit.

Since the combined shape is formed by exactly 6 such regular hexagons without overlapping, its total area is simply the sum of all their individual areas.

Total area of the combined shape = 6 × 1 = 6 units.

Ratio of the combined area to the area of one hexagon = 6 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 6:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of regular hexagons combined together = 6

**Concept Used:**

When multiple non-overlapping two-dimensional figures are joined together, the total area of the resulting figure is equal to the sum of the individual areas (Conservation of Area principle).

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
 

 
 Center

 

 Area = A
 
 Combined Shape (Area = 6A)
 One Hexagon

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the area of one regular hexagon = A

⇒ The large polygon is constructed by placing 6 regular hexagons around a common center in a tiled format.

⇒ Total Area of the new shape = Area of Hexagon 1 + Area of Hexagon 2 + ... + Area of Hexagon 6

⇒ Total Area = 6 × A = 6A

⇒ Required Ratio = (Total Area of combined shape) ÷ (Area of one hexagon)

⇒ Required Ratio = 6A / A = 6:1

**∴ The correct answer is 6:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Regular Hexagon

The area of a regular hexagon with side length a is given by the formula: Area = (3√3 ÷ 2) × a².

Conservation of Area

In two-dimensional geometry, if a planar figure is divided into several non-overlapping pieces, the total area of the whole figure exactly equals the sum of the areas of those distinct pieces.

Tessellation of Hexagons

Regular hexagons are one of the only three regular polygons (along with equilateral triangles and squares) that can perfectly tile a flat plane without leaving gaps or creating overlaps.
</p

where 'a' is the side length of the regular hexagon.

Every interior angle of a regular hexagon is 120°, while every exterior angle is 60°.

question: A regular hexagon is inscribed inside a circle of radius 14 cm. Find the area of the hexagon.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A regular hexagon inscribed in a circle is made up of 6 equilateral triangles with sides equal to the circle's radius.

Side of the hexagon (a) = Radius (r) = 14 cm

Area = 6 × (√3 ÷ 4) × r²

Area = 6 × (√3 ÷ 4) × 196 = 294√3

Area ≈ 294 × 1.732 ≈ 509.21 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 509.21 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• O r = 14 cm a = 14 cm Regular Hexagon Inside A Circle 

**Given:**

Radius of the circumscribed circle (r) = 14 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of a regular hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × a²

Where 'a' is the side length of the regular hexagon.

**Calculations:**

⇒ For a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle, the side length 'a' is equal to the radius 'r' of the circle.

⇒ Side length (a) = 14 cm

⇒ Area = (3√3 ÷ 2) × (14)²

⇒ Area = (3√3 ÷ 2) × 196

⇒ Area = 3 × 98 × √3

⇒ Area = 294√3 cm²

⇒ Substituting the value of √3 ≈ 1.732:

⇒ Area ≈ 294 × 1.732

⇒ Area ≈ 509.208 cm²

⇒ Rounding off to two decimal places gives 509.21 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 509.21 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circumradius of a Regular Hexagon

When a regular hexagon is inscribed inside a circle, the radius of the circle (circumradius) is exactly equal to the side length of the hexagon: R = a.

Inradius of a Regular Hexagon

When a circle is inscribed inside a regular hexagon, the radius of the circle (inradius) is equal to the altitude of the equilateral triangles forming the hexagon: r = (√3 ÷ 2) × a.

Composition of a Hexagon

A regular hexagon is formed by 6 identical equilateral triangles. Thus, its total area is exactly 6 times the area of one equilateral triangle: Area = 6 × [(√3 ÷ 4) × a²].

Inscribed vs Circumscribed Areas

For any given circle, the area of the regular hexagon circumscribed around it is exactly 4/3 times the area of the regular hexagon inscribed within it.

question: The sum of all interior angles of a 20-sided polygon is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any polygon with n sides, the sum of its interior angles is simply calculated as (n − 2) × 180°.

Here, the polygon has 20 sides, so n = 20.

⇒ Sum = (20 − 2) × 180° = 18 × 180° = 3240°.

**∴ The correct answer is 3240°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of sides of the polygon, n = 20

**Formula Used:**

Sum of all interior angles of an n-sided polygon = (n − 2) × 180°

 
 
• 
• 
• Generic Polygon (Triangles = n − 2) Sum of Interior Angles = (n − 2) × 180° For 20-sided: n = 20 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of interior angles = (20 − 2) × 180°

⇒ Sum of interior angles = 18 × 180°

⇒ Sum of interior angles = 3240°

**∴ The correct answer is 3240°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of all exterior angles of any convex polygon is always exactly 360°, regardless of how many sides the polygon has.

Each Interior Angle

If the polygon is regular (all sides and angles are equal), each interior angle can be found by dividing the total sum by n: [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n.

Number of Diagonals

The total number of diagonals that can be drawn in an n-sided polygon is given by the direct formula: n × (n − 3) ÷ 2.

question: The ratio of areas of two regular polygons with same number of sides is 4:9. What is the ratio of their side lengths?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any two regular polygons with the same number of sides, they are geometrically similar.

The ratio of their corresponding sides is exactly the square root of the ratio of their areas.

Side ratio = √(Area ratio)

⇒ Side ratio = √(4 / 9) = 2 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is 2:3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of areas of two regular polygons = 4 : 9

Both polygons have an equal number of sides, say 'n'.

**Formula Used:**

Area of a regular polygon with 'n' sides = (n × a²) ÷ [4 × tan(180°/n)], where 'a' is the side length.

 
 Area = 4 
• Side 1 
 Area = 9 
• Side 2 
• 
 Ratio 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the sides of the two polygons be a₁ and a₂.

⇒ Let their areas be A₁ and A₂ respectively.

⇒ Since the number of sides 'n' is equal, the constant terms n and [4 × tan(180°/n)] will cancel out when calculating the ratio.

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = a₁² / a₂²

⇒ 4 / 9 = (a₁ / a₂)²

⇒ a₁ / a₂ = √(4 / 9)

⇒ a₁ / a₂ = 2 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is 2:3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Similarity of Regular Polygons

All regular polygons with the same number of sides are geometrically similar. The ratio of their areas is strictly the square of the ratio of their corresponding side lengths.

Perimeter Ratio

For any two similar figures, the ratio of their perimeters is precisely equal to the linear scale factor, which is the direct ratio of their corresponding side lengths.

Volume of Similar 3D Solids

If two 3D solids are similar, the ratio of their volumes is identical to the cube of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions (V₁ / V₂ = (a₁ / a₂)³).

question: What is the ratio of the interior angle of a regular hexagon to the interior angle of a regular 12-sided polygon (dodecagon)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Each interior angle of a regular polygon is given by 180° − (360° ÷ n), where n is the number of sides.

Interior angle of a regular hexagon (n = 6) = 180° − 60° = 120°.

Interior angle of a regular 12-sided polygon (n = 12) = 180° − 30° = 150°.

Required Ratio = 120° : 150° = 4 : 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of sides of regular hexagon (n₁) = 6

Number of sides of regular dodecagon (n₂) = 12

**Formula Used:**

Interior angle of a regular n-sided polygon = [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n

 
 Hexagon 120° 
 Dodecagon 150° Interior Angle Ratio = 120° : 150° = 4 : 5 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interior angle of a regular hexagon = [(6 − 2) × 180°] ÷ 6

⇒ Interior angle of a regular hexagon = [4 × 180°] ÷ 6 = 120°

⇒ Interior angle of a regular 12-sided polygon = [(12 − 2) × 180°] ÷ 12

⇒ Interior angle of a regular 12-sided polygon = [10 × 180°] ÷ 12 = 150°

⇒ Ratio of their interior angles = 120° : 150°

⇒ Ratio = 12 : 15 = 4 : 5

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of an n-sided polygon is given by (n − 2) × 180°.

Exterior Angle of Regular Polygon

Each exterior angle of a regular n-sided polygon is given by 360° ÷ n. The sum of all exterior angles is always 360°.

Number of Diagonals

The total number of diagonals in an n-sided polygon can be calculated using the formula [n × (n − 3)] ÷ 2.

question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, angles A,B,C are in the ratio 1:2:3. If angle D=120°, what is angle A?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The sum of all 4 interior angles of a quadrilateral is 360°.

Sum of the remaining angles A, B, and C = 360° − 120° = 240°.

The angles A, B, and C are divided in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 (Total = 6 parts).

Angle A corresponds to 1 part, which is 40°.

**∴ The correct answer is 40°.**

question: A regular hexagonal nut has outer side 6 cm and inner hollow side 3 cm. What is the material approximate area in the cross-section?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a hollow regular hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × (Outer Side² − Inner Side²)

⇒ Area = (3 × 1.732 ÷ 2) × (6² − 3²)

⇒ Area = 2.598 × (36 − 9)

⇒ Area = 2.598 × 27 = 70.146 ≈ 70 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 70 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Outer side of the hexagonal nut (R) = 6 cm

Inner hollow side of the hexagonal nut (r) = 3 cm

 
 
 
• 
• 
• 6 cm 
• 
• 
• 3 cm Cross-section of Hexagonal Nut 

**Formula Used:**

Area of a regular hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × a²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of the outer regular hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × 6²

⇒ Area of outer hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × 36 = 54√3 cm²

⇒ Area of the inner hollow regular hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × 3²

⇒ Area of inner hexagon = (3√3 ÷ 2) × 9 = 13.5√3 cm²

⇒ Cross-sectional area of the material = Area of outer hexagon − Area of inner hexagon

⇒ Material Area = 54√3 − 13.5√3 = 40.5√3 cm²

⇒ Taking √3 ≈ 1.732, Area = 40.5 × 1.732 = 70.146 cm²

⇒ Rounding to the nearest whole number, Area ≈ 70 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 70 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Regular Hexagon

A regular hexagon can be completely divided into 6 equilateral triangles. The total area is exactly 6 × (√3 ÷ 4) × a² = (3√3 ÷ 2) × a², where 'a' is the length of its side.

Inradius of a Regular Hexagon

The radius of the inscribed circle (also called the apothem) is the perpendicular distance from the geometric center to any flat side, given by r = (√3 ÷ 2) × a.

Circumradius of a Regular Hexagon

The radius of the circumscribed circle passing through all six outer vertices is exactly equal to the side length of the regular hexagon, therefore R = a.

question: In a triangle ABC, D and E are points on BC such that AD = AE and ∠BAD = ∠CAE. If AB = (2p + 3), BD = 2p, AC = (3q - 1) and CE = q, then find the value of (p + q).
solution:
**Given:**

D = AE and ∠BAD = ∠CAE

AB = (2p + 3), BD = 2p, AC = (3q - 1) and CE = q

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b7f8cfe8c179f9fa4e0e37384e635f722930c33db3533e38204d48c4276aab5b.png] 

In ΔABD and ΔAEC,

AD = AE [Given]

∠ADB = ∠AEC [Exterior angles of ΔADE, where ∠ADE = ∠AED]

∠BAD = ∠CAE [Given]

So, ΔADB ∼ ΔAEC [A - S - A rule]

Then, 

⇒ AB/AC = BD/CE = AD/AE

⇒ (2p + 3)/(3q - 1) = 2p/q = 1 [∵ AD = AE]

By taking 2p/q = 1 

⇒ 2p = q .....(1)

By taking (2p + 3)/(3q - 1) = 1 

⇒ 2p + 3 = 3q - 1

⇒ 3q - 2p = 3 + 1

⇒ 3q - q = 4 [∵ 2p = q]

⇒ 2q = 4

⇒ q = 4/2 = 2

Put q = 2 in equation (1),

2p = 2

⇒ p = 2/2 = 1

Then, (p + q) = 1 + 2 = 3

**∴ The value of (p + q) is 3**

An angle bisector of an angle of a triangle divides the opposite side into two segments that are proportional to the other two sides of the triangle.
