question: In triangle ABC, the length of side BC is 2 cm less than twice the length of side AB. The length of side AC exceeds the length of side AB by 10 cm. The perimeter of the triangle is 40 cm. Determine the length (in cm) of the smallest side of the triangle.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the length of the side AB be x cm.

From the given problem, BC = 2x − 2 and AC = x + 10.

Perimeter = AB + BC + AC ⇒ x + 2x − 2 + x + 10 = 40

⇒ 4x + 8 = 40 ⇒ 4x = 32 ⇒ x = 8 cm.

The sides of the triangle are 8 cm, 14 cm, and 18 cm. The smallest side is clearly 8 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of side BC is 2 cm less than twice the length of side AB.

Length of side AC is 10 cm more than side AB.

Perimeter of triangle = 40 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4582980ffd39d958b96cee6a328efa736c73b57be1ef16fa61c1344ddbee948a.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a triangle = Sum of all its three sides (AB + BC + AC)

**Calculations:**

Let the length of side AB be x cm.

⇒ BC = (2x − 2) cm

⇒ AC = (x + 10) cm

⇒ Perimeter = AB + BC + AC

⇒ x + (2x − 2) + (x + 10) = 40

⇒ 4x + 8 = 40

⇒ 4x = 32

⇒ x = 32 ÷ 4

⇒ x = 8 cm

Now, substitute the value of x to find the lengths of the remaining sides:

⇒ AB = 8 cm

⇒ BC = 2 × (8) − 2 = 16 − 2 = 14 cm

⇒ AC = 8 + 10 = 18 cm

Comparing all three sides (8 cm, 14 cm, and 18 cm), the length of the smallest side is AB which equals 8 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Triangle Inequality Theorem

For any valid triangle, the sum of the lengths of any two sides must always be strictly greater than the length of the remaining third side (a + b > c).

Types of Triangles by Sides

Triangles are classified by their sides as Scalene (all 3 sides unequal), Isosceles (any 2 sides equal), and Equilateral (all 3 sides equal).

Perimeter and Semi-perimeter

The perimeter is simply the total outer boundary sum (a + b + c), while the semi-perimeter (s) used in finding area via Heron's formula is (a + b + c) ÷ 2.
</p

question: One-quarter of a circular pizza of radius 21 cm was removed from the whole pizza. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the remaining pizza? (Use π = (22)/(7))
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When 1/4 of a circular pizza is removed, the remaining shape consists of 3/4 of the original circumference plus two straight edges equal to the radius.

Perimeter = (3/4) × 2πr + 2r

Perimeter = (3/4) × 2 × (22/7) × 21 + (2 × 21)

Perimeter = 99 + 42 = 141 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 141 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b438551a0cf2fa7575c9c2e320edae4bef12707c96d94c48df3c58a1dee4f756.png] 

**Given:**

Radius of the circular pizza (r) = 21 cm

Part removed = 1/4 of the pizza

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of remaining shape = Length of remaining arc + 2 × Radius

Length of arc = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

**Calculations:**

⇒ Angle of the remaining pizza (θ) = 360° − (1/4 × 360°) = 270°

⇒ Length of remaining arc = (270° ÷ 360°) × 2 × (22/7) × 21

⇒ Length of remaining arc = (3/4) × 2 × 22 × 3

⇒ Length of remaining arc = (3/4) × 132 = 99 cm

⇒ Total straight edges = 2 × Radius = 2 × 21 = 42 cm

⇒ Perimeter of remaining pizza = 99 + 42 = 141 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 141 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Semicircle

A semicircle's perimeter includes half the circumference and the full straight diameter: P = πr + 2r = r(π + 2).

Length of an Arc

The length of an arc is proportional to its central angle θ: Arc Length = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector with central angle θ is a fraction of the total area: Area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr².
</p

question: A prism with a parallelogram base has base area 80 cm² and height 12 cm. If its lateral surface area is 384 cm², what is the perimeter of the base?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any right prism, the direct relation is: Lateral Surface Area = Base Perimeter × Height.

The given Base Area (80 cm²) is extraneous data deliberately provided to cause confusion.

Base Perimeter = 384 ÷ 12

Base Perimeter = 32 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 32 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base Area = 80 cm²

Height (h) = 12 cm

Lateral Surface Area = 384 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Lateral Surface Area of a right prism = Perimeter of Base × Height

 
• 
• 
• 
 
 
 
• 
• 
• h = 12 cm Base Area = 80 cm² Lateral Surface Area = 384 cm² 

**Calculations:**

⇒ LSA = Perimeter × Height

⇒ 384 = Perimeter × 12

⇒ Perimeter = 384 ÷ 12

⇒ Perimeter = 32 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 32 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Right Prism

A prism is a 3D solid with two identical and parallel polygonal bases. In a right prism, the lateral faces are always flat rectangles.

Volume of a Prism

The volume strictly relies on the area of the base. The formula is: Volume = Base Area × Height. For this particular shape, it would be 80 × 12 = 960 cm³.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

TSA = Lateral Surface Area + 2 × Base Area. For the given measurements, TSA = 384 + (2 × 80) = 544 cm².

Extraneous Data in Examinations

Competitive tests often inject extra numerical data to observe if candidates can identify the specific, required formula parameter. The base area was provided purely as a distraction from the straightforward relation.

question: A man walks a square plot of area 121 m². If he walks once around its boundary, how far does he walk?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side of the square = √Area = √121 = 11 m.

Distance walked in one round = Perimeter of the square.

Perimeter = 4 × Side = 4 × 11 = 44 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 44 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of the square plot = 121 m²

**Formula Used:**

Area of a square = (Side)²

Perimeter of a square = 4 × Side

 Area = 121 m2 Side = 11 m 11 m 11 m 11 m 11 m Distance Walked = Perimeter 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (Side)² = 121

⇒ Side = √121

⇒ Side = 11 m

The man walks once around the boundary, which is exactly equal to the perimeter of the square plot.

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × Side

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × 11

⇒ Perimeter = 44 m

**∴ The correct answer is 44 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Square

The region enclosed by the boundaries of a square is its area. It is given by the square of its side: Area = a², or by using the diagonal length (d): Area = d² ÷ 2.

Perimeter of a Square

The total length of the outer boundary of the square is its perimeter. It is calculated by adding all four equal sides together: Perimeter = 4a.

Diagonal of a Square

The straight line segment connecting two opposite corners of a square. Its length is calculated using the Pythagorean theorem as: Diagonal = a√2.

question: The width of the path around a square field is 4.5 m and its area is 105.75 m². Find the cost of fencing the field at the rate of Rs. 100 per meter.
solution:
**Given:**

The width of the path around a square field = 4.5 m

The area of the path = 105.75 m2

**Formula used:**

The perimeter of a square = 4 × Side

The area of a square = (Side)²

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/273325535b4eab9aacdb05e77bda70db8cbdad19bcb9dfe1f6589f46cb528595.png] **

Let, each side of the field = x

Then, each side with the path = x + 4.5 + 4.5 = x + 9

So, (x + 9)² - x² = 105.75

⇒ x2 + 18x + 81 - x2 = 105.75

⇒ 18x + 81 = 105.75

⇒ 18x = 105.75 - 81 = 24.75

⇒ x = 24.75/18 = 11/8

∴ Each side of the square field = 11/8 m

The perimterer = 4 × (11/8) = 11/2 m

So, the total cost of fencing = (11/2) × 100 = Rs. 550

**∴ The cost of fencing of the field is Rs. 550**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**In such types of questions, 

Area of path outside the Square is, 

⇒ (2a + 2w)2w = 105.75

here, a is a side of a square and w is width of a square

⇒ (2a + 9)9 = 105.75

⇒ 2a + 9 = 11.75

⇒ 2a = 2.75

Perimeter of a square = 4a

⇒ 2 × 2a = 2 × 2.75 = 5.50

costing of fencing = 5.50 × 100 = 550

∴ The cost of fencing of the field is Rs. 550

question: A plot has an area of 625 m². If a footpath 1 m wide is constructed around it, what is the total area including the footpath?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the area of the plot is 625 m² (a perfect square), we consider it a square plot.

Side of the square plot = √625 = 25 m.

A 1 m wide path outside increases the side by 2 m (1 m on each opposite side).

New side of the boundary = 25 + 2 = 27 m.

Total area including the path = 27² = 729 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 729 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of the plot = 625 m²

Width of the footpath (w) = 1 m

**Formula Used:**

Area of square = (Side)²

Outer side = Inner side + 2 × Width of path

**Calculation:**

⇒ Side of the square plot (a) = √625 = 25 m

⇒ The 1 m wide footpath surrounds the plot uniformly.

⇒ Total side length including the path = a + 2w = 25 + 2 × 1

⇒ Outer side = 27 m

⇒ Total area including the footpath = (27)²

⇒ Total area = 729 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 729 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Path Outside a Square/Rectangle

When a path of width 'w' is built completely outside a shape, its length and breadth both increase by 2w. For a square of side 'a', Area of path = 4w(a + w).

Area of Path Inside a Square/Rectangle

When a path of width 'w' is built completely inside a shape, its interior length and breadth both decrease by 2w. For a square of side 'a', Area of path = 4w(a − w).

Intersecting Paths (Cross Path)

If two perpendicular paths of width 'w' run parallel to the length and breadth through the center of a rectangular plot, Area of path = w(L + B − w).

question: If the length of certain rectangle is decreased by 4 cm and breadth is increased by 2 cm, it would result in a square of the same area. What is the perimeter of the original rectangle?
solution:
**Given: **

The length of a certain rectangle is decreased by 4 cm and the breadth is increased by 2 cm, 

It would result in a square of the same area 

**Concept used: **

Area of rectangle = L × B 

Area of square = Side × Side 

Perimeter of rectangle = 2(L + B)

**Calculations: **

Let length be L and breadth be B, 

Since the sides of the square are equal, 

⇒ L − 4 = B + 2 ...........(1) 

⇒ L = B + 6 

The area of the rectangle is equal to the area of the square, 

L × B = (L - 4)(B + 2) 

⇒ (B + 6)(B) = (B + 6 - 4)(B + 2) 

⇒ B² + 6B = (B + 2)² 

⇒ B2 + 6B = B² + 4B + 4

⇒ 6B = 4B + 4 

⇒ 2B = 4

⇒ B = 2 cm

then form (1) we get,

⇒ L - 4 = B + 2

⇒ L - 4 = 2 + 2

⇒ L = 4 + 4 = 8 cm

Now the Perimeter of the rectangle,

⇒ P = 2(8 + 2)

⇒ P = 2(10) = 20 cm

**∴ The perimeter of the original rectangle is 20 cm.**

question: A cuboid with sides 4, 6 and 8 units is covered with paper. The paper is removed and a square is made from it. What is the side (in units) of the square?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total area of the paper = Total Surface Area of the cuboid.

TSA = 2 × (lb + bh + hl) = 2 × (48 + 24 + 32) = 208 sq. units.

The paper forms a square, so Area of square = side² = 208.

side = √208 ≈ 14.42 units (since 14² = 196 and 15² = 225).

**∴ The correct answer is 14.42 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 8 4 6 Cuboid 
• 
 Unfolded Area = 208 a a Square 

**Given:**

Sides of the cuboid:

Length (l) = 8 units

Breadth (b) = 6 units

Height (h) = 4 units

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of Cuboid = 2 × (lb + bh + hl)

Area of Square = a² (where a is the side of the square)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of the paper used to cover the cuboid = Total Surface Area of the cuboid

⇒ Area = 2 × (8 × 6 + 6 × 4 + 4 × 8)

⇒ Area = 2 × (48 + 24 + 32)

⇒ Area = 2 × 104 = 208 sq. units

This same paper is completely used to form a square. Therefore, the area of the square is equal to the area of the paper.

⇒ Area of the square = 208 sq. units

⇒ a² = 208

⇒ a = √208

We know that 14² = 196 and 15² = 225. Thus, √208 lies between 14 and 15.

⇒ a ≈ 14.42 units

**∴ The correct answer is 14.42 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cuboid

It is the sum of the areas of its 6 rectangular faces. The formula is given by TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl).

Area and Perimeter of a Square

For a square with side length 'a', the Area is calculated as a² and the total perimeter boundary is 4a.

Conservation of Surface Area

When a 2D sheet such as paper or foil is unwrapped from a 3D object and reshaped without cutting or overlapping, its total surface area remains perfectly constant.

question: A rectangular piece of paper is 50 cm long and 22 cm wide. If a cylinder is formed by rolling the paper along its breadth, then the volume of the cylinder is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When rolled along its breadth, Breadth (B) = Circumference, and Length (L) = Height.

Direct formula for Volume = (B² × L) ÷ 4π

Volume = (22 × 22 × 50 × 7) ÷ (4 × 22)

Volume = 7700 ÷ 4 = 1925 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1925 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f04c7b44d5ff43c7f6796feb371b0dd52694522517860d696e37db25cb2be686.png] 

**Given:**

Length of paper (l) = 50 cm

Breadth of paper (b) = 22 cm

When the rectangular sheet is rolled along its breadth:

Circumference of the cylinder's base = 22 cm

Height of the cylinder (h) = 50 cm

**Formula Used:**

Circumference = 2πr

Volume of Cylinder = πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 22

⇒ r = (22 × 7) ÷ (2 × 22)

⇒ r = 3.5 cm

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5 × 50

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × (7/2) × (7/2) × 50

⇒ Volume = 11 × 7 × 25

⇒ Volume = 1925 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1925 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rolling a Rectangular Sheet

When rolled along its length, the length forms the circumference and the breadth becomes the height. When rolled along its breadth, the breadth forms the circumference and the length becomes the height.

Surface Areas of a Cylinder

The Curved Surface Area (CSA) is given by 2πrh, and the Total Surface Area (TSA) is 2πr(h + r), where r is the radius and h is the height.

Relationship with Cone

A cylinder and a cone with the same base radius and height have volumes in the ratio 3:1. The volume of the cone is 1/3 × πr²h.
</p

question: The area of a square is 16x² + 40x + 25 square units. Find the perimeter of the square.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of square = 16x² + 40x + 25 = (4x)² + 2(4x)(5) + 5² = (4x + 5)².

Side of the square = √(4x + 5)² = 4x + 5.

Perimeter = 4 × Side = 4 × (4x + 5) = 16x + 20.

Taking 2 as a common factor, Perimeter = 2(8x + 10).

**∴ The correct answer is 2(8x + 10).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/acd68c1e109ee446f3b2cc9e922bcf38055809b5dc415c090abf238d3485a672.png] 

**Given:**

Area of the square = 16x² + 40x + 25

**Formula Used:**

Area of a square = (Side)²

Perimeter of a square = 4 × Side

Algebraic Identity: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

**Calculation:**

⇒ (Side)² = 16x² + 40x + 25

⇒ (Side)² = (4x)² + 2 × (4x) × 5 + (5)²

⇒ (Side)² = (4x + 5)²

⇒ Side = 4x + 5

Now, calculate the perimeter:

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × (4x + 5)

⇒ Perimeter = 16x + 20

⇒ Perimeter = 2(8x + 10)

**∴ The correct answer is 2(8x + 10).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

Standard identities include (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b². These are frequently used to form perfect squares in geometry problems.

Properties of a Square

All four sides are equal, and each interior angle is 90°. The diagonals are equal and bisect each other at right angles.

Diagonal of a Square

The diagonal is given by the formula d = Side × √2. The area can also be determined directly from the diagonal using the relation Area = d² ÷ 2.
</p

question: Find the area of a square, one of whose diagonals is 4.8 m long.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The area of a square can be directly calculated if the length of its diagonal is known.

Area of square = (Diagonal)² ÷ 2

Area = (4.8)² ÷ 2

Area = 23.04 ÷ 2 = 11.52 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 11.52 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the diagonal of the square (d) = 4.8 m

**Formula Used:**

Diagonal of a square = √2 × Side

Area of a square = (Side)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5b3e9f1599b17ba5a19e6ec5793ac678c37957e77cf8ca13d615118e62a9883.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Side of the square = Diagonal ÷ √2

⇒ Side = 4.8 ÷ √2 m

⇒ Area of the square = (4.8 ÷ √2)²

⇒ Area = (4.8 × 4.8) ÷ (√2 × √2)

⇒ Area = 23.04 ÷ 2

⇒ Area = 11.52 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 11.52 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Square

The perimeter is the total continuous length of the boundary of the square. It is calculated as P = 4 × Side.

Diagonal and Side Relation

A diagonal divides the square into two identical right-angled isosceles triangles. Applying Pythagoras theorem, the relationship formed is Diagonal = √2 × Side.

Circumcircle of a Square

The diagonal of the square is equal to the diameter of its circumscribed circle. The Circumradius (R) is given by R = Diagonal ÷ 2.
</p

question: The perimeter of a rectangular garden is 48 m. If the length is 6 m more than the breadth, the area (in m²) of the garden is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of Length (L) and Breadth (B) = Perimeter ÷ 2 = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 m

Given the difference L − B = 6 m

L = (24 + 6) ÷ 2 = 15 m

B = (24 − 6) ÷ 2 = 9 m

Area = L × B = 15 × 9 = 135 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 135 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of rectangular garden = 48 m

Length (L) = Breadth (B) + 6 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b3c8a5077d25803edb0573b2cf36f111ae87860c2a822466ea795cd5a96285e.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of rectangle = 2(L + B)

Area of rectangle = L × B

**Calculation:**

⇒ 2(B + 6 + B) = 48

⇒ 2(2B + 6) = 48

⇒ 2B + 6 = 24

⇒ 2B = 18

⇒ B = 9 m

⇒ L = 9 + 6 = 15 m

⇒ Area = L × B

⇒ Area = 15 × 9 = 135 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 135 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rectangle

Opposite sides are equal and parallel. All interior angles are exactly 90°.

Diagonal of a Rectangle

Length of diagonal = √(L² + B²). Diagonals are equal in length and bisect each other.

Square as a Rectangle

A square is a special type of rectangle where Length = Breadth. For a square, Area = Side² and Perimeter = 4 × Side.
</p

question: In a rectangular field, the sum of the length and the breadth is 9 cm and area is 18 cm². If the length is 'a' and breadth is 'b', then find the value of (a² − ab + b²).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given the sum of the sides a + b = 9 and their product ab = 18.

By finding two numbers that add up to 9 and multiply to 18, we can easily identify the sides as a = 6 and b = 3.

We need to find the value of (a² − ab + b²).

Substitute the values directly: 6² − (6 × 3) + 3²

⇒ 36 − 18 + 9 = 27

**∴ The correct answer is 27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the rectangular field = a

Breadth of the rectangular field = b

Sum of length and breadth (a + b) = 9 cm

Area of the rectangular field (ab) = 18 cm²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/604a3ea271f88c2f88aa8143864345c18ba66fb13e7d15c6631a9017d01945ea.png] 

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculations:**

From the standard algebraic identity, we can modify the required expression as follows:

⇒ a² − ab + b² = (a² + b² + 2ab) − 3ab

⇒ a² − ab + b² = (a + b)² − 3ab

Now, substitute the given values (a + b = 9 and ab = 18) into the modified equation:

⇒ a² − ab + b² = (9)² − 3 × 18

⇒ a² − ab + b² = 81 − 54

⇒ a² − ab + b² = 27

**∴ The correct answer is 27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Rectangle

The total boundary length of a rectangle, calculated using the formula P = 2(l + b).

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The longest straight line distance between two opposite corners, given by the Pythagorean relationship d = √(l² + b²).

Algebraic Cube Identities

The expression calculated above frequently appears in the sum of cubes formula: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).
</p

question: A circular logo of radius 14 cm is fitted perfectly inside a square plaque. Find the area of unused square space around the circle.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The unused area when a circle is perfectly inscribed in a square is directly given by the formula: **r²(4 − π)**

Substitute the given radius r = 14 cm, and use a precise value for π ≈ 3.1416:

Unused Area = 14² × (4 − 3.1416)

Unused Area = 196 × 0.8584 ≈ 168.25 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 168.25 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the circular logo (r) = 14 cm

**Formula Used:**

Side of the circumscribing square (a) = 2 × r

Area of square = a²

Area of circle = πr²

Unused square space = Area of square − Area of circle

 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 r = 14 cm
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Side = 28 cm
 Unused space (shaded blue)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Side of the square (a) = 2 × 14 = 28 cm

⇒ Area of the square = 28 × 28 = 784 cm²

⇒ Area of the circular logo = 3.1416 × 14 × 14 ≈ 615.75 cm²

⇒ Unused square space = 784 − 615.75 = 168.25 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 168.25 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Circumscribed Square

When a circle of radius r perfectly fits (is inscribed) inside a square, the side of the square is exactly the diameter of the circle (2r). The area of the square evaluates to 4r².

Area of Inscribed Square

Conversely, if a square is inscribed inside a circle of radius r, its diagonal matches the circle's diameter (2r), and its area calculates to 2r².

Inscribed Area Ratio

The ratio of the area of an inscribed circle to the area of its circumscribing square is π : 4. This implies the circle covers approximately 78.5% of the total square space.
</p

question: The sides of a rectangular prism are in the ratio 4:5:6. If the volume of the prism is 960 cm³ what is the length of its longest side?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let the sides of the rectangular prism be 4x, 5x, and 6x.

Volume = 4x × 5x × 6x = 120x³

Since the volume is 960 cm³, we have 120x³ = 960.

⇒ x³ = 8 ⇒ x = 2

The longest side is 6x = 6 × 2 = 12 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The ratio of the sides of the rectangular prism = 4 : 5 : 6

Volume of the prism = 960 cm³

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a rectangular prism = Length × Width × Height

 
 

 
 

 
 

 
 
 Length = 6x
 Height = 4x
 Width = 5x
 Volume = 960 cm³

**Calculations:**

Let the exact dimensions of the sides be 4x, 5x, and 6x.

⇒ Volume = 4x × 5x × 6x

⇒ 120x³ = 960

⇒ x³ = 960 ÷ 120

⇒ x³ = 8

⇒ x = 2

Now, finding the exact lengths of all three sides:

⇒ First side = 4 × 2 = 8 cm

⇒ Second side = 5 × 2 = 10 cm

⇒ Third side = 6 × 2 = 12 cm

⇒ Out of the three, the longest side is clearly 12 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The total area of all 6 faces of a cuboid is calculated using the formula: TSA = 2(lw + wh + hl).

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

The area of the 4 side vertical faces (excluding the top and bottom) is calculated as: LSA = 2h(l + w).

Length of Diagonal

The longest distance between two opposite corners in a rectangular prism is given by the formula: Diagonal = √(l² + w² + h²).
</p

question: A display stand is shaped like a right triangular prism. The triangular base is a right-angled triangle with perpendicular sides measuring 3 cm and 4 cm. The height of the prism is 10 cm. What is the ratio of the area of the largest rectangular face to the area of the smallest rectangular face of the prism?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The rectangular faces of a right triangular prism all share the exact same height.

Thus, their areas are strictly proportional to the side lengths of the triangular base.

The base sides are 3 cm, 4 cm, and the hypotenuse = √(3² + 4²) = 5 cm.

Area of largest face → corresponds to the largest side (5 cm).

Area of smallest face → corresponds to the smallest side (3 cm).

**∴ The correct answer is 5:3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base of the prism = Right-angled triangle with perpendicular sides 3 cm and 4 cm.

Height of the prism = 10 cm.

 
 
 4 cm 3 cm 5 cm Base 30 cm² Small 40 cm² Medium 50 cm² Large 3 cm 4 cm 5 cm 
• 
• 
• 10 cm 

**Formula Used:**

Hypotenuse = √(Base² + Perpendicular²)

Area of rectangular face = Side of base × Height of prism

**Calculations:**

⇒ Hypotenuse of the base triangle = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 cm

⇒ The lengths of the 3 sides of the base are 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm.

⇒ Area of the smallest rectangular face = Smallest side × Height = 3 × 10 = 30 cm²

⇒ Area of the largest rectangular face = Largest side × Height = 5 × 10 = 50 cm²

⇒ Required Ratio = Area of largest face : Area of smallest face

⇒ Required Ratio = 50 : 30 = 5 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 5:3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Right Prism vs Oblique Prism

In a right prism, the lateral faces are always perpendicular to the bases, resulting in entirely rectangular lateral faces. In an oblique prism, the lateral edges are slanted and the lateral faces are parallelograms.

Total Surface Area of Prism

The total surface area (TSA) of any prism is given by: TSA = Lateral Surface Area + 2 × (Base Area). For a right prism, the Lateral Surface Area equals Perimeter of Base × Height.

Volume of a Prism

question: The base of a prism is a rectangle whose length is twice its width. The perimeter of the base is 30 cm. The prism's height decreases in an arithmetic progression from 15 cm in the first layer to 9 cm in the fourth layer. What is the total volume of the prism?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given L = 2W. Base perimeter = 2 × (2W + W) = 6W = 30 ⇒ W = 5 cm, L = 10 cm.

Base Area = L × W = 10 × 5 = 50 cm².

Heights form an AP for 4 layers: 15 cm to 9 cm.

Total Height = Sum of AP = (4 ÷ 2) × (15 + 9) = 2 × 24 = 48 cm.

Total Volume = Base Area × Total Height = 50 × 48 = 2400 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 2400 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Base perimeter = 30 cm

⇒ Length (L) = 2 × Width (W)

⇒ Heights of 4 layers are in AP with 1st term = 15 cm and 4th term = 9 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Perimeter of rectangle = 2 × (L + W)

⇒ Area of rectangle = L × W

⇒ Sum of AP = n ÷ 2 × (First term + Last term)

⇒ Total Volume = Base Area × Total Height

 
• 
• 
• Total Height 48 cm Prism Layers Layer 4: 9 cm Layer 3: 11 cm Layer 2: 13 cm Layer 1: 15 cm Base of Prism L = 10 cm W = 5 cm Base Area 50 cm² Perimeter = 30 cm 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (2W + W) = 30

⇒ 6W = 30 ⇒ W = 5 cm

⇒ L = 2 × 5 = 10 cm

⇒ Base Area = 10 × 5 = 50 cm²

⇒ The heights of the 4 layers form an AP where n = 4, first term a = 15, last term l = 9.

⇒ Total Height = 4 ÷ 2 × (15 + 9) = 2 × 24 = 48 cm

⇒ Total Volume = Base Area × Total Height

⇒ Total Volume = 50 × 48 = 2400 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 2400 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a General Prism

The volume of any uniform prism is calculated as the product of its base area and total vertical height: V = Base Area × Height.

Arithmetic Progression (AP) Sum Formula

When the first term (a) and last term (l) of an AP are known, the sum of n terms is derived using the formula: Sₙ = n ÷ 2 × (a + l).

Composite Solids Concept

For a solid structure generated by stacking individual uniformly based layers on top of each other, the total aggregate volume is essentially the continuous base area multiplied by the net sum of all vertical layer heights.

question: A rectangular aquarium (100 cm L × 50 cm W × 60 cm H) contains water with an initial level of 20 cm. 10 identical metal spheres, each with a diameter of 10 cm, are gently lowered into the aquarium. Assuming the spheres are fully submerged, what is the rise in the water level?
solution:

Rise in water level = (Total Volume of submerged objects) ÷ (Base Area of the container)

Rise in level = [10 × (4/3) × π × 5³] ÷ (100 × 50)

Rise in level = (5000π / 3) ÷ 5000

Rise in level = π/3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is π/3 cm.**

⇒ Number of metal spheres (n) = 10

⇒ Diameter of each sphere = 10 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 5 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

⇒ Displaced Volume = Base Area of container × Rise in fluid level

 
 
• 
• 
• 20 cm 
• 
• Rise: h Base Area = 100 × 50 = 5000 cm² 
• 10 Spheres r = 5 cm Volume Displaced = Total Volume of Spheres 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Base area of the aquarium = 100 × 50 = 5000 cm²

⇒ Volume of one sphere = (4/3) × π × 5³ = 500π / 3 cm³

⇒ Total volume of 10 spheres = 10 × (500π / 3) = 5000π / 3 cm³

question: Two right prisms have the same height of 10 cm. One has a regular hexagonal base with side 6 cm, and the other has a square base with side 6 cm. What is the ratio of their volumes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two right prisms have the same height, the ratio of their volumes is strictly equal to the ratio of their base areas.

Ratio = Area of regular hexagonal base : Area of square base

Ratio = [6 × (√3 / 4) × a²] : a²

Since the side length a = 6 cm is identical for both, a² cancels out completely.

Ratio = (3√3 / 2) : 1 = 3√3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3√3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Side of the regular hexagonal base (a) = 6 cm

Side of the square base (b) = 6 cm

Height of both right prisms (h) = 10 cm

Volume of a prism = Area of base × height

Area of a regular hexagon = (3√3 / 2) × (side)²

Area of a square = (side)²

 
 Hexagonal Base a = 6 cm Square Base b = 6 cm Ratio of Volumes = Ratio of Base Areas 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Volume of the hexagonal prism (V₁) = [(3√3 / 2) × 6²] × 10

⇒ V₁ = (3√3 / 2) × 36 × 10

⇒ V₁ = 54√3 × 10 = 540√3 cm³

⇒ Volume of the square prism (V₂) = [6²] × 10

⇒ V₂ = 36 × 10 = 360 cm³

⇒ Ratio of their volumes = V₁ : V₂

⇒ Ratio = 540√3 : 360

⇒ Dividing both sides by 180, we get:

⇒ Ratio = 3√3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3√3 : 2.**

The volume of any right prism is calculated by multiplying its base area by its height. Formula: V = Base Area × height.

The total surface area encompasses all the faces of the 3D shape. Formula: TSA = Lateral Surface Area + 2 × Base Area, where Lateral Surface Area = Base Perimeter × height.

Area of a parallelogram = Base × Height

⇒ Area = 468 cm²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Parallelogram (Trigonometric)

It can also be calculated as the product of any two adjacent sides multiplied by the sine of the included angle: Area = a × b × sin(θ).

Perimeter of a Parallelogram

The perimeter is the total distance around the outside, given by the formula: 2 × (Sum of adjacent sides).

Area of a Rhombus

A rhombus is a special parallelogram with all equal sides. Its area is calculated as ½ × d₁ × d₂, where d₁ and d₂ are the lengths of the diagonals.

Area of a Trapezium

The area of a trapezium is given by ½ × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height.

question: The area of a sector of a circle is 66 cm² and the angle of the sector is 60°. Find the radius of the circle.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Area of Circle = Area of Sector × (360° / θ)

πr² = 66 × (360 / 60) = 66 × 6 = 396 cm²

r² = 396 ÷ (22/7) = 396 × (7 / 22) = 18 × 7 = 126

r = √126 = √(9 × 14) = 3√14 cm

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of sector = 66 cm²

Angle of sector (θ) = 60°

Value of π ≈ 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Area of sector = (θ / 360°) × πr²

 
 

 60°

•

**Calculations:**

⇒ 66 = (60 / 360) × (22 / 7) × r²

⇒ 66 = (1 / 6) × (22 / 7) × r²

⇒ 66 = (22 / 42) × r²

⇒ r² = (66 × 42) / 22

⇒ r² = 3 × 42

⇒ r² = 126

⇒ r = √126

⇒ r = √(9 × 14)

⇒ r = 3√14 cm

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Length of Arc

The length of the arc of a sector is given by l = (θ / 360°) × 2πr.

Perimeter of a Sector

The perimeter includes the arc length plus two radii: P = l + 2r = [(θ / 360°) × 2πr] + 2r.

Area of Circle

The total area of a circle with radius r is A = πr².

Area in terms of Arc Length

If the arc length l is known, the area of the sector can be calculated as A = (1/2) × l × r.</p

question: Find the area (in cm²) of the sector whose perimeter is 64/3 cm and central angle is 60º. (Use π = 22/7)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Perimeter of a sector = r(2 + πθ/180°)

Given Perimeter = 64/3 cm and central angle θ = 60°.

⇒ r(2 + (22/7) × 60/180) = 64/3 ⇒ r(2 + 22/21) = 64/3 ⇒ r(64/21) = 64/3 ⇒ r = 7 cm.

Area of sector = (θ/360°) × πr² = (60/360) × 22/7 × 7²

Area = 1/6 × 154 = 77/3 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 77/3 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of the sector = 64/3 cm

Central angle (θ) = 60°

Value of π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Arc length (l) = (θ/360°) × 2πr

Perimeter of sector = 2r + l

Area of sector = (θ/360°) × πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2f236a8966fa88d5c2cca60cffa0b39f7102e2c1868d3046a817846eaa420c94.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Arc length (l) = (60/360) × 2 × (22/7) × r

⇒ l = (1/6) × (44/7) × r

⇒ l = 22r/21

⇒ Perimeter = 2r + 22r/21 = (42r + 22r)/21

⇒ Perimeter = 64r/21

Equating the formula with the given value:

⇒ 64r/21 = 64/3

⇒ r/21 = 1/3

⇒ r = 21/3 = 7 cm

Now, substitute the radius to find the area of the sector:

⇒ Area = (60/360) × (22/7) × (7)²

⇒ Area = (1/6) × (22/7) × 49

⇒ Area = (1/6) × 22 × 7

⇒ Area = 154/6

⇒ Area = 77/3 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 77/3 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

The region enclosed by two radii and the corresponding arc. The formula is A = (θ/360°) × πr² or alternatively A = 1/2 × l × r, where l is the arc length.

Length of an Arc

The continuous portion of the circumference of a circle. The length is determined by the central angle using the formula l = (θ/360°) × 2πr.

Perimeter of a Sector

The total boundary length of the sector, which is the sum of the two radii and the arc length. Formula: Perimeter = 2r + l.
</p

question: The side of an equilateral triangle is 28 cm. Taking each vertex as the centre, a circle is described with a radius equal to half the length of the side of the triangle. Find the area of that part of the triangle which is not included in the circles (use π = 22/7).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The sum of the three 60° sectors at the vertices of an equilateral triangle forms exactly one semicircle.

Required Area = Area of Equilateral Triangle − Area of Semicircle

Required Area = [(√3 ÷ 4) × side²] − [(1 ÷ 2) × π × radius²]

Required Area = [(√3 ÷ 4) × 28²] − [(1 ÷ 2) × (22 ÷ 7) × 14²]

Required Area = (196 × 1.73) − 308 = 339.08 − 308 = 31.08 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 31.08 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/44564a3a1189fa45ed5aaffa617c80ba67f1a5b6e7cab1e037bab590b1756230.png] 

**Given:**

Side of the equilateral triangle, a = 28 cm

Radius of the circle, r = a ÷ 2 = 14 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of an equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × a²

Area of a sector of angle θ = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area of the equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × 28²

⇒ Area of triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × 784 = 196√3 cm²

⇒ Taking √3 ≈ 1.73, Area = 196 × 1.73 = 339.08 cm²

⇒ The triangle has three identical sectors, each with a central angle of 60°.

⇒ Total area of 3 sectors = 3 × (60° ÷ 360°) × π × 14²

⇒ Total sector area = 3 × (1 ÷ 6) × (22 ÷ 7) × 196

⇒ Total sector area = (1 ÷ 2) × 22 × 28 = 11 × 28 = 308 cm²

⇒ Area of the remaining part = Area of triangle − Area of 3 sectors

⇒ Area of the remaining part = 339.08 − 308 = 31.08 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 31.08 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Equilateral Triangle

All three sides are equal, and all internal angles are 60°. The height is given by (√3 ÷ 2) × a.

Area of a Circular Sector

The area of a sector with central angle θ and radius r is given by the formula: A = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr².

Incircle and Circumcircle

For an equilateral triangle of side a, the inradius r = a ÷ (2√3) and circumradius R = a ÷ √3. Their area ratio is always 1 : 4.
</p

Use the direct relationship for the area of a sector: Area = ½ × L × r

⇒ Area = ½ × 44 × 84 = 1848 cm²

⇒ L = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

⇒ 44 = (30° ÷ 360°) × 2 × (22/7) × r

⇒ 44 = (1/12) × (44/7) × r

⇒ 1 = (1/12) × (1/7) × r

⇒ r = 12 × 7

⇒ r = 84 cm

Now, substitute the value of the radius into the area formula:

⇒ Area = ½ × L × r

⇒ Area = ½ × 44 × 84

⇒ Area = 22 × 84

⇒ Area = 1848 cm²

The arc length is directly proportional to the central angle subtended: L = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

The total boundary length includes the arc length plus two times the radius: Perimeter = L + 2r.

question: Find the measure of the central angle of a sector if its area is 16π and the radius is 8.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total area of the circle = π × r² = π × 8² = 64π

Area of the sector is given as 16π.

Ratio of sector area to total area = 16π ÷ 64π = 1/4

Central angle = (1/4) × 360° = 90°

**∴ The correct answer is 90°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ 16π = (θ ÷ 360°) × π × (8)²

⇒ 16π = (θ ÷ 360°) × 64π

⇒ 16 ÷ 64 = θ ÷ 360°

⇒ 1/4 = θ ÷ 360°

⇒ θ = 360° ÷ 4 = 90°

**∴ The correct answer is 90°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The length of an arc of a sector with central angle θ is given by l = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

question: If the area of a sector of a circle is 462 cm² and the central angle is 120°, then its radius is ___.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A central angle of 120° means the sector is exactly 1/3 of a full circle.

Area of full circle = Area of sector × 3 = 462 × 3 = 1386 cm².

⇒ πr² = 1386

⇒ (22 ÷ 7) × r² = 1386

⇒ r² = 1386 × (7 ÷ 22) = 63 × 7 = 441

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ 462 = (1 ÷ 3) × (22 ÷ 7) × r²

⇒ r² = (462 × 3 × 7) ÷ 22

⇒ r² = 21 × 3 × 7

⇒ r² = 441

⇒ r = √441

⇒ r = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The area of a sector of a circle with radius r and central angle θ (in degrees) represents a proportional slice of the entire circle's area. It is calculated using the formula: A = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr².

Perimeter of a Sector

The complete boundary or perimeter of a sector includes the curved arc length along with the two straight radii enclosing it. The formula is: Perimeter = L + 2r.

A central angle of 90° means the sector is exactly a quarter of the full circle.

question: A sector of a circle with a radius of 15 cm has a central angle of 45°. Another sector of the same circle has a central angle of π/4 radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to the area of the second sector?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For sectors of the same circle, the area is directly proportional to the central angle.

Angle of the first sector = 45°

Angle of the second sector = π/4 radians = (180° ÷ 4) = 45°

Since both central angles are equal, their areas will be exactly the same.

**∴ The correct answer is 1:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

Area of a sector (when θ is in degrees) = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

Area of a sector (when θ is in radians) = (1 ÷ 2) × r²θ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of first sector = (45° ÷ 360°) × π × (15)²

⇒ Area of first sector = (1 ÷ 8) × 225π = 28.125π cm²

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector of a circle with radius r and central angle θ is given by (θ ÷ 360°) × πr² if θ is measured in degrees, and (1 ÷ 2)r²θ if θ is measured in radians.

Radian to Degree Conversion

To convert an angle from radians into degrees, multiply the radian value by (180° ÷ π). For example, π radians equals 180°.

Length of an Arc

The arc length of a corresponding sector is calculated as (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr (for degrees) or simply rθ (for radians).
</p

question: What is the area of the segment formed by a chord in a circle of radius 12 cm, if the angle subtended at the center is 150°?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for the Area of a Segment:

⇒ Area = r² × [(π × θ ÷ 360°) − (sin θ ÷ 2)]

⇒ Area = 12² × [(π × 150° ÷ 360°) − (sin 150° ÷ 2)]

⇒ Area = 144 × [(5π ÷ 12) − (1 ÷ 4)]

⇒ Area = 60π − 36 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 60π−36 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Area of Segment = Area of Sector − Area of Triangle

**Given:**

⇒ Radius of the circle (r) = 12 cm

⇒ Angle subtended at the center (θ) = 150°

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Area of Sector = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

⇒ Area of Triangle = (1 ÷ 2) × r² × sin θ

⇒ Area of Segment = Area of Sector − Area of Triangle

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of Sector = (150° ÷ 360°) × π × 12²

⇒ Area of Sector = (5 ÷ 12) × π × 144 = 60π cm²

⇒ To find the area of the triangle, we use sin(150°) = sin(180° − 30°) = sin(30°) = 1 ÷ 2

⇒ Area of Triangle = (1 ÷ 2) × 12² × (1 ÷ 2)

⇒ Area of Triangle = (1 ÷ 2) × 144 × (1 ÷ 2) = 36 cm²

⇒ Area of Segment = 60π − 36 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 60π−36 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Major Segment

It is calculated by subtracting the area of the minor segment from the total area of the circle: Area = πr² − Area of Minor Segment.

Length of an Arc

The arc length corresponding to a central angle θ is a fraction of the circle's circumference: L = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

Perimeter of a Sector

The boundary length of a sector comprises the arc length and two radii: Perimeter = L + 2r.
</p

question: A circular clock has a radius of 14 cm. Calculate the distance covered by the tip of the minute hand in 30 minutes, assuming it is positioned at the edge of the clock face? (Use π= 22/7)

The minute hand covers a complete circle (360°) in 60 minutes.

In 30 minutes, it covers exactly half of the circular path.

Distance covered in 30 minutes = Half of circumference = π × r

Distance = (22/7) × 14 = 44 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 44 cm.**

Area of a full circle = πr² = (22 ÷ 7) × 14 × 14 = 616 cm².

The given area of the sector is 154 cm².

Ratio of the sector area to the full circle area = 154 ÷ 616 = 1 ÷ 4.

Since the area is proportional to the central angle, the angle must be 1/4 of a full circle (360°).

⇒ Sector angle = 360° × (1 ÷ 4) = 90°.

**∴ The correct answer is 90°.**

question: Points P and Q are on the sides AB and BC respectively of a triangle ABC, right angled at B. If AQ = 11 cm, PC = 8 cm. and AC = 13 cm, then find the length (in cm) of PQ:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e1251b4350e51d1697a1dc5f0fa7c5c5cd591854f59cc30ede9ee3adcc6751a7.png] 

In any right angled triange like above 

a = √(b² + c² - d²)

In the question, we have b = 11, c = 8 and d = 13

So, a = √(112 + 82 - 132) 

⇒ a = √16 = 4 cm

**∴ PQ = 4 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

ΔABC is a right-angled triangle at ∠B.

AQ = 11cm

PC = 8cm

AC = 13cm

Concept used: 

Pythagorean theorem states that the sum of the squares on the other two sides of a right-angled triangle is equal to the square on the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle)

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d838dfc74f1cb42b530d42e7c7408ed09aba48586f3fa17365d0dac403ff27d4.png] 

Let the length of AB, BC, BQ & PB be T, S, x & y respectively.

Now,

ΔABC, ΔABQ, ΔBPC and ΔPBQ are all right-angled triangles. 

From ΔABC,

⇒ S² + T² = 13² ....(1)

From ΔABQ,

⇒ x² + T2 = 112 ....(2)

From ΔBPC,

⇒ y² + S2 = 82 ....(3)

From ΔPBQ,

⇒ x2 + y2 = PQ2 ....(4)

Adding (2) & (3),

x2 + T2 + y2 + S2 = 112 + 82

⇒ x2 + y2 + (S2 + T2) = 185

⇒ x2 + y2 = 185 - (S2 + T2) 

⇒ x2 + y2 = 185 - 169

⇒ x2 + y2 = 16

⇒ x2 + y2 = 4²

⇒ PQ² = 4² (From 4)

⇒ PQ = 4 (∵ Negative value can't be consider for length)

**∴ The length of PQ is 4cm.**

question: In a right-angled triangle, the lengths of the medians from the vertices of acute angles are 7 cm and 4sqrt 6 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse of the triangle (in cm)?

**Given data:**

Length of medians = 7 cm and 4√6 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30114a2a0b4b788f47c15e7c5da94dfdcab5df97060f211983dddeb9dec13091.png] 

In Δ ABC, AE = BE and BD = DC

BE² + BC² = EC²

⇒ 96 = x2 + 4y2 - (Equation 1)

Applying Pythagora's theorem to the Δ ABD

AB2 + BD2 = AD2

Substituting the value, we get-

(2x)2 + y2 = 72

⇒ 49 = 4x2 + y2 - (Equation 2)

Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2, we get- 

⇒ 5x² + 5y² = 145

⇒ x2 + y2 = 29

In Δ BED, x2 + y2 = ED² 

⇒ ED = √29.

AC = 2ED = 2√29.

∴ **The length of the hypotenuse of the triangle is 2√29.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cfb223f18f06b7e490444707ced579af3dc366691afbb86f949a6be3fc487c2b.png]

⇒ 4(AD² + CE²) = 5AC²

Now, AD = 7 cm and CE = 4√6

⇒ 4[(7)² + (4√6)²] = 5AC²

⇒ 4(49 + 96) = 5AC²

⇒ 5AC² = 580

⇒ AC = 2√29

∴ The length of the hypotenuse of the triangle is 2√29.

question: The area of a triangle is 96 cm² and the ratio of its sides is 6 ∶ 8 ∶ 10. What is the perimeter of the triangle?
solution:
Given:

The area of a triangle is 96 cm2 and the ratio of its sides is 6 ∶ 8 ∶ 10.

Concept used:

Area of a triangle = sqrt {S (S - A) (S - B) (S - C)} (S = Semi-perimeter = (A + B + C)/2, where A, B, C are the measure of the sides of the triangle)

Calculation:

Let the sides of the triangle be 6k, 8k, and 10k respectively.

Perimeter of the triangle = (6k + 8k + 10k) = 24k

Semi-perimeter = 24k/2 = 12k

​According to the concept,

sqrt {12k (12k - 6k) (12k - 8k) (12k - 10k) } = 96

⇒ sqrt {12k times 6k times 4k times 2k} = 96

⇒ sqrt {144 times 4 times k⁴} = 96

⇒ 24k² = 96

⇒ k² = 96/24

⇒ k² = 4

⇒ k = 2

⇒ 24k = 48

∴ The perimeter of the triangle is 48 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The ratio of sides of the triangle is 6 ∶ 8 ∶ 10, [ as we know 6, 8, 10 are Pythagorean triplets]

Let the sides of the triangle be 6k, 8k, and 10k respectively.

So, the triangle is a right-angle triangle, area = 1/2 × base × height 

⇒ 1/2 × 6k × 8k = 96 

⇒ k2 = 4 

⇒ k = 2

So, the perimeter of the triangle is ⇒ (6k + 8k + 10k) = 24k = 24 × 2 = 48 cm

question: A right-angled isosceles triangle has an area of 50 square units. Its hypotenuse is (in units):
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a right-angled isosceles triangle, the area can be directly related to its hypotenuse (h) using the relation: Area = h² ÷ 4

⇒ 50 = h² ÷ 4

⇒ h² = 200

⇒ h = √200 = 10√2

**∴ The correct answer is 10√2 units.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of the right-angled isosceles triangle = 50 sq. units

**Formula Used:**

Area of a triangle = (1 ÷ 2) × base × height

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse = √(base² + height²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64d4c6abae86526402af13df84876ac2a747e43c4584bdb0ab477a359a9759ec.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the equal sides (base and height) be 'a' units.

⇒ Area = (1 ÷ 2) × a × a = 50

⇒ a² = 50 × 2

⇒ a² = 100

⇒ a = 10 units

⇒ Now, applying Pythagoras Theorem to find the hypotenuse:

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(a² + a²)

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(10² + 10²)

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(100 + 100)

⇒ Hypotenuse = √200

⇒ Hypotenuse = 10√2 units

**∴ The correct answer is 10√2 units.**

**__Additional Information__**

Right-angled Isosceles Triangle Properties

The angles in a right-angled isosceles triangle are always 90°, 45° and 45°. The ratio of its sides is consistently 1 : 1 : √2.

Perimeter

The perimeter of a right-angled isosceles triangle with equal sides 'a' is given by P = a(2 + √2).

Hypotenuse-Area Relationship

If the length of the hypotenuse is 'h', the area can be easily determined directly as Area = h² ÷ 4 without calculating the lengths of the legs.

Pythagorean Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76daef287940965b19fbefe3f121b47d7ec405e8ee74ab5678dbaee41007c21a.png]

⇒ Area of ΔABC = √(25 × 15 × 5 × 5) = √(9375) = 25√15 cm²

⇒ Given √15 ≈ 3.87, Area = 25 × 3.87 = 96.75 cm²

question: A triangle has sides 8 cm and 10 cm, and the angle between them is 120°. What is its area?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a triangle = ½ × a × b × sin(θ)

Given sides a = 8 cm, b = 10 cm and angle θ = 120°

Area = ½ × 8 × 10 × sin(120°)

Area = 40 × √3 / 2 = 20√3 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 20√3 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Two sides of a triangle, a = 8 cm and b = 10 cm

⇒ Included angle between the sides, θ = 120°

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Area of triangle = ½ × a × b × sin(θ)

 
 
 120° A B C 10 cm 8 cm 

**Calculations:**

⇒ sin(120°) = sin(180° − 60°) = sin(60°) = √3 / 2

⇒ Substituting the values in the area formula:

⇒ Area = ½ × 8 × 10 × (√3 / 2)

⇒ Area = 4 × 10 × (√3 / 2)

⇒ Area = 40 × √3 / 2

⇒ Area = 20√3 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 20√3 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area Using Base and Height

When the base and perpendicular height of a triangle are given: Area = ½ × base × height.

Heron's Formula

When all three sides (a, b, c) of a triangle are known: Area = √[s × (s − a) × (s − b) × (s − c)], where s = (a + b + c) / 2 is the semi-perimeter.

Sine Rule Formula for Area

The area of any triangle can be calculated using two sides and the included angle: Area = ½ × a × b × sin(C) = ½ × b × c × sin(A) = ½ × c × a × sin(B).

Area of triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height = 1/2 × 40 × 30 = 600 m².

Combined Area = 600 + 1000 = 1600 m².

Percentage = (600 ÷ 1600) × 100 = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 1600 m² and 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base of the triangle = 40 m

Height of the triangle = 30 m

Length of the rectangle = 40 m

Breadth of the rectangle = 25 m

**Formulas Used:**

Area of a Triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height

Area of a Rectangle = Length × Breadth

Percentage = (Part Value ÷ Total Value) × 100

 
 
• 40 m 25 m 30 m Area = 600 sq m Area = 1000 sq m 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of the triangle = 1/2 × 40 × 30

⇒ Area of the triangle = 20 × 30 = 600 m²

⇒ Area of the rectangle = 40 × 25 = 1000 m²

⇒ Total combined area = 600 + 1000 = 1600 m²

⇒ Percentage of the triangle's area in total area = (600 ÷ 1600) × 100

⇒ Percentage = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 1600 m² and 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of 2D Shapes

The area of a planar figure refers to the total space enclosed within its boundary. For standard polygons like triangles and rectangles, direct mathematical formulas are applied based on their distinct dimensions.

Types of Triangles Based on Area

For an equilateral triangle, area = (√3 ÷ 4) × side². For scalene triangles, Heron's formula is widely utilized: Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)], where s represents the semi-perimeter.

Percentages in Geometry

Comparing the region of two interlinked figures as a percentage effectively establishes proportional spatial distribution. It is calculated continuously by dividing the targeted subset area by the overall total area multiplied by 100.

question: The area of a regular triangle increases by 44%. By what percentage did the side length increase?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any 2D geometrical figure, Area ∝ (Side)².

Since the area increases by 44%, the new area becomes 144% of the original, which corresponds to a multiplying factor of 1.44.

The multiplying factor for the side length will be the square root of the area factor: √1.44 = 1.2.

A multiplier of 1.2 means the side length has increased by 0.2, which is exactly 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 Area = A Side = a 
 Area = 1.44A Side = 1.2a 
• 
 Area +44% Side +20% 

**Given:**

The area of a regular (equilateral) triangle increases by 44%.

**Formula Used:**

Area of an equilateral triangle = √3 ÷ 4 × a², where a is the side length.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial side length of the triangle be a.

⇒ Initial Area (A₁) = √3 ÷ 4 × a²

⇒ Final Area (A₂) = A₁ + 44% of A₁ = 1.44 × A₁

⇒ Let the final side length of the triangle be a'.

⇒ √3 ÷ 4 × (a')² = 1.44 × (√3 ÷ 4 × a²)

⇒ By cancelling out the common terms (√3 ÷ 4) on both sides:

⇒ (a')² = 1.44 × a²

⇒ Taking the square root on both sides:

⇒ a' = 1.2 × a

⇒ Increase in side length = a' − a = 1.2a − a = 0.2a

⇒ Percentage increase in side length = (0.2a ÷ a) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a 2D figure has its dimensions increased uniformly by x%, the total percentage change in its area is given by the formula: Area % Change = x + x + (x² ÷ 100). For x = 20%, Area Change = 20 + 20 + 400÷100 = 44%.

Area of Similar Figures

The ratio of the areas of any two similar regular geometric figures is directly proportional to the square of the ratio of their corresponding side lengths.

Properties of a Regular Triangle

A regular triangle is an equilateral triangle where all three sides are equal, all interior angles are 60°, and its height is determined by the formula: h = √3 ÷ 2 × side.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For congruent triangles ΔPQR ≅ ΔABC, the order of vertices directly dictates the corresponding parts.

Side PQ corresponds directly to side AB, so PQ = AB = 6 cm (thus QP = 6 cm).

Using the angle sum property in ΔABC, ∠C = 180º − (70º + 50º) = 60º.

Angle R corresponds directly to Angle C, so ∠R = 60º.

Matching our findings with the given options, we find that QP = 6 cm and ∠R = 60º is the only true statement.

**∴ The correct answer is QP = 6 cm, ∠R = 60º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ ΔPQR ≅ ΔABC

⇒ AB = 6 cm, ∠B = 50º and ∠A = 70º

**In ΔABC:**

⇒ The sum of interior angles in a triangle is exactly 180º

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180º

⇒ 70º + 50º + ∠C = 180º

⇒ 120º + ∠C = 180º

⇒ ∠C = 60º

**Using CPCTC (Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent):**

⇒ Since ΔPQR ≅ ΔABC, their corresponding sides and angles must be perfectly identical.

**Corresponding Sides:**

⇒ PQ = AB, QR = BC, and PR = AC

⇒ Since AB = 6 cm, we have PQ = 6 cm (or QP = 6 cm)

**Corresponding Angles:**

⇒ ∠P = ∠A = 70º

⇒ ∠Q = ∠B = 50º

⇒ ∠R = ∠C = 60º

**Checking the given options sequentially:**

⇒ Option 1: QR = 6 cm, ∠Q = 60º (Incorrect, QP = 6 cm and ∠Q = 50º)

⇒ Option 2: QR = 6 cm, ∠R = 60º (Incorrect, QP = 6 cm)

⇒ Option 3: QP = 6 cm, ∠P = 60º (Incorrect, ∠P = 70º)

⇒ Option 4: QP = 6 cm, ∠R = 60º (Correct)

**∴ The correct answer is QP = 6 cm, ∠R = 60º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Congruence of Triangles

Two triangles are strictly congruent if they share the exact same shape and size. The primary criteria for congruence are SSS (Side-Side-Side), SAS (Side-Angle-Side), ASA (Angle-Side-Angle), AAS (Angle-Angle-Side), and RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side).

CPCTC Rule

CPCTC stands for "Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent." It indicates that if two triangles are proven congruent, all of their corresponding interior angles and boundary sides are perfectly equal.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all three interior angles in any triangle inherently adds up to exactly 180º. Using the standard formula: ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180º.
</p

Midpoint Theorem

The line segment connecting the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is half as long as that third side.

The triangle formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of any triangle divides the original triangle into four smaller congruent triangles of exactly equal area.

Since D is the midpoint of BC, the hypotenuses BD and CD are equal.

The perpendiculars from D to sides AB and AC are also equal, so DL = DM.

In right-angled ΔBLD and ΔCMD, both the hypotenuses and one side are equal.

By RHS congruence, ΔBLD ≅ ΔCMD, which implies the base angles are equal (∠B = ∠C).

If two angles of a triangle are equal, the opposite sides are also equal (AB = AC).

**∴ The correct answer is isosceles triangle.**

In ΔABC, D is the mid-point of BC ⇒ BD = DC

DL ⊥ AB and DM ⊥ AC ⇒ ∠BLD = ∠CMD = 90°

Lengths of the perpendiculars are equal ⇒ DL = DM

**Proof:**

In right-angled ΔBLD and right-angled ΔCMD:

⇒ ∠BLD = ∠CMD = 90° (Given)

⇒ Hypotenuse BD = Hypotenuse DC (D is the mid-point of BC)

⇒ Side DL = Side DM (Given)

⇒ By RHS (Right angle - Hypotenuse - Side) congruence criterion, ΔBLD ≅ ΔCMD.

Therefore, the corresponding parts are equal:

⇒ ∠LBD = ∠MCD (CPCT)

⇒ ∠B = ∠C

In any triangle, the sides opposite to equal angles are always equal in length.

⇒ AB = AC

⇒ Since two sides of ΔABC are equal, it must be an isosceles triangle.

Two right-angled triangles are congruent if the hypotenuse and one side of one triangle are respectively equal to the hypotenuse and one side of the second triangle.

An isosceles triangle has at least two equal sides and two equal base angles. The median drawn to the unequal side always acts as the altitude and the angle bisector.

Equidistant Property of an Angle Bisector

Any point lying on the bisector of an angle is strictly equidistant from the arms of that angle. Here, D being equidistant from AB and AC implies AD bisects ∠A.

question: In a ∆PQR, PQ = PR and PT is perpendicular to QR. If PQ = 17 cm, PT = 15 cm, then what is the measure (in cm) of QR?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an isosceles triangle, the altitude drawn to the unequal side bisects the base.

This splits the triangle into two identical right-angled triangles.

Using the standard Pythagorean triplet (8, 15, 17), if the hypotenuse = 17 and perpendicular = 15, then the base (QT) = 8.

Since the altitude bisects the base, the total length of QR is twice the length of QT.

⇒ QR = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ In ΔPQR, PQ = PR = 17 cm.

⇒ PT ⊥ QR and PT = 15 cm.

 
 
• 
 P Q R T 17 cm 17 cm 15 cm x x 

**Concept Used:**

⇒ The altitude drawn from the vertex of an isosceles triangle to its base exactly bisects the base.

⇒ ∴ QT = TR = QR ÷ 2.

**Calculation:**

⇒ In right-angled ΔPQT, apply Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ PQ² = PT² + QT²

⇒ 17² = 15² + QT²

⇒ 289 = 225 + QT²

⇒ QT² = 289 − 225 = 64

⇒ QT = √64 = 8 cm.

⇒ Since QT is exactly half of the base QR:

⇒ QR = 2 × QT

⇒ QR = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Isosceles Triangles

In an isosceles triangle, the two angles opposite to the equal sides are also equal. Furthermore, the altitude drawn to the unequal side functions as an angle bisector and median simultaneously.

Pythagoras Theorem

Applicable only to right-angled triangles, it dictates that the square of the longest side (hypotenuse) equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a² + b² = c².

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Memorising frequent integer combinations dramatically reduces exam calculation time. Core examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25), and (9, 40, 41).

For a right-angled triangle, the lengths of the sides must form a valid Pythagorean triplet.

Standard Pythagorean triplets frequently asked in exams include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

According to the Pythagoras Theorem, for a triangle to be right-angled, the sum of the squares of the two smaller sides must be equal to the square of the longest side (hypotenuse):

a² + b² = c²

 

 
 Base = 12

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let's check Option 1: 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25. The square of the third side is 6² = 36. Since 25 ≠ 36, it is not a right-angled triangle.

⇒ Let's check Option 2: 8² + 15² = 64 + 225 = 289. The square of the third side is 16² = 256. Since 289 ≠ 256, it is not a right-angled triangle.

⇒ Let's check Option 3: 5² + 10² = 25 + 100 = 125. The square of the third side is 12² = 144. Since 125 ≠ 144, it is not a right-angled triangle.

⇒ Let's check Option 4: 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169. The square of the third side is 13² = 169. Since 169 = 169, it perfectly satisfies the theorem.

**∴ The correct answer is {5, 12, 13}.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is exactly equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Some basic integer triplets to memorize are (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25), and (9, 40, 41). Any constant multiple of these triplets (e.g., 6, 8, 10) also forms a right-angled triangle.

Identifying Triangle Types

If c is the longest side: If a² + b² > c², the triangle is an acute-angled triangle. If a² + b² < c², the triangle is an obtuse-angled triangle.

question: Which of the following are the angles of a scalene triangle?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

By definition, a scalene triangle is a triangle in which all three sides and all three interior angles are of completely different measures.

Checking the given options, only the set 60°, 30° and 90° consists of entirely distinct angles.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°, 30° and 90°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given Options:**

⇒ 1) 60°, 30° and 90°

⇒ 2) 60°, 60° and 60°

⇒ 3) 110°, 35° and 35°

⇒ 4) 90°, 45° and 45°

 Scalene Right Triangle (All angles distinct)

**Properties Used:**

⇒ In an equilateral triangle, all three angles are equal (each 60°).

⇒ In an isosceles triangle, exactly two angles are equal to each other.

⇒ In a scalene triangle, all three angles must be strictly unequal.

**Evaluating each option based on angle equality:**

⇒ Option 1: 60°, 30° and 90° → All three angles are different. Thus, it forms a scalene triangle.

⇒ Option 2: 60°, 60° and 60° → All three angles are the same. Thus, it forms an equilateral triangle.

⇒ Option 3: 110°, 35° and 35° → Two angles are the same (35°). Thus, it forms an isosceles triangle.

⇒ Option 4: 90°, 45° and 45° → Two angles are the same (45°). Thus, it forms an isosceles right triangle.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°, 30° and 90°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property

The total sum of the interior angles in any valid planar triangle is always exactly 180°.

Classification by Sides

Equilateral triangles have all equal sides, isosceles triangles have two equal sides, and scalene triangles possess entirely unequal side lengths.

Classification by Angles

An acute triangle has all interior angles measuring less than 90°. A right triangle has exactly one 90° angle, and an obtuse triangle features exactly one angle strictly greater than 90°.
</p

subject: MATH
question:
For triangles, which of the following statement(s) are true?

(a) Sum of interior angles is 180°.

(b) All interior angles can’t be equal.

(c) Can have at the most one obtuse angle.

(d) Sum of two sides may or may not be equal to the third side.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Evaluate each statement logically based on the geometric properties of a planar triangle.

(a) The sum of interior angles is exactly 180°, which is a universally fundamental property. (True)

(b) An equilateral triangle has three equal interior angles of 60° each. (False)

(c) A triangle can have at most one obtuse angle (>90°), else the sum exceeds 180°. (True)

(d) The triangle inequality theorem states the sum of two sides must be **strictly greater** than the third side. (False)

**∴ The correct answer is (a) and (c).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Four statements regarding the properties of a triangle.

 

 
 

 

 

 
 B
 C
 A

 c
 b
 a
 
 
 Properties:
 ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°
 a + b > c
 Max 1 obtuse ∠

**Analysis:**

⇒ **Statement (a):** By the Angle Sum Property of a triangle, the sum of all three interior angles is always equal to 180°. Hence, statement (a) is logically sound.

⇒ **Statement (b):** All interior angles of a triangle can indeed be identical. For example, in an equilateral triangle, all three angles measure exactly 60°. Hence, statement (b) is invalid.

⇒ **Statement (c):** If a triangle possessed two obtuse angles (both greater than 90°), their combined sum would be strictly greater than 180°, defying the core angle sum property. Thus, a triangle can possess at most one obtuse angle. Hence, statement (c) is logically sound.

⇒ **Statement (d):** The Triangle Inequality Theorem dictates that the sum of the lengths of any two sides of a triangle must always be strictly greater than the length of the third side. It can never be equal or less. Hence, statement (d) is invalid.

⇒ Conclusively, only statements (a) and (c) correctly describe the properties of a triangle.

**∴ The correct answer is (a) and (c).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Triangle Inequality Theorem

For any triangle possessing sides a, b, and c, the theorem declares: a + b > c, a + c > b, and b + c > a. Furthermore, the difference between any two sides is always strictly less than the length of the third side.

Exterior Angle Property

The scalar measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is mathematically equivalent to the sum of the measures of its two opposing (remote) interior angles.

Classification of Triangles (by Angles)

Acute (all interior angles are strictly less than 90°), Right (possesses exactly one 90° angle), and Obtuse (possesses exactly one interior angle strictly greater than 90°).
</p

subject: MATH
question: Six cubes, each of edge 2 cm, are joined end to end. What is the total surface area of the resulting cuboid in cm²?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

6 individual cubes have a total of 6 × 6 = 36 faces.

Joining them end-to-end forms 5 joints between the cubes.

Each joint hides 2 faces, leaving 36 − (5 × 2) = 26 visible faces.

Area of each square face = a² = 2² = 4 cm².

Total surface area = 26 × 4 = 104 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 104 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b22fa3ba086d4600a76ac177dfc2af9a6fa837447ad3d7088c74c115a0c7640.png] 

**Given:**

Number of cubes = 6

Edge of each cube (a) = 2 cm

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of a Cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

**Calculations:**

When 6 uniform cubes are joined end to end, a cuboid is formed where the length increases but breadth and height remain unchanged.

⇒ Length of the resulting cuboid (l) = 6 × 2 = 12 cm

⇒ Breadth of the resulting cuboid (b) = 2 cm

⇒ Height of the resulting cuboid (h) = 2 cm

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × (l × b + b × h + h × l)

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × (12 × 2 + 2 × 2 + 2 × 12)

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × (24 + 4 + 24)

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × 52 = 104 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 104 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cube

The total surface area of a single cube of edge length 'a' is given by 6a², as it is composed of 6 identical square faces.

Joining 'n' Cubes

When 'n' cubes of side 'a' are joined end-to-end, the resulting shape is a cuboid with length 'n × a', while the breadth and height remain 'a'.

Lateral Surface Area

The lateral (or curved) surface area of a cuboid excludes the top and bottom faces. It is given by the formula LSA = 2h(l + b).
</p

question: In a ΔABC, points P, Q and R are taken on AB, BC and CA, respectively, such that BQ = PQ and QC = QR. If ∠BAC = 75º, what is the measure of ∠PQR (in degrees)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/626ab74d9ea5000cf727fc54c65f1619ee6984d00c3e11ea54b5c299b076fd9c.png] 

∠BAC = 75º

∠ABC + ∠ACB + ∠BAC = 180°

∠ABC + ∠ACB + 75° = 180°

∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180° - 75° = 105°

Let, ∠ABC = ∠PBQ = 70° and ∠ACB = ∠RCQ = 35°

So, ∠PQR = 180° - (∠PQB + ∠RQC)

= 180° - [(180° - 2∠PBQ) + (180° - 2∠RCQ) [∵ BQ = PQ; QC = QR]

= 180° - [(180° - 2 × 70°) + (180° - 2 × 35°)]

= 180° - (40° + 110°)

= 180° - 150°

= 30°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In a ΔABC, ∠BAC = 75º

BQ = PQ and QC = QR

**Concept used:**

The sum of all three angles of a triangle = 180°

The sum of all angles on a straight line = 180°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/626ab74d9ea5000cf727fc54c65f1619ee6984d00c3e11ea54b5c299b076fd9c.png] 

Let, ∠ABC = x and ∠ACB = y

So, ∠ABC = ∠PBQ = ∠QPB = x [∵ BQ = PQ]

∠ACB = ∠RCQ = ∠QRC = y [QC = QR]

In ΔABC, ∠ABC + ∠ACB + ∠BAC = 180°

⇒ x + y + 75° = 180°

⇒ x + y = 180° - 75° = 105° .....(1)

For ΔBPQ and ΔCRQ,

(∠PBQ + ∠QPB + ∠PQB) + (∠RCQ + ∠QRC + ∠RQC) = 180° + 180° = 360°

⇒ (x + x + ∠PQB) + (y + y + ∠RQC) = 360°

⇒ 2x + 2y + ∠PQB + ∠RQC = 360°

⇒ 2 (x + y) + ∠PQB + ∠RQC = 360°

⇒ (2 × 105°) + ∠PQB + ∠RQC = 360° [∵ x + y = 105°]

⇒ ∠PQB + ∠RQC = 360° - 210° = 150° .....(2)

Also, ∠PQB + ∠RQC + ∠PQR = 180°

⇒ 150° + ∠PQR = 180° [∵ ∠PQB + ∠RQC = 150°]

⇒ ∠PQR = 180° - 150° = 30°

**∴ The measure of ∠PQR (in degrees) is 30°**

question: Sides AB and AC of ∆ ABC are produced to points D and E, respectively. The bisectors of ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at P. If ∠A = 78°, then the measure of ∠P is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Given, ∠A = 78°

If the bisectors of ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at P

∠P = 90° - ∠A/2

⇒ ∠P = 90° - 78°/2

⇒ ∠P = 90° - 39° = 51°

The sum of all angles on a straight line is 180°

∠ABC + ∠CBD = 180°

⇒ ∠CBD = 180° - ∠ABC

⇒ ∠CBD/2 = (180° - ∠ABC)/2

⇒ ∠CBP = 90° - ∠ABC/2 [∵ BP is the bisector of ∠CBD]

Similarly, ∠BCP = 90° - ∠ACB/2

In ΔBCP, ∠CBP + ∠BCP + ∠P = 180°

⇒ (90° - ∠ABC/2) + (90° - ∠ACB/2) + ∠P = 180°

⇒ 180° - (180° - ∠BAC)/2 + ∠P = 180°

⇒ ∠P = (180° - ∠BAC)/2

⇒ ∠P = (180° - 78°)/2

⇒ ∠P = (102°)/2 = 51°

**∴ The measure of ∠P is 51°**
