question: In an election between two candidates P and Q, P got 78% of the total valid votes. If the total votes of the electorate were 75,60,000, then what was the number of valid votes that Q got if 10% of the voters did not cast their vote and 15% of the votes polled were declared invalid?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Valid votes received by Q can be directly found using successive percentage multipliers.

Q's Valid Votes = Total Electorate × Polled % × Valid % × Q's Share %

⇒ Q's Valid Votes = 75,60,000 × 90% × 85% × (100% − 78%)

⇒ Q's Valid Votes = 75,60,000 × (9 ÷ 10) × (17 ÷ 20) × (11 ÷ 50)

⇒ Q's Valid Votes = 7560 × 9 × 17 × 11 = 12,72,348

**∴ The correct answer is 12,72,348.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b1650c0845c2b60993cb48dc3569602c70932596bbe7892f3d020e976721f31.png] 

**Given:**

Total votes of the electorate = 75,60,000

Percentage of voters who did not vote = 10%

Percentage of invalid votes = 15%

Percentage of valid votes secured by P = 78%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of votes polled = (100% − 10%) of 75,60,000

⇒ Number of votes polled = 90% of 75,60,000 = (90 ÷ 100) × 75,60,000 = 68,04,000

⇒ Number of valid votes = (100% − 15%) of 68,04,000

⇒ Number of valid votes = 85% of 68,04,000 = (85 ÷ 100) × 68,04,000 = 57,83,400

⇒ Since P got 78% of the valid votes, Q must have received the remaining valid votes.

⇒ Percentage of valid votes Q received = 100% − 78% = 22%

⇒ Number of valid votes Q got = 22% of 57,83,400

⇒ Number of valid votes Q got = (22 ÷ 100) × 57,83,400 = 12,72,348

**∴ The correct answer is 12,72,348.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Method

When a base value continuously undergoes percentage reductions or increments sequentially, the final value can be obtained via a single chain product: Base × (1 ± R₁/100) × (1 ± R₂/100).

Election Base Shifting

It is crucial to remember that the percentage of invalid votes is calculated strictly on the 'Polled Votes', not on the 'Total Electorate'. The base automatically changes after every reduction in real-time election distribution problems.
</p

question: In an election between R and S, R gets 110% of the votes of S and beats S by 770 votes. If there were no invalid votes, then the total number of votes polled is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of votes of R to S = 110 : 100 = 11 : 10.

Difference in ratio units = 11 − 10 = 1 unit.

Given winning margin = 1 unit = 770.

Total votes in ratio units = 11 + 10 = 21 units.

Total votes = 21 × 770 = 16170.

**∴ The correct answer is 16170.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Votes of R = 110% of votes of S.

R beats S by 770 votes.

There were no invalid votes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51ab76c4af838984db8340225b38ebc2f5ccc6d8c36e06c305ea13f349af1f0b.png] 

Let the number of votes received by S be 100x.

⇒ Votes received by R = 110% of 100x = 110x

⇒ Winning margin = Votes of R − Votes of S

⇒ 110x − 100x = 770

⇒ 10x = 770

⇒ x = 77

⇒ Total votes polled = Votes of R + Votes of S

⇒ Total votes polled = 110x + 100x = 210x

⇒ Total votes polled = 210 × 77 = 16170

**∴ The correct answer is 16170.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Base Change

It is essential to identify the base value properly. The phrase "110% of the votes of S" means S's votes act as the 100% base for this comparison.

Election Concepts

In a valid two-candidate election, total valid votes = votes of winner + votes of loser. The winning margin is always the difference between their respective vote counts or percentage values on the same base.
</p

question: Two candidates contested in an election. 80% of the voters cast their votes, out of which 5% of the polled votes were invalid. The winning candidate got 70% of valid votes and won by a majority of 36,480 votes. Find the total number of voters.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Majority = 70% − 30% = 40% of valid votes.

Total Voters × 80% × 95% × 40% = 36,480

Total Voters × (4/5) × (19/20) × (2/5) = 36,480

Total Voters × (152/500) = 36,480

Total Voters = 36,480 × (500 ÷ 152) = 1,20,000

**∴ The correct answer is 1,20,000 voters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Polled votes = 80% of total voters

Valid votes = 95% of polled votes

Winning candidate votes = 70% of valid votes

Majority = 36,480 votes

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0104a94791bc208969b79f345fe5b0434aae5fa0d7e023c6df7c37ea14337fd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total number of voters be 100x.

⇒ Polled votes = 80% of 100x = 80x

⇒ Valid votes = 95% of 80x = 76x

⇒ Winner's share = 70% of 76x

⇒ Loser's share = (100% − 70%) = 30% of 76x

⇒ Majority = Winner's share − Loser's share

⇒ Majority = (70% − 30%) = 40% of 76x

⇒ Majority = 0.40 × 76x = 30.4x

⇒ 30.4x = 36,480

⇒ x = 36,480 ÷ 30.4 = 1,200

⇒ Total voters = 100x = 100 × 1,200 = 1,20,000

**∴ The correct answer is 1,20,000 voters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Trick

When multiple percentage reductions occur consecutively (e.g., voters → polled → valid), the final value can be found by directly multiplying the base with their equivalent successive fractions: Final Value = Initial Base × (1 − r₁/100) × (1 − r₂/100).

Majority in Elections

The term "majority" exclusively represents the margin or the difference between the winning candidate's votes and the opposing candidate's votes. Majority % = (Winner % − Loser %) calculated out of valid votes only.

Valid vs Invalid Votes

Only the votes that are actively polled in the election can be considered for determining validity. Hence, Valid Votes = Polled Votes − Invalid Votes. Do not subtract invalid votes directly from the total voters list.
</p

question: In an election between two candidates, the one who gets 88% of the votes is elected by a majority of 684 votes. What is the total number of votes polled? (all polled votes are valid)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Winner's vote share = 88%

Loser's vote share = 100% − 88% = 12%

Majority (Difference) = 88% − 12% = 76%

76% of total votes = 684

Total votes = (684 ÷ 76) × 100 = 900

**∴ The correct answer is 900 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Winning candidate's vote share = 88%

Majority (difference in votes) = 684

**Formula Used:**

Total Votes = 100%

Losing Candidate % = 100% − Winning Candidate %

Majority = Winning % − Losing %

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e863f1d6c5980e18f16c4a54d4ef4bbb4cef8fa378d2aaa8e8aebb568c71d178.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total number of polled votes be x.

⇒ Votes secured by the winning candidate = 0.88x

⇒ Votes secured by the losing candidate = x − 0.88x = 0.12x

⇒ Difference in their votes (Majority) = 0.88x − 0.12x = 0.76x

⇒ According to the problem, the majority is 684 votes.

⇒ 0.76x = 684

⇒ x = 684 ÷ 0.76

⇒ x = (684 × 100) ÷ 76

⇒ x = 9 × 100

⇒ x = 900

**∴ The correct answer is 900 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Valid and Invalid Votes

If some votes are declared invalid, then Valid Votes = Total Votes − Invalid Votes. The percentages of the winner and loser are typically calculated based on valid votes, unless specified otherwise.

Multiple Candidates Election

When there are more than two candidates, the majority is calculated as the difference between the votes of the winner and the runner-up (the candidate with the second-highest votes).

Percentage Base Method

Finding the total quantity when a part is given is a direct application of base percentage. Total Value = Given Value ÷ Percentage Fraction.

question: A certain number of students from school X appeared in an examination and 20% students failed. From school Y, 130% more students than that from school X, appeared in the same examination. ⇒ 100x + 130x

⇒ 230x

⇒ 330x

⇒ (90/100 × 330)

⇒ 297x

So, number of passed students in school Y = (297x – 80x)

⇒ 217x

Number of failed students in school Y = (230x – 217x)

⇒ 13x

Percentage of failed students in school Y = (13x/230x) × 100

⇒ (1300x/230x)

⇒ 5.65% ~ 5.7%

**∴ The percentage of students who failed from school Y is 5.7%**

question: The income of A is 20% less than the income of B and the income of C is 70% of the sum of incomes of A and B. The income of D is 25% more than the income of C. If the difference between the incomes of B and D is Rs. 23000, then what is the income (in Rs.) of A?
solution:

Let Income of B = 100 units, then A = 80 units (20% less).

Income of C = 70% of (100 + 80) = 126 units.

Income of D = 125% of 126 = 157.5 units.

Difference (D − B) = 57.5 units → ₹23000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹400.

Income of A = 80 × 400 = ₹32000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹32000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Income of A = Income of B − 20% of Income of B

Income of C = 70% of (Income of A + Income of B)

Income of D = Income of C + 25% of Income of C

Difference between incomes of B and D = ₹23000

 
 A = 80x
 
 
 B = 100x

 
 C = 126x
 
 
 D = 157.5x
 
 
•

 Diff = 57.5x = ₹23000

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the income of B = 100x

⇒ Income of A = 100x − 20x = 80x

⇒ Income of C = 70% of (80x + 100x) = 126x

⇒ Income of D = 126x + 25% of 126x = 157.5x

⇒ Difference between D and B = 157.5x − 100x = 57.5x

⇒ 57.5x = 23000

⇒ x = 23000 ÷ 57.5

⇒ x = 400

⇒ Income of A = 80x = 80 × 400 = 32000

Ratio of Income: Expenditure: Savings = 45000: 33000: 12000 = 15: 11: 4

Using the weighted average method: Income = Expenditure + Savings

15 × 20% = 11 × 12% + 4 × x ⇒ 300% = 132% + 4x ⇒ 4x = 168% ⇒ x = 42%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Income = ₹45,000

Initial Expenditure = ₹33,000

Income is increased by 20% and Expenditure is increased by 12%.

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Percentage Increase = (Increase in Value ÷ Original Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a65412a82785a82ec15c9150c672853ca11c5292282400ba4b7b06e94055e4e2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ New Expenditure = ₹33,000 + (12% of ₹33,000) = ₹33,000 + ₹3,960 = ₹36,960

⇒ New Savings = New Income − New Expenditure

⇒ New Savings = ₹54,000 − ₹36,960 = ₹17,040

⇒ Increase in Savings = ₹17,040 − ₹12,000 = ₹5,040

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = (5,040 ÷ 12,000) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = 42%

**∴ The correct answer is 42%.**

Income is always the sum of Expenditure and Savings. Any absolute or percentage change in income naturally distributes across changes in both expenditure and savings.

When a base quantity is divided into two parts, the net percentage change in the total is mathematically equivalent to the weighted average of the percentage changes in its individual parts: I × I% = E × E% + S × S%.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100. A positive result directly indicates an increase, while a negative result indicates a decrease.

question: Kalyan spends 80% of his income. His income increases by 15% and his expenditure also increases by 5%. The percentage of increase in his savings is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Expenditure to Savings = 80% : 20% = 4 : 1.

We apply the weighted average method: Income = Expenditure + Savings.

Change in Income = (Exp Ratio × Exp Change + Sav Ratio × Sav Change) ÷ Total Ratio

⇒ 15% = (4 × 5% + 1 × x%) ÷ 5

⇒ 75% = 20% + x% ⇒ x = 55%

**∴ The correct answer is 55%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Kalyan spends 80% of his income.

Increase in income = 15%.

Increase in expenditure = 5%.

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Percentage Increase = (Increase Value ÷ Initial Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe676e11c7b5cc88f9a98caef9fe4134c499afdb29816b38ac73b3bde9d5d14f.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let initial income be 100 units.

⇒ Initial expenditure = 80% of 100 = 80 units

⇒ Initial savings = 100 − 80 = 20 units

⇒ After a 15% increase, new income = 100 + 15 = 115 units

⇒ After a 5% increase, new expenditure = 80 + (5% of 80) = 80 + 4 = 84 units

⇒ New savings = New income − New expenditure = 115 − 84 = 31 units

⇒ Increase in savings = 31 − 20 = 11 units

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = (11 ÷ 20) × 100 = 55%

**∴ The correct answer is 55%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure & Savings

The basic relationship is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any percentage change in income impacts both expenditure and savings proportional to their initial distributions.

Percentage Change Formula

The percentage change is always calculated on the base original value: % Change = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

Weighted Average (Alligation) Method

When a whole is divided into two parts in the ratio n₁ : n₂, the net percentage change can be calculated directly as: Net % = (n₁ × x₁ + n₂ × x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
</p

question: Ajay spends 66(2)/(3)% of his income on different household items. If his income increases by 25% and expenditure increase by 20%, then the effect on his savings will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since Expenditure is 66(2/3)% = 2/3 of Income, let Income = 3 units, Expenditure = 2 units, and Savings = 1 unit.

Using weighted average: (Exp Ratio × Exp % Change) + (Sav Ratio × Sav % Change) = (Inc Ratio × Inc % Change)

⇒ 2 × 20% + 1 × x = 3 × 25%

⇒ 40% + x = 75%

⇒ x = 35%

**∴ The correct answer is 35%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/291a8a2365031f33b1beb161cbabb47a483157230249e008c0dbac76fbcc0f23.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ Expenditure = 66(2/3)% of Income = 2/3 × Income

Let initial Income = 300

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 2/3 × 300 = 200

⇒ Initial Savings = Income − Expenditure = 300 − 200 = 100

⇒ New Income = 300 + (25/100 × 300) = 300 + 75 = 375

⇒ New Expenditure = 200 + (20/100 × 200) = 200 + 40 = 240

⇒ New Savings = New Income − New Expenditure = 375 − 240 = 135

⇒ Increase in Savings = 135 − 100 = 35

⇒ Percentage effect on Savings = (35 ÷ 100) × 100% = 35%

**∴ The correct answer is 35%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure & Savings Relationship

Income = Expenditure + Savings. The overall percentage change in income acts as the weighted average of the percentage changes in expenditure and savings.

Mixture & Alligation Approach

This problem type can also be effectively solved using the Alligation cross method on percentage changes, where Ratio of Expenditure to Savings = (Savings % Change − Income % Change) : (Income % Change − Expenditure % Change).

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = (Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value × 100%. A positive resulting value indicates an increase, while a negative value signifies a decrease.
</p

question: If an employee’s income is ₹72,000, the amount he spends is 40% higher than his savings. Therefore, his savings (in ₹) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Savings be 100%. Then Expenditure = 100% + 40% = 140%.

Ratio of Savings : Expenditure = 100 : 140 = 5 : 7

Total Income = Savings + Expenditure = 5 + 7 = 12 units.

Given 12 units = ₹72,000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹6,000

Savings = 5 units = 5 × 6,000 = ₹30,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹30000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Income = ₹72,000

Expenditure is 40% higher than Savings.

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d37ea8ba762f8302257f9eb26ff535a080884eae58f10676d7c0dbb912672675.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let his Savings be x.

⇒ Expenditure = x + (40% of x) = x + 0.4x = 1.4x

⇒ Total Income = x + 1.4x = 2.4x

⇒ According to the question, 2.4x = 72000

⇒ x = 72000 ÷ 2.4

⇒ x = 720000 ÷ 24

⇒ x = 30000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹30000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure & Savings

The fundamental equation of personal finance is: Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any total change in income is always equal to the sum of the changes in expenditure and savings.

Ratio Method for Percentages

When a value is P% higher than another, their ratio becomes (100 + P) : 100. This heavily simplifies calculations by avoiding decimals and allowing you to solve the question completely using proportional unit parts.

Base Value Identification

It is crucial to identify the correct base. Here, Expenditure is 40% higher than Savings, meaning Savings is the base (100%). Misinterpreting the base value is the most common error in percentage problems.

question: Vipul spends 30% of his monthly income on rent, 60% of the remaining on groceries, and 40% of the remaining on others. If he saves ₹ 7056 in a month, then how much (in ₹) does he spend on groceries?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Savings % = 100% × (100% − 30%) × (100% − 60%) × (100% − 40%)

⇒ Savings = 100% × 0.7 × 0.4 × 0.6 = 16.8%

Given 16.8% of Income = ₹ 7056 ⇒ 1% = 7056 ÷ 16.8 = ₹ 420

Grocery % = 60% of the first remaining (70%) = 42%

Amount spent on groceries = 42% × 420 = ₹ 17640

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 17640.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rent spend = 30% of Income

Grocery spend = 60% of remaining

Other spend = 40% of remaining

Savings = ₹ 7056

**Formula Used:**

Remaining Amount = Initial Amount × (100 − Spend %)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/65f57dd1d7d0a48e437bdaa5f2d5b96ba0f53da5fbdd48db1391cbe5dbdc0e17.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total monthly income be x.

⇒ Amount left after paying rent = x − 0.30x = 0.70x

⇒ Amount spent on groceries = 60% of 0.70x = 0.42x

⇒ Amount left after grocery spend = 0.70x − 0.42x = 0.28x

⇒ Amount spent on others = 40% of 0.28x = 0.112x

⇒ Final Savings = 0.28x − 0.112x = 0.168x

⇒ 0.168x = 7056

⇒ x = 7056 ÷ 0.168 = ₹ 42000

⇒ Amount spent on groceries = 0.42 × 42000 = ₹ 17640

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 17640.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Model

When a base value is continuously reduced by varying percentages, the final value is calculated as: Final = Base × (1 − R₁/100) × (1 − R₂/100)...

Multiplier Fraction Method

Instead of decimals, use fractions: 30% = 3/10 (remaining 7/10), 60% = 3/5 (remaining 2/5), 40% = 2/5 (remaining 3/5). Total remaining fraction = 7/10 × 2/5 × 3/5 = 42/250 = 16.8%.

Reverse Calculation

To find initial income from final savings directly, divide the savings successively by the remaining percentage factors: Base = Savings ÷ [ (1 − p₁) × (1 − p₂) ... ]

question: The income of a person is ₹16,500, and his expenditure is ₹12,000. Next year, his income increases by 24% but his expenditure decreases by 10%. The percentage increase (rounded off to the nearest integer) in his savings is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Initial Income : Expenditure : Savings = 16500 : 12000 : 4500 ⇒ 11 : 8 : 3.

Using the weighted average method: (Total Ratio × Income Change) = (E_ratio × Expenditure Change) + (S_ratio × Savings Change)

11 × 24 = 8 × (−10) + 3 × x

264 = −80 + 3x ⇒ 3x = 344 ⇒ x = 114.66%

Rounding off to the nearest integer, we get 115%.

**∴ The correct answer is 115%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c58b02376947e16396d72f5528fc17a52ea5e31ef6680ebc350a57c19459fdfd.png] 

**Given:**

Initial Income = ₹16,500

Initial Expenditure = ₹12,000

⇒ Initial Savings = Income − Expenditure = 16,500 − 12,000 = ₹4,500

**Calculations:**

⇒ New Income = 16,500 + (24% of 16,500) = 16,500 × 1.24 = ₹20,460

⇒ New Expenditure = 12,000 − (10% of 12,000) = 12,000 × 0.90 = ₹10,800

⇒ New Savings = New Income − New Expenditure = 20,460 − 10,800 = ₹9,660

⇒ Increase in Savings = 9,660 − 4,500 = ₹5,160

⇒ Percentage Increase = (Increase ÷ Initial Savings) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = (5,160 ÷ 4,500) × 100 = 114.66%

⇒ Percentage Increase ≈ 115% (rounded off to the nearest integer)

**∴ The correct answer is 115%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure, and Savings Relationship

Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any absolute change in income is exactly equal to the sum of absolute changes in expenditure and savings.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100. A positive value represents a growth/increase while a negative value signifies a reduction.

Weighted Average Method for Change

If an entity is divided into two parts, the overall percentage change is the weighted average of the changes of its parts: Total % Change = (R₁ × C₁ + R₂ × C₂) ÷ (R₁ + R₂), where R represents the ratio and C represents the percentage change.

question: The salaries of P and Q together amount to ₹9,60,000. P and Q save 64% and 44%, respectively of their individual salaries. If P's expenditure is 1.5 times Q's expenditure, then what is the ratio of P's salary to Q's salary?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

P's expenditure % = 100% − 64% = 36%

Q's expenditure % = 100% − 44% = 56%

Given, P's expenditure = 1.5 × Q's expenditure

⇒ 36% of P = 1.5 × 56% of Q

⇒ P / Q = (1.5 × 56) / 36 = 84 / 36 = 7 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is 7 : 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Total Salary of P and Q = ₹9,60,000

⇒ Savings of P = 64% of P's Salary

⇒ Savings of Q = 44% of Q's Salary

⇒ Expenditure of P = 1.5 × Expenditure of Q

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0ef7390ae1a6bf48647532e64a6cff557290ed844b17838d36c1faa425870727.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Expenditure of P = (100 − 64)% of P's Salary = 36% of P's Salary

⇒ Expenditure of Q = (100 − 44)% of Q's Salary = 56% of Q's Salary

⇒ According to the given condition, 36% of P's Salary = 1.5 × 56% of Q's Salary

⇒ (36 / 100) × P = 1.5 × (56 / 100) × Q

⇒ 36 × P = 84 × Q

⇒ P / Q = 84 / 36

⇒ P / Q = 7 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is 7 : 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure and Savings

Total Income is the sum of total expenditure and total savings: Income = Expenditure + Savings.

Redundant Data Trick

When calculating ratios or percentage relationships, exact values (such as the combined sum of ₹9,60,000) are often unnecessary and skipping them saves valuable time.

Ratio Scaling Rule

If a × A = b × B, then A : B = b : a. This cross-multiplication principle quickly converts algebraic equations into straightforward ratios by swapping the coefficients.
</p

question: The ratio of expenditure to savings of a woman is 4 : 1. If her income and expenditure are increased by 20% and 10%, respectively, then find the percentage change in her savings.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the weighted average / net deviation method:

Overall % change = [(Exp Ratio × Exp % Change) + (Sav Ratio × Sav % Change)] ÷ Total Ratio

20% = [(4 × 10%) + (1 × x%)] ÷ (4 + 1)

100% = 40% + x% ⇒ x = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of Expenditure : Savings = 4 : 1

Increase in Income = 20%

Increase in Expenditure = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage Change = [(New Value − Original Value) ÷ Original Value] × 100%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/33478e6c9d04cbe5e194a5f6671cef71a53303abac6cb414c8bcec495f713541.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the savings be 100 units.

⇒ Then, expenditure = 4 × 100 = 400 units.

⇒ Initial Income = 400 + 100 = 500 units.

⇒ New Income = 500 + (20% of 500) = 500 + 100 = 600 units.

⇒ New Expenditure = 400 + (10% of 400) = 400 + 40 = 440 units.

⇒ New Savings = New Income − New Expenditure

⇒ New Savings = 600 − 440 = 160 units.

⇒ Increase in savings = 160 − 100 = 60 units.

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = (60 ÷ 100) × 100% = 60%.

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income and Expenditure relation

Income is always the sum of expenditure and savings (I = E + S). Any change in income must be balanced by combined changes in expenditure and savings.

Weighted Average Method

When a quantity is divided into parts, the overall percentage change is the weighted average of the percentage changes of its parts: Overall % = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂).

Alligation Method

The rule of alligation can also be applied to find the ratio of parts or the change in one part if the overall change and the change in the other part are known.
</p

question: The monthly income of Ramesh in year 2021 was ₹18,600 and his monthly expenditure was ₹12,400. In year 2022 his income increased by 15% and his expenditure increased by 8%. Find the percentage increase in his savings.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Initial Income : Expenditure : Savings = 18600 : 12400 : 6200 = 3 : 2 : 1.

We know, Income = Expenditure + Savings ⇒ 3 = 2 + 1.

Applying the net percentage change equation (Weighted Average):

⇒ 3 × 15% = (2 × 8%) + (1 × x%)

⇒ 45% = 16% + x% ⇒ x = 29%

**∴ The correct answer is 29%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Income = ₹18,600

Initial Expenditure = ₹12,400

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Percentage Increase = (Increase ÷ Original Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/537457c31e5d93f3e838f59cc55621485e7e81a524453a5b696effc323d59163.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Savings = ₹18,600 − ₹12,400 = ₹6,200

⇒ New Income = ₹18,600 × (100 + 15)% = ₹18,600 × 1.15 = ₹21,390

⇒ New Expenditure = ₹12,400 × (100 + 8)% = ₹12,400 × 1.08 = ₹13,392

⇒ New Savings = ₹21,390 − ₹13,392 = ₹7,998

⇒ Increase in Savings = ₹7,998 − ₹6,200 = ₹1,798

⇒ Percentage increase in Savings = (1,798 ÷ 6,200) × 100 = 29%

**∴ The correct answer is 29%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure & Savings Relation

Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any percentage change in income is strictly distributed between expenditure and savings based on their proportional weightage.

Weighted Average Method

When a quantity is divided into two parts in the ratio a : b, and the parts change by x% and y%, the net percentage change is given by (ax + by) ÷ (a + b).

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100.

question: Suresh's expenditure and savings are in the ratio of 3 : 1. His income increases by 25%. If his savings increase by 20%, then by how much percentage does his expenditure increase?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Given E : S = 3 : 1 ⇒ Income (I) = 3 + 1 = 4 parts

Using the weighted average equation: E × Eᵢₙ꜀ + S × Sᵢₙ꜀ = I × Iᵢₙ꜀

⇒ 3 × Eᵢₙ꜀ + 1 × 20% = 4 × 25%

⇒ 3 × Eᵢₙ꜀ + 20 = 100 ⇒ 3 × Eᵢₙ꜀ = 80 ⇒ Eᵢₙ꜀ = 80/3% = 26 (2/3)%

**∴ The correct answer is 26 (2/3)%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of expenditure to savings = 3 : 1

Increase in income = 25%

Increase in savings = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage Increase = (Increase ÷ Original Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e79038c2174e0d9807d2e2d5ec9b6d6bc8c7bef0fdd6303e1084aae81ad1a63.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let original expenditure be 300 and original savings be 100.

⇒ Original Income = 300 + 100 = 400

⇒ New Income = 400 + (25% of 400) = 400 + 100 = 500

⇒ New Savings = 100 + (20% of 100) = 100 + 20 = 120

⇒ New Expenditure = New Income − New Savings

⇒ New Expenditure = 500 − 120 = 380

⇒ Increase in Expenditure = 380 − 300 = 80

⇒ Percentage increase in Expenditure = (80 ÷ 300) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = 80/3 = 26 (2/3)%

**∴ The correct answer is 26 (2/3)%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure & Savings Rule

Income is the sum of expenditure and savings (I = E + S). Any percentage change in income is distributed between expenditure and savings based on their respective proportional weights.

Weighted Average Method

When a value is split into two parts, the net percentage change can be determined using: Total % Change = (Part1 × %Change1 + Part2 × %Change2) ÷ (Part1 + Part2). This method offers the fastest way to solve mixture and distribution type percentage problems.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100. Always make sure to use the original or old value as the base denominator.
</p

⇒ Annual Net Return = 9% of ₹8,00,000

⇒ Annual Net Return = (9 ÷ 100) × 8,00,000 = ₹72,000

⇒ Monthly Net Return = 72,000 ÷ 12 = ₹6,000

⇒ Total Monthly Rent = Monthly Net Return + Monthly Maintenance

⇒ Total Monthly Rent = 6,000 + 2,000 = ₹8,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,000.**

ROI is a financial metric used to evaluate the profitability of an investment. It is calculated as the ratio of net profit to the initial investment cost, often expressed as an annual percentage.

Gross vs Net Income

Gross income refers to the total revenue generated (e.g., total rent collected), while net income is the profit remaining after deducting all operating expenses such as maintenance and taxes.

When cash flows or returns are uniform throughout the year, a monthly equivalent is obtained by simply dividing the annual expected value by 12. Monthly Return = Annual Return ÷ 12.

question: P and Q are two fixed points 10 cm apart, and R is a point on PQ such that PR = 6 cm. By what percentage is the length of QR decreased when the length of PR is increased by 5%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the total length PQ is fixed at 10 cm, the absolute increase in PR will exactly equal the absolute decrease in QR.

Increase in PR = 5% of 6 cm = 0.3 cm, so QR decreases by exactly 0.3 cm.

Initial length of QR = 10 − 6 = 4 cm.

Percentage decrease in QR = (0.3 ÷ 4) × 100 = 7.5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total length PQ = 10 cm

Initial length PR = 6 cm

Percentage increase in PR = 5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1eb9e62948b42f6e0325a8cb26ef13425202ec3217e8debb48cb2a23297b7c5e.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Percentage Decrease = (Decrease in Value ÷ Initial Value) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial length of QR = PQ − PR = 10 − 6 = 4 cm.

⇒ PR is increased by 5%, so New PR = 6 + (5% of 6) = 6 + 0.3 = 6.3 cm.

⇒ Since PQ is fixed at 10 cm, New QR = PQ − New PR = 10 − 6.3 = 3.7 cm.

⇒ Decrease in QR = Initial QR − New QR = 4 − 3.7 = 0.3 cm.

⇒ Percentage decrease in QR = (0.3 ÷ 4) × 100 = 7.5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

Always calculate the percentage increase or decrease using the original (initial) base value: % Change = (Change ÷ Initial Value) × 100.

Constant Sum Property

When the sum of two components is strictly constant (such as segments of a fixed line), any absolute positive variation in one component precisely matches the absolute negative variation in the other.

Base Value Importance

Although the absolute change (0.3 cm) is identical for both segments PR and QR, their percentage changes differ (5% vs 7.5%) due to their different starting base values (6 cm and 4 cm).
</p

Volume depends on three dimensions: Length, Breadth, and Height.

 B

 +10%
 in L, B, H

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial dimensions be L, B, and H.

⇒ Initial Volume (V₁) = L × B × H

⇒ After a 10% increase, the new dimensions are 1.1L, 1.1B, and 1.1H.

⇒ New Volume (V₂) = 1.1L × 1.1B × 1.1H

Successive Percentage Change Formula

When a value is changed by x% and then y%, the net percentage change is calculated as x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100. For three successive changes, apply the formula step-by-step.

question: A spherical balloon is inflated, causing its radius to grow by 10%. By what percentage does its surface area increase?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The surface area of a sphere is proportional to the square of its radius (r²).

When a dimension increases by x%, the percentage increase in area is found using the successive percentage formula: x + x + (x × x) ÷ 100

Given the increase in radius, x = 10%

Percentage increase in surface area = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10) ÷ 100 = 20 + 1 = 21%

**∴ The correct answer is 21%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in the radius of the spherical balloon = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Surface Area of a sphere = 4πr²

 
• r Initial Area = 4πr² 
• 1.1r New Area = 1.21 × 4πr² 
• 
 +10% Radius Surface Area Increase = 21% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial radius of the sphere be r.

⇒ Initial Surface Area (A₁) = 4πr²

⇒ New radius after 10% increase = r + (10 ÷ 100)r = 1.1r

⇒ New Surface Area (A₂) = 4π(1.1r)²

⇒ A₂ = 4π(1.21r²) = 1.21(4πr²)

⇒ Increase in Area = A₂ − A₁ = 1.21(4πr²) − 1(4πr²) = 0.21(4πr²)

⇒ Percentage increase = (Increase in Area ÷ Initial Area) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = [0.21(4πr²) ÷ 4πr²] × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = 0.21 × 100 = 21%

**∴ The correct answer is 21%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Percentage Change

Since the volume of a sphere depends on the cube of its radius (r³), the percentage change in volume is calculated by applying the percentage change successively three times, or by evaluating [(1 + x/100)³ − 1] × 100.

Successive Percentage Formula

For two consecutive changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by (a + b + ab ÷ 100)%. This is particularly useful for 2D mensuration problems involving area.

1D Dimension Change

Any one-dimensional measurement like circumference, diameter, or perimeter changes by the exact same percentage as the radius. Therefore, a 10% increase in radius will yield exactly a 10% increase in the circumference.

question: A town has males and females in a ratio of 3:2. After 5 years, the male population increases by 10%, and the female population by 25%. What is the new ratio?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial population of males and females be 300 and 200 respectively (to maintain the 3:2 ratio).

New male population = 300 × 110% = 330

New female population = 200 × 125% = 250

New ratio = 330 : 250 = 33 : 25

**∴ The correct answer is 33:25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial ratio of males to females = 3 : 2

Increase in male population = 10%

Increase in female population = 25%

 
 Initial Base (300 : 200) Final Population Male: 300 
 +10% Male: 330 Fem: 200 
 +25% Fem: 250 
• Final Ratio → 330 : 250 = 33 : 25 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the number of males = 3x and females = 2x.

⇒ New male population = 3x × (100% + 10%) = 3x × 1.10 = 3.3x

⇒ New female population = 2x × (100% + 25%) = 2x × 1.25 = 2.5x

⇒ New Ratio = 3.3x : 2.5x

⇒ Multiply both terms by 10 to remove decimals ⇒ 33x : 25x = 33 : 25

**∴ The correct answer is 33:25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase

When a value increases by R%, the new value is obtained directly by multiplying the original value by (100 + R)/100.

Properties of Ratio

A ratio remains unchanged when both its antecedent (first term) and consequent (second term) are multiplied or divided by the same non-zero number.

Base Assumption Technique

In ratio and percentage problems, assuming base values as multiples of 100 (e.g., 300 and 200 for a 3:2 ratio) perfectly avoids fractional calculations and speeds up the entire solution.

question: Every month, a man consumes 20 kg of rice and 8 kg of wheat. The price of rice is 20% of the price of wheat, resulting in a total expenditure of ₹300 per month for rice and wheat combined. If the price of wheat is increased by 20%, what percentage reduction in rice consumption is needed to maintain the same expenditure of ₹300? (Given that price of rice and consumption of wheat is constant.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Price ratio of Rice to Wheat = 20% = 1 : 5.

Expenditure ratio (Rice : Wheat) = (20 × 1) : (8 × 5) = 20 : 40 = 1 : 2.

Wheat expenditure increases by 20%, so extra cost = 20% of 2 units = 0.4 units.

To keep total expenditure constant, rice expenditure must decrease by 0.4 units.

Since rice price is constant, % reduction in consumption = (0.4 ÷ 1) × 100 = 40%.

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total expenditure = ₹300

Initial consumption of rice (Cᵣ) = 20 kg

Initial consumption of wheat (Cw) = 8 kg

Price of rice (Pᵣ) = 20% of Price of wheat (Pw) ⇒ Pw = 5 × Pᵣ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b2dce248bf23b0465e3954c1af064ed3c6e8e9d7896de5f01d9282c3d837f39.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total expenditure = (Cᵣ × Pᵣ) + (Cw × Pw) = 300

⇒ (20 × Pᵣ) + (8 × 5 Pᵣ) = 300

⇒ 20 Pᵣ + 40 Pᵣ = 300

⇒ 60 Pᵣ = 300 ⇒ Pᵣ = ₹5/kg

⇒ Pw = 5 × 5 = ₹25/kg

Initial expenditures:

⇒ Wheat expenditure = 8 × 25 = ₹200

⇒ Rice expenditure = 20 × 5 = ₹100

New conditions:

⇒ Price of wheat increases by 20%

⇒ New price of wheat = 25 × 1.20 = ₹30/kg

⇒ New wheat expenditure = 8 × 30 = ₹240

⇒ New rice expenditure = 300 − 240 = ₹60 (Since total is constant at ₹300)

⇒ New rice consumption = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 kg (Since Pᵣ is constant at ₹5/kg)

Percentage reduction in rice consumption:

⇒ Reduction = 20 − 12 = 8 kg

⇒ Percentage reduction = (8 ÷ 20) × 100 = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Expenditure Formula

Total Expenditure = Price × Consumption. If expenditure is constant, price and consumption are inversely proportional.

Percentage Increase / Decrease

Percentage Change = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100. It is always calculated on the base or original value.

Constant Total Expenditure with Multiple Items

If Total Expenditure = Exp₁ + Exp₂ is constant, any absolute increase in Exp₁ must be exactly balanced by an equal absolute decrease in Exp₂.

question: The cost of tomatoes per kg is increased by 300%. A housewife reduces her consumption of tomatoes by 70%. By what percentage does her expenditure on tomatoes increase or decrease?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The net percentage change in expenditure can be found using the successive percentage formula: x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100

Here, the price increases by 300% (x = +300) and consumption decreases by 70% (y = −70).

Net change = 300 − 70 + [300 × (−70)] ÷ 100

Net change = 230 − 210 = +20%

Since the result is positive, the expenditure increases by 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is Increases, 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage increase in price = 300%

Percentage decrease in consumption = 70%

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2f710747a78f0a27df2b475103284d95ebd6ee56c73d54b8c2e0bf012f211d4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial price of tomatoes be ₹100 per kg and the initial consumption be 10 kg.

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 100 × 10 = ₹1000

⇒ New price after 300% increase = 100 + (300 ÷ 100) × 100 = ₹400 per kg

⇒ New consumption after 70% decrease = 10 − (70 ÷ 100) × 10 = 3 kg

⇒ New Expenditure = 400 × 3 = ₹1200

⇒ Change in Expenditure = 1200 − 1000 = ₹200 (Increase)

⇒ Percentage Increase = (200 ÷ 1000) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is Increases, 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a quantity is successively changed by x% and y%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100. Use positive values for an increase and negative values for a decrease.

Price, Consumption, and Expenditure Relation

The foundational rule is Expenditure = Price × Consumption. If expenditure needs to remain constant while the price increases, consumption must be decreased proportionately.

Fraction Equivalent Method

For compound percentage calculations, converting percentages to fractional multipliers simplifies multiplication. For example, a 300% increase means multiplying the base value by 4, and a 70% decrease means multiplying the base value by 3/10.

question: A reduction of 20% in the price of bananas enables a customer to buy 6 more bananas for ₹80. What is the reduced price of bananas per dozen (in ₹)?
solution:
**Given:**

A reduction of 20% in the price of bananas enables a customer to buy 6 more bananas for ₹80

**Calculation:**

Let the C.P of each banana be x

Total number of bananas in ₹ 80 = 80/x

New price = x – x × (20/100)

⇒ (100 - 20)x/100

⇒ 80x/100 or 4x/5

New number of bananas in ₹80 = 80/(4x/5)

⇒ 80/(4x/5)

⇒ 100/x

⇒ (100/x) – (80/x) = 6 

⇒ 20/x = 6 

⇒ x = 20/6

New price of bananas = 20/6 × 4/5

⇒ 8/3

The reduced price of bananas per dozen = (8/3) × 12

⇒ 32

**∴ The reduced price of bananas per dozen (in ₹) is 32.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ **

Let the original price of a banana be 5x, new price will be 4x(reduced by 20%)

Now, according to the question,

⇒ 80over 4x - 80over 5x = 6

⇒ {80 (5 - 4)}over 4 times 5 times x = 6

⇒ {80 (5 - 4)}over 20 times x = 6

⇒ 4over x = 6

⇒ x = 2over3

The new price of bananas is,

⇒ 4x = 4 ×2over3

The price per dozen is

⇒ 4 × 2over3 × 12 = 32

Ratio and Proportion Basics

A ratio indicates how many times one number contains another. The ratio of x to y is mathematically represented as x : y or x ÷ y.

question: Rajan spent 10% of his salary on rent. He spent 20% of the remaining part of the salary on transport. After which he spent 40% of the balance of the salary on food. Further, he spent 80% of the balance on various bills. He deposits Rs. 5000 in the bank and kept the remaining Rs. 1480 for his own petty expenditure. Find his monthly salary (in Rs.)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Let the total salary of Rajan be Rs. x.

Total saving of Rajan = 1480 + 5000 = Rs. 6480

Now,

x × (100 - 10/100) × (100 - 20)/100 × (100 - 40)/100 × (100 - 80)/100 = 6480

⇒ x × (90/100) × (80/100) × (60/100) × (20/100) = 6480

⇒ x × 0.0864 = 6480

⇒ x = 64800000/864

⇒ x = Rs. 75000

**Traditional method:**

**Given:**

Salary spent on rent = 10%

Salary spent on transport of the balance = 20%

Salary spent on food of the balance = 40%

Salary spent on various bills of the balance = 80%

Money deposited in bank = Rs. 5000

Money kept for his own petty expenditure = Rs. 1480

**Calculation:**

Let total salary be Rs. 100x

Salary spent on rent = 10% of Rs. 100x

⇒ (100x × 10/100)

⇒ 10x

Remaining salary spent on transport = 20% of 90x

⇒ (20/100 × 90x)

⇒ 18x

Remaining salary spent on food = 40% of 72x

⇒ (40/100 × 72x)

⇒ 28.8x

Remaining salary spent on various bills = 80% of 43.2x

⇒ (80/100 × 43.2x)

⇒ 34.56x

Remaining salary = 100x – (10 + 18 + 28.8 + 34.56)x

⇒ (100 – 91.36)x

⇒ 8.64x

Money deposited in the bank and saved for his own petty expenditure = Rs. (5000 + 1480)

⇒ Rs. 6480

Now, as per the question,

⇒ 8.64x = Rs. 6480

⇒ 100x = (6480/8.64 × 100)

⇒ Rs. 75,000

**∴ His monthly salary is Rs. 75,000**

question: A fruit seller sells 45% of the oranges that he has along with one more orange to a customer. He then sells 20% of the remaining oranges and 2 more oranges to a second customer. He then sells 90% of the now remaining oranges to a third customer and is still left with 5 oranges. How many oranges did the fruit seller have initially?
solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the initial oranges with the fruit seller be x.

1st selling = 0.45x + 1

Remaining = x - (0.45x + 1) = 0.55x - 1

2nd selling = 1over 5 × (0.55x - 1) = 0.11x - 0.2 + 2 = 0.11x + 1.8

Remaining after second selling = 0.55x - 1 - (0.11x + 1.8) = 0.55x - 0.11x - 1 - 1.8 = 0.44x - 2.8

3rd selling = 90% × (0.44x - 2.8)

Remaining after 3rd selling = 0.1 × (0.44x - 2.8) = 0.044x - 0.28

According to the question-

⇒ 0.044x - 0.28 = 5

⇒ 0.044x = 5.28

⇒ x = 5.28over 0.044 = 120

∴ **The number of oranges was 120. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

At last, he sells 90% of the remaining oranges after selling the oranges to a second customer, then he has 10% of the remaining oranges.

10% of the remaining oranges after selling the oranges to the second customer = 5

So remaining oranges after selling the oranges to the second customer = 100% of the remaining oranges after selling the oranges to the second customer = 50 oranges

He gave 2 extra oranges to the second customer, so the remaining oranges = 50 + 2

He sells 20% of the remaining oranges to the second customer, so he has 80% of the remaining oranges = 52

100% of remaining oranges after selling the oranges to the first customer = (52/4) * 5 = 65 oranges

He gave 1 extra orange to the first customer, so the total oranges after selling 45% of the oranges = 65 + 1 = 66 oranges

(100% - 45% = 55%) of total oranges = 66

so

100% of oranges = (66/55) * 100 = 120 oranges

question: The price of an item is increased twice successively. The final price is ₹2,295 and initial price was ₹1,000. The percentage increment the second time was twice the percentage increment the first time. By what percentage was the price increased the second time?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total percentage increase = ((2295 − 1000) ÷ 1000) × 100 = 129.5%

By checking the given options, if the second increment is 70% (Option 3), then the first increment is 35%.

Applying the successive percentage formula: 35% + 70% + (35 × 70) ÷ 100 = 105% + 24.5% = 129.5%

This matches our calculated total increase perfectly, confirming that the second increase is indeed 70%.

**∴ The correct answer is 70%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Price = ₹1000

Final Price = ₹2295

**Formula Used:**

Effective Percentage Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a4abcc9973131f8a3e3c76c8bc6865cc9472150abcb856c9851bcb7355ea641.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total percentage increase = ((2295 − 1000) ÷ 1000) × 100 = 129.5%

⇒ Let the first percentage increase be x% and the second percentage increase be 2x%.

⇒ Using the successive percentage change formula: x + 2x + (x × 2x) ÷ 100 = 129.5

⇒ 3x + x² ÷ 50 = 129.5

⇒ Multiplying the entire equation by 50 to eliminate the fraction:

⇒ 150x + x² = 6475

⇒ x² + 150x − 6475 = 0

⇒ x² + 185x − 35x − 6475 = 0

⇒ x(x + 185) − 35(x + 185) = 0

⇒ (x − 35)(x + 185) = 0

⇒ Since a percentage increment must be positive, x = 35%

⇒ Therefore, the second increment is 2x = 2 × 35% = 70%

**∴ The correct answer is 70%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the net effective change is given by the formula: Effective % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100. This is useful for saving steps instead of calculating intermediate values.

Multiplier Method

For successive increases, the final value can be directly calculated by multiplying the base value with respective multiplying factors: Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + a ÷ 100) × (1 + b ÷ 100).

Absolute Percentage Change

No matter how many intermediate changes occur, the total net percentage change over a period can always be found using the starting and ending amounts: % Change = ((Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value) × 100.

question: A vendor sells shirts at ₹500 each, earning a 2% commission, and ties at ₹150 each, with a 12% commission. If he sells 3 shirts and 4 ties per day, what will be his total commission earned in 30 days?
solution:

Daily commission from shirts = 3 × (2% of 500) = 3 × 10 = ₹30

Daily commission from ties = 4 × (12% of 150) = 4 × 18 = ₹72

Total daily commission = 30 + 72 = ₹102

Total commission earned in 30 days = 102 × 30 = ₹3060

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3060.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Price of a tie = ₹150, Commission on a tie = 12%

Items sold per day = 3 shirts and 4 ties

Total days = 30

 Ties
 Price: ₹150 | Comm: 12%
 Comm/item: ₹18

 Total in 30 Days = ₹3060

Percentage Application

Percentage implies 'out of 100'. Thus, x% of y is calculated as (x ÷ 100) × y. In practical applications like commissions, discounts, or taxes, the percentage is applied directly to the base value.

Commission and Base Amount

Commission is generally paid as a percentage of the total sales value. If multiple items are sold with varying commission rates, they must be calculated individually before summation.

Unitary Method

Finding the value for a single unit and then multiplying it by the total number of units required is called the unitary method. It is highly effective for scaling daily quantities to monthly or annual values.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Current Population = P × (1 + R/100)T

 Past (P) Year 1 58,320

 + 8% + 8% Population Growth over 2 Years P × 1.08 × 1.08 = 58,320 

**Calculations:**

Let the population 2 years ago be P.

⇒ 58320 = P × (1 + 8/100)²

⇒ 58320 = P × (108/100)²

⇒ 58320 = P × (27/25)²

⇒ 58320 = P × (729/625)

⇒ P = 58320 × (625/729)

⇒ P = 80 × 625

Rate of depreciation for 1st year (R₁) = 10%

Rate of depreciation for 2nd year (R₂) = 20%

Rate of depreciation for 3rd year (R₃) = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 − R₁/100) × (1 − R₂/100) × (1 − R₃/100)

 
 
•

**Calculations:**

⇒ Value after 1st year = 10000 − (10% of 10000) = 10000 − 1000 = 9000

⇒ Value after 2nd year = 9000 − (20% of 9000) = 9000 − 1800 = 7200

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by (a + b + a×b/100)%. For depreciation, the values of a and b are taken as negative.

Constant Depreciation Formula

If the rate of depreciation is constant at R% per annum, the value after n years is calculated as Value = P × (1 − R/100)ⁿ.

The same successive multiplication principle applies to population growth or compound interest, where rates are added instead of subtracted: Final Value = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ.

question: A number is first increased by 12% and then increased by 23%. The number, so obtained, is now decreased by 34%. What is the net increase or decrease percent in the original number (nearest to an integer)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The net change for two successive percentage changes is: x + y + (x × y) / 100

First two increases (+12% and +23%): Net = 12 + 23 + (12 × 23) / 100 = 35 + 2.76 = +37.76%

Now, combine the new net (+37.76%) with the final decrease (−34%):

Net Change = 37.76 − 34 − (37.76 × 34) / 100 = 3.76 − 12.8384 = −9.0784%

The negative sign indicates an overall decrease, which is approximately 9%.

**∴ The correct answer is 9% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial increase = 12%, Second increase = 23%, Final decrease = 34%

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + r₁/100) × (1 + r₂/100) × (1 − r₃/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4acf4b4ced3db86161ef732db1c9c6493fdb6cc7a90872a0f2fc24383cc25805.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the original number be 100.

⇒ Value after 12% increase = 100 × 1.12 = 112

⇒ Value after 23% increase = 112 × 1.23 = 137.76

⇒ Value after 34% decrease = 137.76 × 0.66 = 90.9216

⇒ Net Change = Final Value − Initial Value

⇒ Net Change = 90.9216 − 100 = −9.0784

⇒ A negative value indicates a decrease in the original number.

⇒ Decrease percentage ≈ 9% (nearest to an integer).

**∴ The correct answer is 9% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change Formula

When a quantity undergoes two successive changes of a% and b%, the equivalent overall percentage change is given by (a + b + ab/100)%. Use a positive value for an increase and a negative value for a decrease.

Multiplying Factor Method

For multiple successive percentage variations, using decimal multipliers is highly efficient. An increase of r% uses a multiplying factor of (1 + r/100), while a decrease of r% uses (1 − r/100). The final value is found by multiplying the initial base value by all successive factors.

question: Ravi's salary was increased by 50%. After some time, his new salary was also increased by 50%. Find his gain percentage on the salary.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a value is successively increased by x% and y%, the net percentage change is calculated using the successive percentage formula:

Net % Change = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100

Here, both increments are 50% (so x = 50, y = 50).

Net % Change = 50 + 50 + (50 × 50) ÷ 100 = 100 + 25 = 125%

**∴ The correct answer is 125%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/959a3df6cdaa68bd3d15e0bd7156fc35e2b19dab12d7d01b98f3dc4b4278de3d.png] 

**Given:**

First salary increase = 50%

Second salary increase = 50%

**Formula Used:**

Gain Percentage = (Total Gain ÷ Initial Salary) × 100%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial salary of Ravi be 100 units.

⇒ After the first 50% increase, salary = 100 + (50% of 100) = 150 units.

⇒ After the second 50% increase, salary = 150 + (50% of 150) = 150 + 75 = 225 units.

⇒ Total Gain = Final Salary − Initial Salary = 225 − 100 = 125 units.

⇒ Gain Percentage = (125 ÷ 100) × 100% = 125%.

**∴ The correct answer is 125%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

When a value undergoes two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the effective percentage change is [a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100]%. Remember to use a negative sign if it involves a decrease.

Multiplier Method (Fractional Equivalent)

A 50% increase means the new value becomes 150% (or 3/2) of the original base. Two successive 50% increases mean multiplying the base by (3/2) × (3/2) = 9/4. This represents an overall increase of 5/4 over the initial value, which is exactly 125%.

Base Change Implication

A common exam mistake is simply adding the percentages directly (50% + 50% = 100%). However, successive calculations must factor in that the second percentage increase operates on an already enlarged base, which intrinsically leads to a higher net gain.

**Calculations:**

Let the initial salary of the worker be 100.

⇒ Salary after 25% increase = 100 + (25 ÷ 100 × 100) = 125

⇒ Decrease amount = 12% of 125 = (12 ÷ 100) × 125 = 15

⇒ Final salary = 125 − 15 = 110

⇒ Overall change = Final salary − Initial salary = 110 − 100 = +10

⇒ Percentage change = (10 ÷ 100) × 100% = 10% increase

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is subjected to successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the net change can be found using the formula: Net % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Multiplying Factor Method

For successive changes, the final value can be directly calculated as: Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± f₁) × (1 ± f₂), where f represents the fractional equivalent of the percentage.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100. A positive result denotes an increase, while a negative result indicates a decrease.

question: An investor, invested ₹2,00,000 in shares. The shares rose by 18% on the first day, fell by 15% on the second day, and then fell by 3% on the third day. What is the net percentage increase or decrease in the value of the investor's shares? (Rounded up to one decimal place)

Effective change for +0.3% and −3%: 0.3 − 3 − (0.3 × 3) / 100 = −2.7 − 0.009 = −2.709%

The negative sign represents a decrease. Rounding to one decimal place gives a 2.7% decrease.

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by 2.7%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

Net Value = Initial Value × (100 ± R₁)/100 × (100 ± R₂)/100 × (100 ± R₃)/100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial value of shares be 100 (since the final answer is a percentage, the base of ₹2,00,000 is not needed).

⇒ Value after Day 1 = 100 × 118/100 = 118

⇒ Value after Day 2 = 118 × 85/100 = 100.3

⇒ Value after Day 3 = 100.3 × 97/100 = 97.291

Independence of Base Value

subject: MATH
question: Two successive percentage decrease of 25% each is by what percentage less than two successive percentage increase of 25% each? (Round to two decimal places.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net equivalent % formula = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100

Equivalent decrease = −25 − 25 + (−25 × −25) ÷ 100 = −43.75%

Equivalent increase = 25 + 25 + (25 × 25) ÷ 100 = 56.25%

Required % = [(56.25 − 43.75) ÷ 56.25] × 100

⇒ (12.5 ÷ 56.25) × 100 = (2 ÷ 9) × 100 = 22.22%

**∴ The correct answer is 22.22%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1683b38976f503af2a442a1ae899736b175e2dc1249eab818fde75afe99830f4.png] 

**Given:**

Two successive percentage increases of 25%.

Two successive percentage decreases of 25%.

**Formula Used:**

Effective % change = A + B + (A × B) ÷ 100

Percentage less = [(Greater Value − Smaller Value) ÷ Greater Value] × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ For two successive decreases of 25%:

⇒ Effective decrease = 25 + 25 − (25 × 25) ÷ 100

⇒ Effective decrease = 50 − 6.25 = 43.75%

⇒ For two successive increases of 25%:

⇒ Effective increase = 25 + 25 + (25 × 25) ÷ 100

⇒ Effective increase = 50 + 6.25 = 56.25%

⇒ Difference between the two values = 56.25% − 43.75% = 12.5%

⇒ Percentage by which decrease is less than increase = (Difference ÷ Effective increase) × 100

⇒ Required % = (12.5 ÷ 56.25) × 100

⇒ Required % = (1250 ÷ 5625) × 100

⇒ Required % = (2 ÷ 9) × 100 = 200 ÷ 9 %

⇒ Required % ≈ 22.22%

**∴ The correct answer is 22.22%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is subjected to two successive changes of x% and y%, the net change is given by (x + y + xy ÷ 100)%. Use a positive sign for an increase and a negative sign for a decrease.

Percentage Less / More

To find by what percent A is less than B, always take the difference with respect to the base value B using the formula: [(B − A) ÷ B] × 100.

Successive Discounts

For two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂%, the single equivalent discount formula directly evaluates as (d₁ + d₂ − d₁ × d₂ ÷ 100)%.
</p

question: If B is 25% more than A, and C is 20% more than B, then what is A : C?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the value of A be 100.

Since B is 25% more than A, B = 100 + 25 = 125.

Since C is 20% more than B, C = 125 + (20 / 100) × 125 = 125 + 25 = 150.

The ratio of A : C = 100 : 150 = 2 : 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

B is 25% more than A.

C is 20% more than B.

**Method Used:**

Fractional representation of percentage increase.

 B
 125
 
 
• 
 +20%
 
 
 C
 150
 
 A : C = 100 : 150 = 2 : 3

**Calculations:**

⇒ 25% expressed as a fraction = 1 / 4

⇒ B = A + (1 / 4) × A = 5 / 4 × A

⇒ Ratio of A / B = 4 / 5

⇒ 20% expressed as a fraction = 1 / 5

⇒ C = B + (1 / 5) × B = 6 / 5 × B

⇒ Ratio of B / C = 5 / 6

⇒ To find the overall ratio A : C, multiply the individual ratios:

⇒ A / C = (A / B) × (B / C)

⇒ A / C = (4 / 5) × (5 / 6) = 20 / 30 = 2 / 3

Converting percentages directly to simplified fractions helps in speeding up ratio calculations. Always memorize common fractions like 25% = 1/4 and 20% = 1/5.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two sequential ratios a:b and b:c is calculated by multiplying them: (a/b) × (b/c) = a/c. This provides the direct relationship between the first and last terms.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes multiple changes sequentially, you can multiply the base with successive scaling factors. For example: Final = Base × (1 + %1) × (1 + %2).

question: The price of a product is decreased by x% and then increased by x%. The final price becomes 10% less than the original. What is the value of x (approximately)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a value is first decreased by x% and then increased by x%, there is always a net decrease of (x² ÷ 100)%.

Given the overall net decrease is 10%.

⇒ x² ÷ 100 = 10

⇒ x² = 1000

⇒ x = √1000 ≈ 31.62

**∴ The correct answer is 31.6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Final price is 10% less than the original price.

 100 100 − x 90 
• −x% 
• +x% 
 Net Decrease = 10% 
 
 

**Formula Used:**

Effective Percentage Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

Let the original price be 100.

⇒ Price after x% decrease = 100 − x

⇒ Price after subsequent x% increase = (100 − x) × (100 + x) ÷ 100

⇒ Final price = (10000 − x²) ÷ 100 = 100 − x² ÷ 100

Given that the final price becomes 10% less than the original.

⇒ Final expected price = 100 − 10 = 90

Equating both values:

⇒ 100 − x² ÷ 100 = 90

⇒ x² ÷ 100 = 10

⇒ x² = 1000

Using √10 ≈ 3.162:

Equal Percentage Increase and Decrease

question: Three candidates were participating in an election. The person in third place got 20% of the total votes while the difference between the votes of the winner and the first runner-up was 20% of the total votes. If the difference between the votes of the first runner-up and the second runner-up was 37,000, how many votes did the winner receive?
solution:
**Given:**

There are 3 candidates in the election.

The third-place candidate got 20% of the total votes.

The difference between the votes of the winner and the first runner-up was 20% of the total votes.

The difference between the votes of the first runner-up and the second runner-up was 37,000 votes.

**Formula used:**

Percentage = (Part / Whole) × 100

Total = Part1 + Part2 + Part3

**Solution:**

Let 100x be the total number of votes.

Let the winners get votes and the 2nd runner-up get b votes.

The number of votes for the third-place candidate is 20% of total votes = 20x.

So the total number of votes winner and 2nd runner-up gets is

a + b + 20x = 100x

a + b = 80x ..........(1)

According to the question.

The difference in the votes between votes of the winner and the first runner-up was 20% of the total votes

So,

a - b = 20x......... (2)

Solving equation (1) & (2),

We get a = 50x and b = 30x

Now, the difference between the votes of the first runner-up and the second runner-up was 37,000

So, 30x - 20x = 37000

x = 3700

The number of votes for the winner is 50x = 50 × 3700 = 1,85,000

**Therefore, the winner received 1,85,000 votes.**

So, person in 3rd place got 20% which is = 20 unit remaining 80 unit

Difference of votes of 1st and 2nd is 20%, so winner must got 50 unit and 2ⁿd got 30 unit

According to the question, the difference of votes between 2ⁿd and 3rd is 37000

So,(30 - 20) = 10 unit → 37,000

So, 50 unit → 37000/10 × 50 = 37000 × 5 = 185000

S.P of both items = (120x + 108x) = Rs. 228x

Overall profit at the end of both transaction = (228x - 220x) = Rs. 8x

Profit percentage = (8x/220x) × 100% = 3(7)/(11)%

**∴ The overall profit percentage is 3(7)/(11)%**

question: A and B invested their money in a business in the ratio of 9 ∶ 5. If 10% of the total profit goes for charity and A’s share is Rs. 29,840, what is the total profit (in Rs., to the nearest integer)?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total distributed profit = Total profit × 90%.

A's share = Total profit × (90 / 100) × [9 / (9 + 5)].

29840 = Total profit × (9 / 10) × (9 / 14).

Total profit = 29840 × (140 / 81) = 4177600 / 81 = 51575.30...

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 51,575.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Investment ratio of A and B = 9 : 5

Percentage of profit going to charity = 10%

A's profit share = Rs. 29,840

**Formula Used:**

Profit ratio = Investment ratio (when the time period is identical)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0aa64d11c2782894d903762947d6faf235f5bfb4ca30f205a9848154f511a62b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total profit be P.

⇒ Profit distributed between A and B = P − 10% of P = 90% of P = 0.9P.

⇒ Investment ratio of A and B = 9 : 5

⇒ Total ratio parts = 9 + 5 = 14 parts.

⇒ A's profit share = (9 / 14) of the remaining profit

⇒ 29840 = (9 / 14) × 0.9P

⇒ 29840 = (8.1 / 14) × P

⇒ P = (29840 × 14) / 8.1

⇒ P = 417760 / 8.1 = 4177600 / 81

⇒ P = 51575.308...

⇒ Rounding to the nearest integer, Total Profit ≈ Rs. 51,575

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 51,575.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sleeping Partner

A partner who only invests money but does not take part in the management of the business is known as a sleeping partner. Active partners receive a fixed salary or a certain percentage of the profit for managing the business before the remaining profit is distributed among all partners.

Compound Partnership

When investments are made for different time periods, it is called a compound partnership. The profit share ratio is the product of capital invested and the time period of investment (P₁ : P₂ = C₁×T₁ : C₂×T₂).

Joining Mid-way

If a partner joins x months after the start of a financial year, their investment time period for that year is (12 − x) months, which must be multiplied by their capital to determine their final profit share ratio compared to the primary investors.

question: If the selling price of an article is doubled, then the profit becomes four times. What was the original profit percentage?

**Given:**

If the selling price of an article is doubled, then the profit becomes four times.

⇒ {(3 - 2) × 100}/2 = 100/2 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

question: Mona purchased two sets of jewellery for Rs. 4,000 each. She sold these sets of jewellery, gaining 8% on one and losing 6% on the other. Calculate her total loss or gain in this whole transaction.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When Cost Price (CP) is same for both items:

Net Gain/Loss = Total Profit Value − Total Loss Value

⇒ Net Gain/Loss = (8% of 4000) − (6% of 4000)

⇒ Net Gain/Loss = 2% of 4000 = 80

⇒ Since the result is positive, it is a gain of Rs. 80.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 80 gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

CP of each jewellery set = Rs. 4000

Profit% on 1st set = 8%

Loss% on 2nd set = 6%

**Formula Used:**

Profit or Loss = CP × (Profit or Loss % / 100)

 Transaction Breakdown
 
 
 Set 1: CP = 4000
 

 +8% Gain
 
 
 Set 2: CP = 4000
 

 −6% Loss
 
 
• 
 Total Result = Gain (320) − Loss (240) = Rs. 80
 
 
 
 

 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP = 4000 + 4000 = Rs. 8000

⇒ Profit on the first jewellery set = 4000 × (8 / 100) = Rs. 320

⇒ Loss on the second jewellery set = 4000 × (6 / 100) = Rs. 240

⇒ Total Gain/Loss = 320 − 240 = +80

⇒ Since the net value is positive, it is a gain of Rs. 80.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 80 gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Case of Same Cost Price (CP)

If two items are bought at the same CP, the net profit or loss percent is simply the arithmetic average of individual profit/loss percentages: Net % = (P1% ± L2%) / 2.

Case of Same Selling Price (SP)

If two items are sold at the same SP, one at x% profit and another at x% loss, there is always a net loss of (x² / 100)%.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100 | Loss % = (Loss / CP) × 100. Profit and loss are always calculated on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise.</p

question: An article is sold at a profit of 250%. What is the ratio of its cost price to selling price?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let the Cost Price (CP) = 100 units.

Profit is given as 250%, so Profit = 250 units.

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = 100 + 250 = 350 units.

Required Ratio (CP : SP) = 100 : 350 = 2 : 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 7.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit percentage = 250%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) + Profit

Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × CP

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e30d104fc230fdf52546a98cf5d10285a195d9f547c0ad15293fc8676a8c615a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) be x.

⇒ Profit = 250% of x = 2.5x

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit

⇒ SP = x + 2.5x = 3.5x

⇒ Ratio of CP to SP = CP ÷ SP

⇒ Ratio = x ÷ 3.5x

⇒ Ratio = 1 ÷ 3.5

⇒ Multiply by 10 to remove the decimal: Ratio = 10 ÷ 35

⇒ Dividing both sides by 5: Ratio = 2 ÷ 7

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 7.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP)

The actual amount paid to purchase an article or the price at which it is manufactured.

Selling Price (SP)

The final price at which an article is sold to a customer. A transaction results in profit when SP > CP.

Important Profit Formulas

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100
SP = CP × [(100 + Profit %) ÷ 100]

question: Samreen sells a keyboard for ₹1,260 at a profit of 25%, and another keyboard for ₹1,440 at a loss of 10%. What is her total gain or loss percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total SP = ₹1260 + ₹1440 = ₹2700

Total CP = 1260 × (100 ÷ 125) + 1440 × (100 ÷ 90) = ₹1008 + ₹1600 = ₹2608

Overall Gain = Total SP − Total CP = 2700 − 2608 = ₹92

Gain % = (92 ÷ 2608) × 100 = 575 ÷ 163 = 3 ⁸⁶/₁₆₃%

**∴ The correct answer is 3 ⁸⁶/₁₆₃% Gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of first keyboard = ₹1260, Profit = 25%

Selling Price (SP) of second keyboard = ₹1440, Loss = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)] × SP

Cost Price (CP) = [100 ÷ (100 − Loss%)] × SP

Gain % = (Gain ÷ Total CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc8b975cabc12fb7ddf530ddce26f0a4033797483078e0a13eef38891ee5d324.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of first keyboard = (100 ÷ 125) × 1260 = (4 ÷ 5) × 1260 = ₹1008

⇒ CP of second keyboard = (100 ÷ 90) × 1440 = (10 ÷ 9) × 1440 = ₹1600

⇒ Total CP = 1008 + 1600 = ₹2608

⇒ Total SP = 1260 + 1440 = ₹2700

⇒ Total Gain = Total SP − Total CP = 2700 − 2608 = ₹92

⇒ Gain Percentage = (92 ÷ 2608) × 100

⇒ Gain Percentage = 9200 ÷ 2608 = 2300 ÷ 652

⇒ Gain Percentage = 575 ÷ 163 = 3 ⁸⁶/₁₆₃%

**∴ The correct answer is 3 ⁸⁶/₁₆₃% Gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Overall Profit or Loss on Same Selling Price

When two identical items are sold at the same selling price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always an overall loss given by Loss% = (x ÷ 10)². In this problem, selling prices are different, so individual calculation was required.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100. This relationship is useful when the items are sold after offering a flat discount on the catalog or marked price.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer claims to sell items at his cost price but uses a false weight, his profit percent is evaluated as: Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.

Using the Alligation Method directly on profit percentages to find the ratio of their Cost Prices (CP):

Ratio of CP of Sofa to Table = (Table Profit % − Overall Profit %) : (Overall Profit % − Sofa Profit %)

⇒ Ratio = (15.25 − 13) : (13 − 10) = 2.25 : 3 = 225 : 300 = 3 : 4

Total CP parts = 3 + 4 = 7 parts ⇒ 7 parts = ₹28,000

⇒ 1 part = ₹4,000

Difference in CP = 4 parts − 3 parts = 1 part = ₹4,000

⇒ Profit percentage on selling the Sofa = 10%

⇒ Profit percentage on selling the Table = 15.25%

⇒ Overall profit percentage on both = 13%

**Formula Used:**

We apply the Rule of Alligation to find the ratio of the Cost Prices of the two articles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4c4e22d74f4ad4aef6134dfe43f8bed451703a553b1c2325902048cf0ae7e099.png]

⇒ x = 28000 ÷ 7 = 4000

⇒ Required difference in CP = CP of Table − CP of Sofa

⇒ Difference = 4x − 3x = x

⇒ Difference = ₹4000

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation in Profit & Loss

When two items are mixed or sold together at different profit/loss percentages, applying the alligation method yields the ratio of their Base Values, which is the Cost Price (CP) for profit and loss scenarios.

Weighted Average Formula

The overall profit percentage is the weighted average of the individual profit percentages. Formula: Overall % = (CP₁ × P₁ + CP₂ × P₂) ÷ (CP₁ + CP₂).

Handling Loss in Alligation

If an item is sold at a loss, its percentage must be written with a negative sign (e.g., −10%) in the alligation cross. The arithmetic difference must be carefully calculated considering the negative sign.
