question: A lent Rs. 5000 to B for a duration of 2 years and Rs. 3000 to C for a period of 4 years both at the same simple interest rate. In total, he received Rs. 2200 as interest from both borrowers. What is the rate of interest per annum?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equivalent principal for 1 year = (5000 × 2) + (3000 × 4) = 10000 + 12000 = 22000

Total Simple Interest received = 2200

Rate (decimal) = Total Interest ÷ Equivalent Principal = 2200 ÷ 22000

Rate = 0.1

**∴ The correct answer is 0.1 per annum.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Principal lent to B = ₹5000, Time = 2 years

Principal lent to C = ₹3000, Time = 4 years

Total simple interest = ₹2200

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = Principal × Rate × Time

(where Rate is taken as a decimal fraction r)

 
 Lent to B
 ₹5000 × 2 yrs

 
 Lent to C
 ₹3000 × 4 yrs

 

 

 

 

 
 Total SI = ₹2200

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest from B = 5000 × r × 2 = 10000r

⇒ Interest from C = 3000 × r × 4 = 12000r

⇒ Total Interest = 10000r + 12000r

⇒ 22000r = 2200

⇒ r = 2200 ÷ 22000

⇒ r = 0.1

**∴ The correct answer is 0.1 per annum.**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate in %, and T is Time in years.

Decimal vs Percentage Rate

When solving equations, the percentage rate R can be expressed directly as a decimal r (where r = R ÷ 100) making the SI calculation simply P × r × T.

Equivalent Principal

When multiple investments are made at the same simple interest rate, the overall principal equivalent to a 1-year term is the sum of the products of each Principal and its respective Time period.

question: A person invested a total sum of ₹2200 in three different schemes of simple interest at 4%, 5%, and 10% per annum. At the end of one year, he got the same interest from all three schemes. What was the amount (in ₹) invested at 5%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the simple interest from different schemes is equal, the ratio of investments is inversely proportional to the product of Rate and Time.

Ratio of investments = 1/R₁ : 1/R₂ : 1/R₃ (since time is 1 year for all)

Ratio = 1/4 : 1/5 : 1/10 = 5 : 4 : 2

Total parts = 5 + 4 + 2 = 11 parts = ₹2200 ⇒ 1 part = ₹200

Amount invested at 5% corresponds to 4 parts = 4 × 200 = ₹800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 Total = ₹2200
 
 

 

 

 
 
 Part 1
 @ 4% for 1 yr
 
 
 Part 2
 @ 5% for 1 yr
 
 
 Part 3
 @ 10% for 1 yr
 
 

 

 

 
 
 Interest is EQUAL across all three parts (I1 = I2 = I3)

**Given:**

Total sum invested = ₹2200

Rate of interest for scheme 1 (R₁) = 4%

Rate of interest for scheme 2 (R₂) = 5%

Rate of interest for scheme 3 (R₃) = 10%

Time period (T) = 1 year

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

Let the amounts invested in the three schemes be P₁, P₂, and P₃.

⇒ P₁ + P₂ + P₃ = 2200

According to the question, the simple interest earned from all three schemes is equal:

⇒ (P₁ × 4 × 1) ÷ 100 = (P₂ × 5 × 1) ÷ 100 = (P₃ × 10 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 4P₁ = 5P₂ = 10P₃

Dividing the equation by the LCM of 4, 5, and 10 (which is 20):

⇒ 4P₁ ÷ 20 = 5P₂ ÷ 20 = 10P₃ ÷ 20

⇒ P₁ ÷ 5 = P₂ ÷ 4 = P₃ ÷ 2

⇒ Ratio of investments (P₁ : P₂ : P₃) = 5 : 4 : 2

Sum of the ratio parts = 5 + 4 + 2 = 11 parts

⇒ 11 parts = 2200

⇒ 1 part = 2200 ÷ 11 = 200

The amount invested at 5% is P₂, which corresponds to 4 parts.

⇒ Amount invested at 5% = 4 × 200 = ₹800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equal Interest Condition in SI

If a total sum is divided into multiple parts such that the Simple Interest earned on each part is equal, the ratio of the principal amounts is directly given by: P₁ : P₂ : P₃ = (1/R₁T₁) : (1/R₂T₂) : (1/R₃T₃).

Equal Amount Condition in SI

If a sum is divided such that the Final Amount (Principal + Interest) earned on each part is equal, the ratio of the principal investments is given by: P₁ : P₂ : P₃ = 1/(100 + R₁T₁) : 1/(100 + R₂T₂) : 1/(100 + R₃T₃).

Simple vs Compound Interest Concept

In Simple Interest, the interest is calculated only on the original principal for the entire time period. In Compound Interest, the interest is calculated on both the principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods.

Simple Interest (SI)

question: If A, B, and C are three amounts of money such that B is the simple interest on A, and C is the simple interest on B, all for the same time and at the same rate of interest, then which of the following is true?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the rate of interest and time period are the same, the ratio of Simple Interest to Principal remains constant.

Ratio for the first case = B ÷ A

Ratio for the second case = C ÷ B

Equating both ratios: B ÷ A = C ÷ B

By cross-multiplying, we get: B² = AC

**∴ The correct answer is B² = AC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple interest on amount A = B

Simple interest on amount B = C

Rate of interest (R) and Time (T) are the same for both cases.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 A

 

 SI = B

 
 B

 

 SI = C

 
 C

 Ratio of SI to P is constant → B/A = C/B

**Calculations:**

⇒ For the first case, the principal is A and simple interest is B.

⇒ B = (A × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ (R × T) ÷ 100 = B ÷ A --- (Equation 1)

⇒ For the second case, the principal is B and simple interest is C.

⇒ C = (B × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ (R × T) ÷ 100 = C ÷ B --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Equating Equation 1 and Equation 2, we get:

⇒ B ÷ A = C ÷ B

⇒ B × B = A × C

⇒ B² = AC

**∴ The correct answer is B² = AC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P = Principal, R = Rate %, and T = Time.

Compound Interest (CI)

Amount A = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)T and CI = A − P.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference is D = P × (R ÷ 100)².

question: What is the value of ((0.1×0.1×0.1+0.03×0.03×0.03))/((0.3×0.3×0.3+0.09×0.09×0.09))
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Observe the relationship between the numerator and the denominator.

Each term in the denominator is exactly 3 times the corresponding term in the numerator.

Expression = (0.1³ + 0.03³) ÷ [(3 × 0.1)³ + (3 × 0.03)³]

⇒ 1 ÷ 3³ = 1 ÷ 27

⇒ 1 ÷ 27 ≈ 0.037

**∴ The correct answer is 0.037.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = (0.1 × 0.1 × 0.1 + 0.03 × 0.03 × 0.03) ÷ (0.3 × 0.3 × 0.3 + 0.09 × 0.09 × 0.09)

**Formula Used:**

(x × y)ⁿ = xⁿ × yⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Numerator = 0.1³ + 0.03³

⇒ Denominator = 0.3³ + 0.09³

⇒ Denominator = (3 × 0.1)³ + (3 × 0.03)³

⇒ Denominator = 3³ × 0.1³ + 3³ × 0.03³

⇒ Denominator = 27 × (0.1³ + 0.03³)

⇒ Expression = (0.1³ + 0.03³) ÷ [27 × (0.1³ + 0.03³)]

⇒ Expression = 1 ÷ 27

⇒ 1 ÷ 27 = 0.037037...

**∴ The correct answer is 0.037.**

**__Additional Information__**

Laws of Exponents

When terms are multiplied and raised to a common power, the power distributes directly to both numbers: (xy)ⁿ = xⁿ × yⁿ. This allows easy extraction of common multiples from complex decimals.

Algebraic Simplification

In simplification problems involving decimals that look similar, always check if the denominator is a direct multiple of the numerator before calculating the actual cubes or squares.

Recurring Decimals

Fractions like 1 ÷ 27 result in non-terminating, repeating decimals. The value 1 ÷ 27 equals 0.037037037..., which is generally rounded off to 0.037 as given in the exam options.
</p

Using the Digital Root (DR) method:

DR of 44³ = 8³ = 512 ⇒ 8

DR of 35³ = 8³ = 512 ⇒ 8

DR of 53³ = 8³ = 512 ⇒ 8, and DR of 159 = 1 + 5 + 9 = 15 ⇒ 6

Expression DR = 8 + 8 − 8 + 6 = 14 ⇒ 5

Checking options, DR of −20659 is 9 − (2 + 0 + 6 + 5 + 9) = 9 − 22 ⇒ 9 − 4 = 5. (Matches perfectly)

**∴ The correct answer is -20659.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

44³ + 35³ − 53³ + 159

**Calculations:**

First, calculate the cube of each number:

⇒ 44³ = 44 × 44 × 44 = 85184

⇒ 35³ = 35 × 35 × 35 = 42875

⇒ 53³ = 53 × 53 × 53 = 148877

Substitute the values back into the expression:

⇒ 85184 + 42875 − 148877 + 159

Summing the positive numbers:

⇒ (85184 + 42875 + 159) − 148877

⇒ 128218 − 148877

Subtracting the larger value from the smaller value:

⇒ −20659

**∴ The correct answer is -20659.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Digital Root Method

The sum of the digits of a number until a single digit is obtained. It serves as an excellent shortcut to verify large calculations without doing the actual arithmetic.

Digital Root for Negative Numbers

If an algebraic calculation involves negative final roots, you find the positive single digit form by subtracting its absolute digital root from 9.

question: What is the value of (0.02³ + 0.004³) ÷ (0.2³ + 0.04³)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Observe the relationship between the numerator and denominator terms.

Each term in the numerator is exactly 1/10 of the corresponding term in the denominator (0.02 = 0.2 ÷ 10 and 0.004 = 0.04 ÷ 10).

Since all terms are cubed, the overall multiplying factor becomes (1/10)³ = 1/1000.

The whole expression simplifies directly to 1/1000 = 0.001.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.001.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(0.02³ + 0.004³) ÷ (0.2³ + 0.04³)

**Formula Used:**

(x/y)ⁿ = xⁿ ÷ yⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us rewrite the decimal terms in the numerator as fractions of the denominator terms.

⇒ 0.02 = 0.2 ÷ 10

⇒ 0.004 = 0.04 ÷ 10

⇒ Numerator = (0.2 ÷ 10)³ + (0.04 ÷ 10)³

⇒ Numerator = (0.2³ ÷ 1000) + (0.04³ ÷ 1000)

⇒ Numerator = (1 ÷ 1000) × (0.2³ + 0.04³)

⇒ Substitute this back into the original expression.

⇒ Expression = [(1 ÷ 1000) × (0.2³ + 0.04³)] ÷ (0.2³ + 0.04³)

⇒ Cancel out the common term (0.2³ + 0.04³).

⇒ Expression = 1 ÷ 1000 = 0.001

**∴ The correct answer is 0.001.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Laws of Exponents

When dividing terms with the same base, powers are subtracted: am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ. Also, (ab)ⁿ = aⁿbⁿ.

BODMAS Rule

Always follow the logical sequence of Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction while simplifying algebraic and decimal expressions.
</p

⇒ Expression = Numerator ÷ Denominator

⇒ Expression = [(0.4)³ + (0.02)³] ÷ {27 × [(0.4)³ + (0.02)³]}

⇒ Expression = 1 / 27

**∴ The correct answer is 1/27.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities for Cubes

Formulas such as a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) are frequently used to expand and simplify complex fractional equations.

Laws of Exponents

When multiplying numbers within a shared exponent, the rule is (x × y)ⁿ = xⁿ × yⁿ. This allows proportional multipliers to be factored out perfectly.

BODMAS Rule

Here, a = 19, b = 20, and c = −39. Since 19 + 20 − 39 = 0, we can apply the trick.

19³ + 20³ − 39³ = 3 × 19 × 20 × (−39) = −44460.

Now, add 118 to this result: −44460 + 118 = −44342.

**∴ The correct answer is −44342.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

19³ + 20³ − 39³ + 118

**Formula Used:**

If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let a = 19, b = 20, and c = −39

⇒ Sum of terms: a + b + c = 19 + 20 − 39 = 0

⇒ Therefore, 19³ + 20³ + (−39)³ = 3 × 19 × 20 × (−39)

⇒ 3 × 19 = 57

⇒ 57 × 20 = 1140

⇒ 1140 × (−39) = −44460

⇒ Substituting this value back into the original expression:

⇒ −44460 + 118 = −44342

**∴ The correct answer is −44342.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Cubes

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca). If a + b + c = 0, the right-hand side becomes 0, leading to the direct shortcut: a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

Sum of Cubes Formula

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)

Difference of Cubes Formula

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

BODMAS Rule

Always follow the correct order of operations in algebraic expressions: Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division × Multiplication, Addition − Subtraction.

question: If 25% of (P + Q) = 75% of (P - Q), then find the ratio P: Q.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given 25% of (P + Q) = 75% of (P − Q).

Taking the inverse ratio: (P + Q) / (P − Q) = 75% / 25% = 3 / 1

Applying the Componendo and Dividendo rule:

P / Q = (3 + 1) / (3 − 1)

⇒ P / Q = 4 / 2 = 2 / 1

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

25% of (P + Q) = 75% of (P − Q)

 P (2 parts) Q (1 part) P + Q (3 parts) P − Q (1 part) 
• 
• 
• 
• Ratio P : Q = 2 : 1 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (25 / 100) × (P + Q) = (75 / 100) × (P − Q)

⇒ 1 × (P + Q) = 3 × (P − Q)

⇒ P + Q = 3P − 3Q

Bringing all P terms to one side and Q terms to the other:

⇒ Q + 3Q = 3P − P

⇒ 4Q = 2P

⇒ P / Q = 4 / 2

⇒ P : Q = 2 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Componendo and Dividendo

If a / b = c / d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This rule is extremely useful for rapidly solving equations that involve sums and differences of the same two variables.

Inverse Ratio Logic

If A% of X = B% of Y, the ratio of the variables is inversely proportional to their respective percentages. Therefore, X / Y = B / A.

Percentage Simplification

Converting standard percentages to simple fractions (e.g., 25% = 1 / 4, 75% = 3 / 4) makes cross-multiplication faster and prevents errors with larger numerical values.

⇒ 0.5 = 5 × 0.1

⇒ 0.05 = 5 × 0.01

⇒ 0.005 = 5 × 0.001

⇒ Substituting these rewritten values into the main expression:

⇒ [(5 × 0.1)³ + (5 × 0.01)³ + (5 × 0.001)³] ÷ [(0.1)³ + (0.01)³ + (0.001)³]

⇒ Expanding the cubes using the rule (a × b)³ = a³ × b³:

⇒ [5³ × (0.1)³ + 5³ × (0.01)³ + 5³ × (0.001)³] ÷ [(0.1)³ + (0.01)³ + (0.001)³]

⇒ Taking 5³ as a common factor from the numerator:

⇒ 5³ × [(0.1)³ + (0.01)³ + (0.001)³] ÷ [(0.1)³ + (0.01)³ + (0.001)³]

⇒ The common bracket term cancels out completely.

⇒ Remaining value = 5³ = 125

**∴ The correct answer is 125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Laws of Exponents

When a product of numbers is raised to a power, the power is smoothly distributed to each multiplier: (a × b)ⁿ = aⁿ × bⁿ.

Value = 1 ÷ 2³ = 1/8 = 0.125

⇒ Using the exponent rule (a × b)ⁿ = aⁿ × bⁿ:

⇒ Denominator = (2³ × 0.12³) + (2³ × 0.06³)

⇒ Taking 2³ common from both terms:

⇒ Denominator = 8 × (0.12³ + 0.06³)

⇒ Now substitute the denominator back into the given expression:

⇒ Expression = (0.12³ + 0.06³) ÷ [8 × (0.12³ + 0.06³)]

⇒ The term (0.12³ + 0.06³) cancels out entirely from both numerator and denominator.

⇒ Expression = 1 / 8

⇒ Expression = 0.125

**∴ The correct answer is 0.125.**

question: Simplify the expression: sqrt{(9+4sqrt{5})}
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rewrite the expression in the form √(x + 2√y) to apply the direct splitting method.

√(9 + 4√5) = √(9 + 2√(4 × 5)) = √(9 + 2√20)

Find two numbers whose sum is 9 and product is 20 ⇒ The numbers are 5 and 4.

The square root is directly the sum of their individual square roots: √5 + √4.

⇒ √5 + 2

**∴ The correct answer is √5 + 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: √(9 + 4√5)

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculations:**

⇒ We need to express 9 + 4√5 as a perfect square to remove the outer root.

⇒ Compare the irrational part (4√5) with the 2ab term of the identity: 2ab = 4√5 ⇒ ab = 2√5.

⇒ By trial, possible values for a and b are 2 and √5.

⇒ Verify the sum of their squares: a² + b² = 2² + (√5)² = 4 + 5 = 9.

⇒ Since a² + b² = 9 perfectly matches the rational part, we can rewrite the expression:

⇒ 9 + 4√5 = 4 + 5 + 4√5 = 2² + (√5)² + 2 × 2 × √5 = (2 + √5)²

⇒ √(9 + 4√5) = √((2 + √5)²)

⇒ √(9 + 4√5) = 2 + √5 = √5 + 2

**∴ The correct answer is √5 + 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Surds

To find the square root of a mixed surd a ± 2√b, find two numbers whose sum is a and product is b. The answer will be √x ± √y.

Conjugate of a Surd

The conjugate of a + √b is a − √b. This property is highly useful when rationalising the denominator of an irrational fraction.

BODMAS Rule

Always simplify expressions following the correct order: Brackets, Orders (Powers/Roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.
</p

⇒ Denominator = (√7)² − (√3)² = 7 − 3 = 4

⇒ Expression = √7 / 2

question: Simplify: frac{sqrt{5+2sqrt{6}}}{sqrt{5-2sqrt{6}}}
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combine the numerator and denominator under a single square root: √( (5 + 2√6) / (5 − 2√6) )

Rationalize the fraction inside the root by multiplying both numerator and denominator by the conjugate (5 + 2√6).

The denominator becomes 5² − (2√6)² = 25 − 24 = 1.

The numerator becomes (5 + 2√6)².

The expression directly simplifies to √( (5 + 2√6)² / 1 ) = 5 + 2√6.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 + 2√6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: √(5 + 2√6) / √(5 − 2√6)

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, express the terms inside the square roots as perfect squares.

⇒ 5 + 2√6 = 3 + 2 + 2√(3 × 2) = (√3)² + (√2)² + 2(√3)(√2) = (√3 + √2)²

⇒ 5 − 2√6 = 3 + 2 − 2√(3 × 2) = (√3)² + (√2)² − 2(√3)(√2) = (√3 − √2)²

⇒ Substitute these back into the original expression:

⇒ √(√3 + √2)² / √(√3 − √2)²

⇒ Simplify the square roots:

⇒ (√3 + √2) / (√3 − √2)

⇒ Rationalize the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate (√3 + √2):

⇒ [(√3 + √2) × (√3 + √2)] / [(√3 − √2) × (√3 + √2)]

⇒ Numerator: (√3 + √2)² = (√3)² + (√2)² + 2(√3)(√2) = 3 + 2 + 2√6 = 5 + 2√6

⇒ Denominator: (√3)² − (√2)² = 3 − 2 = 1

⇒ Final value = (5 + 2√6) / 1 = 5 + 2√6

**∴ The correct answer is 5 + 2√6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rationalization of Surds

Rationalization is the process of removing surds from a denominator by multiplying both the numerator and denominator by its conjugate. The conjugate of a + √b is a − √b.

Perfect Squares Involving Surds

Expressions of the form a + 2√b can frequently be rewritten as a perfect square (√x + √y)² if two numbers x and y can be found such that x + y = a and xy = b.

Quotient Property of Radicals

The quotient property states that √x ÷ √y = √(x/y). This allows combining separate roots in a fraction into a single root for easier algebraic simplification.

For an algebraic expression of the form (√a + √b)², the direct result is (a + b) + 2√(ab).

Here, a = 3 and b = 2.

⇒ (3 + 2) + 2√(3 × 2)

⇒ 5 + 2√6

**∴ The correct answer is 5 + 2√6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(√3 + √2)²

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

**Calculations:**

⇒ (√3 + √2)² = (√3)² + 2 × √3 × √2 + (√2)²

⇒ (√3)² = 3

⇒ (√2)² = 2

⇒ 2 × √3 × √2 = 2√6

⇒ 3 + 2√6 + 2

⇒ 5 + 2√6

**∴ The correct answer is 5 + 2√6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square of a Difference

(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b². This rule is used for expanding terms like (√3 − √2)².

Difference of Squares

(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b². This identity is most often used to rationalize denominators involving square roots.

Product of Square Roots

√a × √b = √(ab), provided both a and b are non-negative numbers.

question: Solve:(sqrt{7921}-sqrt{2070.25}) times ((1)/(4))
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the square roots using approximation:

⇒ √7921 = 89

⇒ 43.5 × 0.25 = 10.875

**∴ The correct answer is 10.875.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(√7921 − √2070.25) × (1/4)

**Calculation:**

⇒ We know that 80² = 6400 and 90² = 8100.

⇒ Since 7921 ends in 1 and is close to 8100, √7921 = 89.

⇒ Similarly, 45² = 2025 and 46² = 2116.

⇒ Since 2070.25 is between them and ends in .25, √2070.25 = 45.5.

⇒ Substitute these square roots into the given expression:

⇒ (89 − 45.5) × (1/4)

⇒ 43.5 × 0.25

⇒ 10.875

**∴ The correct answer is 10.875.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root Trick for numbers ending in 5

For a number ending in 5, such as N5, its square is given by [N × (N+1)] concatenated with 25. For example, 45² = (4 × 5) followed by 25 = 2025.

Decimal Roots

If a perfect square decimal has two digits after the decimal point, its square root will exactly have one digit after the decimal point.

question: What is the value of 4 + 44 + 444 + 4444 + 44444?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a series of a repeated digit 'd' in the form d + dd + ddd + ... up to n terms (where n ≤ 9):

Sum = d × 123...n

Here, the digit d = 4 and there are 5 terms.

Sum = 4 × 12345 = 49380

**∴ The correct answer is 49380.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = 4 + 44 + 444 + 4444 + 44444

**Calculation:**

Factoring out 4 from the expression:

⇒ 4 × (1 + 11 + 111 + 1111 + 11111)

Adding the numbers inside the bracket step-by-step:

⇒ 1 + 11 = 12

⇒ 12 + 111 = 123

⇒ 123 + 1111 = 1234

⇒ 1234 + 11111 = 12345

Now, multiply the sum by 4:

⇒ 4 × 12345

Breaking it down:

⇒ 4 × (10000 + 2000 + 300 + 40 + 5)

⇒ 40000 + 8000 + 1200 + 160 + 20 = 49380

**∴ The correct answer is 49380.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Repeated 1s

The sum of a series 1 + 11 + 111 + ... up to n terms (for n ≤ 9) is always a sequential number 123...n.

Sum of Repeated 9s

For a series like 9 + 99 + 999 + ... up to n terms, rewrite each term as (10 − 1) + (100 − 1) + (1000 − 1) ... to simplify the calculation to (10 + 100 + 1000 + ...) − n.

Column Addition Shortcut for Repeated Digits

To add repeated digit terms vertically, count the digits in each column. The units column has n terms, tens has n−1 terms, and so on. Multiply the digit by the count and sequentially carry over the extra value to the next place.

120 ÷ 15 of 4 + [11 × 4 ÷ 4 of {4 × 2 - (8 - 11)}]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

1. Solve 'of' and Brackets: 15 of 4 = 60 and {4 × 2 − (−3)} = 11.

2. Substitute: 120 ÷ 60 + [11 × 4 ÷ 4 of 11].

3. Square bracket: [11 × 4 ÷ 44] = [44 ÷ 44] = 1.

4. Total: 2 + 1 = 3.

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: 120 ÷ 15 of 4 + [11 × 4 ÷ 4 of {4 × 2 − (8 − 11)}]

Formula Used: VBODMAS rule (Vinculum, Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 120 ÷ (15 × 4) + [11 × 4 ÷ 4 of {8 − (−3)}]

⇒ 120 ÷ 60 + [11 × 4 ÷ 4 of 11]

⇒ 2 + [11 × 4 ÷ 44]

⇒ 2 + [44 ÷ 44]

⇒ 2 + 1

⇒ 3

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It specifies the order of operations: Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. Operations are performed from left to right for same-priority levels.

Precedence of 'Of'

The 'Of' operator represents multiplication but carries a higher priority than Division (÷) and standard Multiplication (×).

Bracket Hierarchy

Mathematical expressions are simplified by solving brackets in the specific sequence: Parentheses ( ) → Curly Braces { } → Square Brackets [ ].</p

Convert mixed fractions to improper fractions.

Multiply by 4/5:

(25/6) × (4/5) = (25 × 4) / (6 × 5) = 100/30 = 10/3.

Add the results:

(9/5) + (10/3).

Find the LCM of 5 and 3: LCM = 15.

(9/5) = 27/15, (10/3) = 50/15.

Add the fractions:

(27/15) + (50/15) = 77/15.

**Therefore, the simplified value is 77/15.**

question: Evaluate the expression: ((1)/(4) div (1)/(2)) div ((1)/(15) + 1 - (9)/(10))
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

First bracket: (1/4 ÷ 1/2) = 1/4 × 2 = 1/2

Second bracket: (1/15 + 1 − 9/10) = 2/30 + 30/30 − 27/30 = 5/30 = 1/6

Combine results: 1/2 ÷ 1/6 = 1/2 × 6 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Expression: (1/4 ÷ 1/2) ÷ (1/15 + 1 − 9/10)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Step 1: Solve the first bracket (1/4 ÷ 1/2)

⇒ 1/4 ÷ 1/2 = 1/4 × 2/1 = 2/4 = 1/2

⇒ Step 2: Solve the second bracket (1/15 + 1 − 9/10)

⇒ Find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the denominators 15 and 10, which is 30.

⇒ 1/15 = 2/30

⇒ 1 = 30/30

⇒ 9/10 = 27/30

⇒ (2/30 + 30/30 − 27/30) = (2 + 30 − 27) / 30 = 5/30 = 1/6

⇒ Step 3: Divide the result of the first bracket by the result of the second bracket

⇒ 1/2 ÷ 1/6 = 1/2 × 6/1

⇒ 6 / 2 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

⇒ (3/2 + 3/8)³ − (9/5 × 5/4)

⇒ Make denominators equal inside the bracket:

⇒ (12/8 + 3/8)³ − 9/4

⇒ Add the terms together inside the bracket:

⇒ (15/8)³ − 9/4

⇒ 3375/512 − 9/4

⇒ 3375/512 − (9 × 128)/(4 × 128)

⇒ 3375/512 − 1152/512

⇒ (3375 − 1152) / 512

⇒ 2223 / 512

⇒ Convert the final fraction back to a decimal:

⇒ 2223 ÷ 512 = 4.341796875

First bracket: LCM of 6 and 4 is 12 → (10 + 9)/12 = 19/12

question: Solve:(sqrt{7225}- sqrt{1225}) × ((1)/(5))
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Square roots of numbers ending in 25 follow a simple pattern: n × (n+1) followed by 25 gives a root of (n5).

√7225 → 72 = 8 × 9 ⇒ Root is 85.

√1225 → 12 = 3 × 4 ⇒ Root is 35.

⇒ (85 − 35) × 1/5

⇒ 50 ÷ 5 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(√7225 − √1225) × (1/5)

**Calculations:**

To calculate √7225:

We know that 80² = 6400 and 90² = 8100.

Since 7225 is between these and ends in 25, the square root must end in 5.

⇒ √7225 = 85

To calculate √1225:

We know that 30² = 900 and 40² = 1600.

Since 1225 is between these and ends in 25, the square root must end in 5.

⇒ √1225 = 35

Substituting the square root values back into the expression:

⇒ (85 − 35) × (1/5)

⇒ 50 × (1/5)

⇒ 50 ÷ 5

⇒ 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the standard order of operations: Brackets, Orders (powers and roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Square Root Shortcut for Ends in 25

For a perfect square ending in 25, remove the last two digits. Factor the remaining number as n × (n + 1). The square root will simply be n followed by 5.

question: 27³ + 10³ - 29³ + 246 is equal to:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the Digital Sum (DS) method to solve instantly.

DS of 27³ = 0; DS of 10³ = 1; DS of 29³ = 8; DS of 246 = 3.

DS of expression = 0 + 1 − 8 + 3 = −4. (Add 9 for positive DS) ⇒ 5.

Checking options, DS of −3460 = −(13) → −4 ⇒ 5, matching perfectly.

**∴ The correct answer is -3460.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

27³ + 10³ − 29³ + 246

**Calculation:**

⇒ 27³ = 27 × 27 × 27 = 19683

⇒ 10³ = 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000

⇒ 29³ = 29 × 29 × 29 = 24389

Substituting the values into the given expression:

⇒ 19683 + 1000 − 24389 + 246

⇒ 20683 − 24389 + 246

⇒ 20929 − 24389

⇒ −3460

**∴ The correct answer is -3460.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Digital Sum Method

The digital sum of a number is the single-digit value obtained by repeatedly adding its digits. It is highly useful in checking calculations because the digital sum of an expression equals the digital sum of its final answer. If a digital sum is negative, add 9 to it.

Unit Digit Concept

The unit digit of an expression can be determined by operating only on the unit digits of the numbers. For example, the unit digit of 27³ is the same as the unit digit of 7³, which is 3.

BODMAS Rule

Simplification should always follow the BODMAS order: Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

question: Solve: sqrt{(5 × 196 ÷ 14 + 25-4)}
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply BODMAS directly to evaluate the expression inside the root.

⇒ √(5 × 196 ÷ 14 + 25 − 4)

⇒ √(5 × 14 + 21)

⇒ √(70 + 21)

⇒ √91

**∴ The correct answer is √91.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

√(5 × 196 ÷ 14 + 25 − 4)

**Concept Used:**

BODMAS Rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Step 1: Perform division inside the bracket.

⇒ 196 ÷ 14 = 14

⇒ The expression becomes: √(5 × 14 + 25 − 4)

⇒ Step 2: Perform multiplication.

⇒ 5 × 14 = 70

⇒ The expression becomes: √(70 + 25 − 4)

⇒ Step 3: Perform addition and subtraction from left to right.

⇒ 70 + 25 = 95

⇒ 95 − 4 = 91

⇒ The final value is √91

**∴ The correct answer is √91.**

**__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It sets the order of mathematical operations: Brackets, Orders (roots/powers), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. Division is always calculated before multiplication.

subject: MATH
question: What is the value of sqrt{6+sqrt{6+sqrt{6+dots}}}
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For an infinite series of the form √(a + √(a + √(a + ...))), we find two consecutive integers whose product is a.

Here, a = 6, which can be factored into consecutive integers as 2 × 3.

Since the series has a positive (+) sign throughout, the answer will be the larger integer.

The larger integer between 2 and 3 is 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The infinite nested radical expression is √(6 + √(6 + √(6 + ...∞)))

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let x = √(6 + √(6 + √(6 + ...∞)))

⇒ Squaring both sides of the equation, we get:

⇒ x² = 6 + √(6 + √(6 + ...∞))

⇒ Since the expression goes to infinity, the repeating part is equal to x:

⇒ x² = 6 + x

⇒ x² − x − 6 = 0

⇒ x² − 3x + 2x − 6 = 0

⇒ x(x − 3) + 2(x − 3) = 0

⇒ (x − 3)(x + 2) = 0

⇒ x = 3 or x = −2

⇒ Since the value of a positive square root cannot be negative, we take x = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Infinite Nested Radical

For a series √(a − √(a − √(a − ...))), if a can be written as the product of two consecutive integers, the answer is the smaller integer. Example: √(6 − √(6 − ...)) = 2.

Multiplicative Infinite Nested Radical

For an infinite series under multiplication like √(a × √(a × √(a × ...))), the final value evaluates exactly to a. Example: √(6 × √(6 × ...)) = 6.

Non-Factorable Infinite Radical

If the term a cannot be factored into two consecutive integers, the exact value of √(a + √(a + ...)) is found using the direct formula (√(4a + 1) + 1) ÷ 2.

question: Evaluate sqrt{12 + sqrt{12 + sqrt{12 + ·s}}}
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For an infinite series of the form √(n + √(n + √(n + ...))), check if n is a product of two consecutive integers.

If n = a × (a + 1), then the answer is the larger integer (a + 1).

Here, the given number is 12.

12 can be factored into consecutive integers as 3 × 4.

Since the series has a positive (+) sign, the answer is the larger factor, which is 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The expression is √(12 + √(12 + √(12 + ...∞)))

**Method Used:**

Assume the given infinite series is equal to x, then substitute x back into the expression to form a quadratic equation.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let x = √(12 + √(12 + √(12 + ...∞)))

Since the series continues infinitely, the term inside the first square root is also equal to x:

⇒ x = √(12 + x)

Squaring both sides of the equation:

⇒ x² = 12 + x

⇒ x² − x − 12 = 0

Factorising the quadratic equation:

⇒ x² − 4x + 3x − 12 = 0

⇒ x(x − 4) + 3(x − 4) = 0

⇒ (x − 4)(x + 3) = 0

⇒ x = 4 or x = −3

Since the principal square root is always non-negative, x cannot be −3.

⇒ x = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Infinite Series with Subtraction

For √(n − √(n − √(n ...∞))), if n = a × (a+1), the answer is the smaller integer, a.

Infinite Series with Multiplication

For √(n × √(n × √(n ...∞))), the answer is always n.

Finite Series with Multiplication

For √(n × √(n × ... k times)), the exact formula used is n⁽²k − 1) ÷ 2k.

When Factors are not Consecutive Integers

For √(n + √(n + ...∞)), use the direct root formula: x = (√(4n+1) + 1) ÷ 2.
</p

Comparing Surds

question: Simplify: √50 + √18 - √8
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly extract perfect squares from the square roots:

⇒ √50 + √18 − √8

⇒ √(25 × 2) + √(9 × 2) − √(4 × 2)

⇒ 5√2 + 3√2 − 2√2 = 6√2

**∴ The correct answer is 6√2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: √50 + √18 − √8

**Method Used:**

Prime factorization of the numbers inside the roots to extract terms outside the square root.

**Calculations:**

⇒ √50 = √(2 × 5 × 5) = 5√2

⇒ √18 = √(2 × 3 × 3) = 3√2

⇒ √8 = √(2 × 2 × 2) = 2√2

Substitute these values back into the expression:

⇒ 5√2 + 3√2 − 2√2

Take √2 as common:

⇒ (5 + 3 − 2) × √2

⇒ 6√2

**∴ The correct answer is 6√2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Similar Surds

Surds which have the same irrational factor are called similar surds. Only similar surds can be added or subtracted. Example: 3√2 and 5√2 are similar surds.

Multiplication and Division of Surds

Unlike addition and subtraction, surds with the same order can be multiplied or divided regardless of their base. √a × √b = √(ab) and √a ÷ √b = √(a/b).

Simplifying Surds

To simplify a square root, find the largest perfect square factor of the number inside the root, and bring its square root outside. Example: √(x²y) = x√y.

Substituting these simplified values into the original expression:

⇒ 7√2 − 4√2 + 5√2

⇒ (7 − 4 + 5)√2

⇒ (3 + 5)√2

⇒ 8√2

question: Simplify: sqrt{(12+6sqrt{3) }}
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In surd square roots √(A + B), split B into 2 × a × b.

Here, 6√3 = 2 × 3 × √3. Let a = 3 and b = √3.

Check if a² + b² = A ⇒ 3² + (√3)² = 9 + 3 = 12. This matches perfectly!

So, the expression is exactly (a + b)² = (3 + √3)².

Taking the square root cancels the square, giving 3 + √3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 + √3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

√(12 + 6√3)

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us express the term inside the square root in the form of a perfect square.

⇒ The given expression is 12 + 6√3.

⇒ We can rewrite the middle term 6√3 as 2 × 3 × √3.

⇒ This implies a = 3 and b = √3 in the identity (a + b)².

⇒ Now, let us check a² + b²: 3² + (√3)² = 9 + 3 = 12.

⇒ So, 12 + 6√3 can be written as 3² + (√3)² + 2 × 3 × √3.

⇒ This perfectly matches the expansion of (3 + √3)².

⇒ Therefore, √(12 + 6√3) = √((3 + √3)²).

⇒ The square root and square cancel each other out.

⇒ Simplification gives 3 + √3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 + √3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Surds

To find the square root of a mixed surd A + √B, assume it equals √x + √y. Squaring both sides gives A + √B = x + y + 2√(xy). Then equate rational and irrational parts to solve for x and y.

Algebraic Identities

The identities (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab are crucial. If the given expression was √(12 − 6√3), the simplified answer would be 3 − √3.

Conjugate Surds

When surds appear in the denominator, multiply both numerator and denominator by the conjugate (changing the middle sign) to rationalise it: 1 ÷ (a + √b) × (a − √b) ÷ (a − √b).
</p

question: Find the value of x in given equation: frac{sqrt{3+x}+sqrt{3-x}}{sqrt{3+x}-sqrt{3-x}} = 2
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply Componendo and Dividendo rule directly:

⇒ [√(3+x)] / [√(3−x)] = (2+1) / (2−1)

⇒ [√(3+x)] / [√(3−x)] = 3

Squaring both sides:

⇒ (3+x) / (3−x) = 9 ⇒ 3 + x = 27 − 9x ⇒ 10x = 24 ⇒ x = 12/5

**∴ The correct answer is 12/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

[√(3+x) + √(3−x)] / [√(3+x) − √(3−x)] = 2

**Method Used: Cross-multiplication**

⇒ √(3+x) + √(3−x) = 2 × [√(3+x) − √(3−x)]

⇒ √(3+x) + √(3−x) = 2√(3+x) − 2√(3−x)

⇒ √(3−x) + 2√(3−x) = 2√(3+x) − √(3+x)

⇒ 3√(3−x) = √(3+x)

Squaring both sides:

⇒ [3√(3−x)]² = [√(3+x)]²

⇒ 9 × (3 − x) = 3 + x

⇒ 27 − 9x = 3 + x

⇒ 27 − 3 = x + 9x

⇒ 24 = 10x

⇒ x = 24 / 10 = 12/5

**∴ The correct answer is 12/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Componendo and Dividendo

If a/b = c/d, then by this rule, (a+b) / (a−b) = (c+d) / (c−d). It quickly reduces complex fractions involving sums and differences of the same terms.

Squaring Equations

When dealing with expressions inside a square root (√), squaring both sides is the primary method to eliminate the root. Always verify roots back into the original equation to identify any extraneous solutions.

Cross Multiplication

For an equation of the form A/B = C/D, cross multiplying yields A × D = B × C, converting fractions into a simple linear expression.
</p

question: Find the value of x in the given equation: frac{sqrt{7+x}+sqrt{7-x}}{sqrt{7+x}-sqrt{7-x}} = 4
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the Componendo and Dividendo rule twice for quick results:

⇒ √(7+x) / √(7−x) = (4 + 1) / (4 − 1) = 5 / 3

Squaring both sides gives: (7 + x) / (7 − x) = 25 / 9

Applying the rule again: 7 / x = (25 + 9) / (25 − 9) = 34 / 16 = 17 / 8

⇒ x = (7 × 8) / 17 = 56/17

**∴ The correct answer is 56/17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

[ √(7+x) + √(7−x) ] / [ √(7+x) − √(7−x) ] = 4

**Formula Used:**

Componendo and Dividendo: If a / b = c / d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d)

**Calculations:**

Applying Componendo and Dividendo to the given equation:

⇒ [ (√(7+x) + √(7−x)) + (√(7+x) − √(7−x)) ] / [ (√(7+x) + √(7−x)) − (√(7+x) − √(7−x)) ] = (4 + 1) / (4 − 1)

⇒ 2√(7+x) / 2√(7−x) = 5 / 3

⇒ √(7+x) / √(7−x) = 5 / 3

Squaring both sides:

⇒ (7 + x) / (7 − x) = 25 / 9

Cross-multiplying to solve for x:

⇒ 9 × (7 + x) = 25 × (7 − x)

⇒ 63 + 9x = 175 − 25x

⇒ 9x + 25x = 175 − 63

⇒ 34x = 112

⇒ x = 112 / 34

⇒ x = 56 / 17

**∴ The correct answer is 56/17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Componendo and Dividendo

If a / b = c / d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This property is extremely useful for simplifying rational expressions involving conjugate pairs.

Invertendo Property

If two ratios are equal, i.e., a / b = c / d, then their inverse ratios are also equal: b / a = d / c.

Alternendo Property

If a / b = c / d, then by alternating the consequent of the first and the antecedent of the second, a / c = b / d.

question: Evaluate the expression:((1)/(3-sqrt{8)}) - ((1)/(sqrt{8)-sqrt{7}}) + ((1)/(sqrt{7)-sqrt{6}}) - ((1)/(sqrt{6)-sqrt{5}}) + ((1)/(sqrt{5)-2}) = ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rewrite 3 as √9 and 2 as √4 to see the continuous pattern.

Rationalizing 1/(√a − √b) gives √a + √b when a − b = 1.

The given expression evaluates to: (√9 + √8) − (√8 + √7) + (√7 + √6) − (√6 + √5) + (√5 + √4)

All intermediate terms cancel out, leaving only the first and last parts: √9 + √4 = 3 + 2 = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

1/(3 − √8) − 1/(√8 − √7) + 1/(√7 − √6) − 1/(√6 − √5) + 1/(√5 − 2)

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Rationalize the first term:

⇒ 1/(3 − √8) = (3 + √8) / (3² − (√8)²) = (3 + √8) / (9 − 8) = 3 + √8

⇒ Rationalize the second term:

⇒ 1/(√8 − √7) = (√8 + √7) / ((√8)² − (√7)²) = (√8 + √7) / (8 − 7) = √8 + √7

⇒ Rationalize the third term:

⇒ 1/(√7 − √6) = (√7 + √6) / (7 − 6) = √7 + √6

⇒ Rationalize the fourth term:

⇒ 1/(√6 − √5) = (√6 + √5) / (6 − 5) = √6 + √5

⇒ Rationalize the fifth term:

⇒ 1/(√5 − 2) = (√5 + 2) / ((√5)² − 2²) = (√5 + 2) / (5 − 4) = √5 + 2

⇒ Substitute all these simplified values back into the original expression:

⇒ (3 + √8) − (√8 + √7) + (√7 + √6) − (√6 + √5) + (√5 + 2)

⇒ Expand by applying the minus signs:

⇒ 3 + √8 − √8 − √7 + √7 + √6 − √6 − √5 + √5 + 2

⇒ Cancel out the opposite matching pairs:

⇒ 3 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 2 = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rationalization of Surds

To remove a square root surd from the denominator, multiply both the numerator and denominator by its conjugate. The conjugate of (√a − √b) is (√a + √b).

Difference of Squares Formula

The standard algebraic identity (x − y)(x + y) = x² − y² is widely applied during rationalization to eliminate square root symbols entirely from denominators.

Continuous Series Simplification

When solving a continuous sequence of surd fractions, locating patterns like differences of 1 will allow quick cancellation of intermediate terms, drastically reducing calculation time.
</p

question: Convert 3.375 into a fraction in simplest form.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Break the given decimal into its integer and fractional parts:

3.375 = 3 + 0.375

Recall the standard decimal conversion for eighths: 0.375 = 3/8

⇒ 3.375 = 3 + 3/8 = (3 × 8 + 3) ÷ 8

⇒ 3.375 = 27/8

**∴ The correct answer is 27/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Decimal value = 3.375

**Method Used:**

To convert a decimal to a fraction, write the entire number without the decimal point over 1 followed by as many zeros as there are decimal places, and then simplify.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since 3.375 has 3 decimal places, we write it over 1000.

⇒ 3.375 = 3375 / 1000

⇒ To simplify, divide both the numerator and denominator by 25:

⇒ Numerator: 3375 ÷ 25 = 135

⇒ Denominator: 1000 ÷ 25 = 40

⇒ The fraction becomes 135 / 40.

⇒ Now, divide both by 5 to reduce it further:

⇒ Numerator: 135 ÷ 5 = 27

⇒ Denominator: 40 ÷ 5 = 8

⇒ The fraction in its simplest form is 27/8.

**∴ The correct answer is 27/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Common Decimal Equivalents

Memorizing common base-8 fractions speeds up calculations in exams: 1/8 = 0.125, 3/8 = 0.375, 5/8 = 0.625, and 7/8 = 0.875.

Proper vs Improper Fractions

A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator (e.g., 3/8). An improper fraction has a numerator greater than or equal to its denominator (e.g., 27/8). Mixed numbers can be formed directly from improper fractions.

Converting Repeating Decimals

For non-terminating but repeating decimals, place the repeating digits over an equal number of 9s instead of 10s. Example: 0.444... = 4/9, and 0.3636... = 36/99 = 4/11.

question: Multiply 0.45 by 0.6 and express the result as a decimal.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Step 1: Ignore the decimals and multiply the integers directly: 45 × 6 = 270.

Step 2: Count the total number of decimal places in the given numbers: 2 (in 0.45) + 1 (in 0.6) = 3 decimal places.

Step 3: Place the decimal point 3 positions from the right in the product: 0.270 = 0.27.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The expression to simplify is 0.45 × 0.6

**Method Used:**

Convert the decimal numbers into fractions, multiply the numerators and denominators, and then convert the result back to a decimal.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 0.45 = 45 / 100

⇒ 0.6 = 6 / 10

⇒ 0.45 × 0.6 = (45 / 100) × (6 / 10)

⇒ 0.45 × 0.6 = (45 × 6) / (100 × 10)

⇒ 0.45 × 0.6 = 270 / 1000

⇒ 0.45 × 0.6 = 27 / 100

⇒ 0.45 × 0.6 = 0.27

**∴ The correct answer is 0.27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Multiplication of Decimals

When multiplying decimal numbers, multiply them exactly as if they are whole numbers. The number of decimal places in the final product will always be equal to the total sum of the decimal places present in the original factors.

Converting Decimals to Fractions

To convert a decimal to a fraction, write the decimal number without the point as the numerator. For the denominator, write 1 followed by as many zeros as there are decimal places in the original number (e.g., 0.85 = 85/100).

BODMAS Rule

When simplifying mathematical expressions containing multiple operations, always follow the BODMAS sequence: Bracket, Order (Powers/Roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.
</p

question: What is the result of (0.5³ + 0.1³ – 0.6³) ÷ (3×0.5×0.1×0.6)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

Here, a = 0.5, b = 0.1, and c = −0.6, which gives a + b + c = 0.5 + 0.1 − 0.6 = 0.

The numerator becomes 3 × 0.5 × 0.1 × (−0.6).

Expression = [3 × 0.5 × 0.1 × (−0.6)] ÷ (3 × 0.5 × 0.1 × 0.6).

All values cancel out leaving exactly −1.

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(0.5³ + 0.1³ − 0.6³) ÷ (3 × 0.5 × 0.1 × 0.6)

**Formula Used:**

If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let a = 0.5, b = 0.1, and c = −0.6

⇒ Sum of terms: a + b + c = 0.5 + 0.1 + (−0.6) = 0.6 − 0.6 = 0

⇒ Since a + b + c = 0, the numerator a³ + b³ + c³ directly equals 3abc.

⇒ Numerator = 3 × 0.5 × 0.1 × (−0.6)

⇒ Substitute this evaluated numerator back into the full expression.

⇒ Expression = [3 × 0.5 × 0.1 × (−0.6)] ÷ (3 × 0.5 × 0.1 × 0.6)

⇒ Cancel out the common terms (3 × 0.5 × 0.1) from both the numerator and the denominator.

⇒ Expression = (−0.6) ÷ 0.6

⇒ Expression = −1

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Identity for Cubes

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

Sum of Two Cubes

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)

Difference of Two Cubes

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

**Evaluate: **

(sqrt{11} + sqrt{7})² - (sqrt{11} - sqrt{7})²
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know the direct algebraic identity: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab

Here, let a = √11 and b = √7

⇒ Result = 4 × √11 × √7

⇒ Result = 4√77

**∴ The correct answer is 4√77.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: (√11 + √7)² − (√11 − √7)²

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

**Calculations:**

⇒ Expand the first term: (√11 + √7)² = (√11)² + (√7)² + 2 × √11 × √7

⇒ (√11 + √7)² = 11 + 7 + 2√77 = 18 + 2√77

⇒ Expand the second term: (√11 − √7)² = (√11)² + (√7)² − 2 × √11 × √7

⇒ (√11 − √7)² = 11 + 7 − 2√77 = 18 − 2√77

⇒ Subtract the second expression from the first: (18 + 2√77) − (18 − 2√77)

⇒ 18 + 2√77 − 18 + 2√77

⇒ 4√77

**∴ The correct answer is 4√77.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Identity

Another useful variation is the sum of the squares: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²).

Difference of Squares

A very commonly used identity in simplification is a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).

Square Root Properties

For any positive numbers x and y, the product of their square roots is √x × √y = √(xy) and squaring a root gives (√x)² = x.
</p

Let each 1/3 segment of the journey be the LCM of the given speeds (40, 50, and 60) = 600 km.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Average Speed = 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7930860355f6178154b6be0b25ee7af06a1257355ef2dfaae9f46d7ff39eb67a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average Speed = (3 × 40 × 50 × 60) ÷ (40 × 50 + 50 × 60 + 60 × 40)

⇒ Average Speed = 360000 ÷ (2000 + 3000 + 2400)

⇒ Average Speed = 360000 ÷ 7400

⇒ Average Speed = 1800 ÷ 37

⇒ Average Speed ≈ 48.648 km/h

⇒ Rounding off to two decimal places, we get 48.65 km/h.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for 2 Equal Distances

When a body travels two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed over the entire journey is given by 2xy ÷ (x + y).

General Average Speed Concept

When distances are unequal, the average speed is strictly calculated by dividing the Total Distance Travelled by the Total Time Taken.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the same direction at speeds x and y, their relative speed is |x − y|. If they move in opposite directions, their relative speed is (x + y).

When total time (T) to travel a distance (D) back and forth with speeds S₁ and S₂ is given, use the direct formula:

Speed returning from school (v₂) = 2.6 km/hr

Total Time = (Distance ÷ v₁) + (Distance ÷ v₂)

 
 House

 3.8 km/hr

 2.6 km/hr Total Time = 5 hours 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the distance between his house and school be D km.

⇒ Total time = Time taken to go + Time taken to return

⇒ (D ÷ 3.8) + (D ÷ 2.6) = 5

When a person travels equal distances at two different speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed for the complete journey is calculated using the formula: Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

⇒ Taking the LCM of denominators (30, 45, and 90), which is 90:

⇒ Total Time = (3d + 2d + d) ÷ 90 = 6d ÷ 90 = d ÷ 15 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 3d ÷ (d ÷ 15)

⇒ Average Speed = 3 × 15 = 45 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 45 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

When two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, the average speed can directly be calculated using the formula: 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

When three equal distances are covered at speeds x, y, and z, the average speed formula expands to: 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

General Average Speed Formula

For unequal distance splits, the direct formulas do not apply. Always use the fundamental definition: Average Speed = Total Distance Covered ÷ Total Time Taken.
</p

question: A boat goes 27 km upstream and 33 km downstream in 6 hours. In the same time it can go 36 km upstream and 22 km downstream. How much time will it take to go 36 km upstream and 44 km downstream?
solution:
**Given:**

27km upstream and 33km downstream = 6 hours

36km upstream and 22km downstream = 6 hours

**Formula:**

Speed of boat = a kmph and Speed of stream = b kmph

Speed of upstream = (a - b) kmph

Speed of downstream = (a + b) kmph

**Calculation:**

⇒ 33/(a + b) + 27/(a - b) = 6

⇒ 22/(a + b) + 36/(a - b) = 6

Then,

⇒ 33/(a + b) + 27/(a - b) = 22/(a + b) + 36/(a - b)

⇒ 11/(a + b) = 9/(a - b) 

⇒ 11a - 11b = 9a + 9b

⇒ 2a = 20b

⇒ a = 10b

Then,

⇒ 33/(10b + b) + 27/(10b - b) = 6

⇒ 3/b + 3/b = 6

⇒ b = 1

⇒ a = 10

Speed downstream = 10 + 1 = 11 kmph

Speed upstream = 10 - 1 = 9 kmph

Then,

⇒ ? = 44/11 + 36/9 

⇒ ? = 4 + 4

⇒ ? = 8

**∴ it will take 8 hours to go 36 km upstream and 44 km downstream.**

question: A boat can go 5 km upstream and 7(1)/(2) km downstream in 45 minutes. It can also go 5 km downstream and 2.5 km Upstream in 25 minutes. How much time (in minutes) will it take to go 6 km downstream?
solution:
**Given:**

The boat takes 45 mins to go 5 km upstream and 7.5 km downstream.

The boat takes 25 mins to go 5 km downstream and 2.5 km upstream

**Concept used:**

When going downstream, the speed of the boat and the flow of the river are added to calculate the net speed.

When going upstream, we take the difference between the speed of the boat and the flow of the river as the net speed. 

Distance = Time × Speed

Elimination method for solving linear equations

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the boat and the flow of the riven be B & R respectively. (in Kilometer per hours i.e. kmph)

Now,

Upstream speed = B - R = 1/P (suppose)

Downstream speed = B + R = 1/Q (suppose)

45 mins = 3/4 hour

25 mins = 5/12 hour

According to the question,

5/(B - R) + 7.5/(B + R) = 3/4

⇒ 5P + 7.5Q = 3/4 ....(1)

According to the question,

2.5/(B - R) + 5/(B + R) = 5/12

⇒ 2.5P + 5Q = 5/12 ....(2)

Solving (1) & (2) we get,

Q = 1/30 i.e. 1/(B + R) = 30

Now,

B + R = 30

The net speed during downstream = 30kmph

Now,

Time taken to cover 6km downstream

⇒ 6/30 hour

⇒ 1/5 hour

⇒ 1/5 × 60 mins

⇒ 12 mins

**∴ 12 mins will it take to go 6 km downstream.**

question: Jehangir had to cover a distance of 90 km in an hour. During the first 25 minutes he travelled at a speed of 15.2 metres per second. How many metres did Jehangir cover per second during the remaining period to reach his destination just on time?
solution:
**Given data:**

Total distance = 90 km = 90000 metres

Total time = 1 hour = 3600 seconds

Time spent travelling at 15.2 m/s = 25 minutes = 1500 seconds

Speed during first 25 minutes = 15.2 m/s

 

**Concept to be used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Solution:**

Distance covered in first 25 minutes = Speed × Time

⇒ 15.2 m/s × 1500 s = 22800 metres

Remaining distance to be covered = Total distance - Distance covered in first 25 min

⇒ 90000 m - 22800 m = 67200 metres

Remaining time = Total time - Time spent in first 25 min

⇒ 3600 s - 1500 s = 2100 seconds

Speed during remaining time = Remaining distance / Remaining time

⇒ 67200 m / 2100 s = 32 m/s

**Therefore, Jehangir should travel at a speed of 32 m/s for the remaining time to reach his destination on time.**

question: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. How much time (in hours) will it take to cover a distance of 105 km in downstream and in coming back?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Time = Distance ÷ (Speed of Boat + Speed of Stream) + Distance ÷ (Speed of Boat − Speed of Stream)

Total Time = 105 ÷ (18 + 3) + 105 ÷ (18 − 3)

Total Time = 105 ÷ 21 + 105 ÷ 15

Total Time = 5 + 7 = 12 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat in still water (u) = 18 km/h

Speed of stream (v) = 3 km/h

Distance covered each way (D) = 105 km

**Formula Used:**

Downstream Speed (Dₛ) = u + v

Upstream Speed (Uₛ) = u − v

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7d1fd925dee30df94bba02ef01b3842b98a934d819db47bdc842c0a9e10a2025.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream Speed (Dₛ) = 18 + 3 = 21 km/h

⇒ Upstream Speed (Uₛ) = 18 − 3 = 15 km/h

⇒ Time taken downstream = 105 ÷ 21 = 5 hours

⇒ Time taken upstream = 105 ÷ 15 = 7 hours

⇒ Total Time = 5 + 7 = 12 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat and Stream from Downstream / Upstream

If downstream speed is Dₛ and upstream speed is Uₛ, then Speed of Boat = (Dₛ + Uₛ) ÷ 2, and Speed of Stream = (Dₛ − Uₛ) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for a Round Trip

For a journey traveling the same distance downstream and upstream, Average Speed = (Dₛ × Uₛ) ÷ Speed of Boat in still water.

Total Time Formula

If total time for a round trip is T, then Total Distance = (T × (u² − v²)) ÷ (2 × u), where u is boat speed and v is stream speed.
</p

subject: MATH
question: A boat can go 54 km upstream in 6 hours. If the speed of the stream is 4.8 km/h, then how much time (in hours) will the boat take to cover a distance of 279 km downstream?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Upstream speed (U) = 54 ÷ 6 = 9 km/h.

Downstream speed (D) = U + 2 × Stream speed = 9 + 2 × 4.8 = 18.6 km/h.

Time downstream = Distance ÷ D = 279 ÷ 18.6 = 15 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance upstream = 54 km

Time upstream = 6 hours

Speed of the stream (S) = 4.8 km/h

Distance downstream = 279 km

**Formula Used:**

Upstream speed (U) = Boat speed (B) − Stream speed (S)

Downstream speed (D) = Boat speed (B) + Stream speed (S)

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fab3347d781c23af0b60cb9a2e8794d8240cf8a3d7329dd05be3f84342876313.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Upstream speed (U) = 54 ÷ 6 = 9 km/h

⇒ U = B − S

⇒ 9 = B − 4.8

⇒ B = 9 + 4.8 = 13.8 km/h

⇒ Downstream speed (D) = B + S = 13.8 + 4.8 = 18.6 km/h

⇒ Time downstream = Distance ÷ Downstream speed

⇒ Time downstream = 279 ÷ 18.6 = 15 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 15 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Upstream and Downstream Speeds

When a boat travels against the flow of the river, it moves upstream (U = B − S). When it travels with the flow, it moves downstream (D = B + S).

Speed of Boat and Stream

If upstream speed (U) and downstream speed (D) are given: Speed of boat in still water (B) = (D + U) ÷ 2. Speed of stream (S) = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Distance, Speed and Time

The fundamental relation is Distance = Speed × Time. For river problems, always determine the effective speed (downstream or upstream) first.
</p

question: A boatman goes 2 km against the current of the stream in 1 hour and goes 1 km along with the current in 10 minutes. How long will it take to go 6 km in stationary water?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Upstream speed = 2 km/h

Downstream speed = 1 km × (60 ÷ 10) = 6 km/h

Boat speed in still water = (Downstream speed + Upstream speed) ÷ 2 = (6 + 2) ÷ 2 = 4 km/h

Time to cover 6 km = Distance ÷ Speed = 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 hr = 1 hr 30 min

**∴ The correct answer is 1 hr 30 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance upstream = 2 km

Time upstream = 1 hour

Distance downstream = 1 km

Time downstream = 10 minutes = 10 ÷ 60 hour = 1/6 hour

**Formula Used:**

Upstream Speed (U) = Distance ÷ Time

Downstream Speed (D) = Distance ÷ Time

Speed of Boat in Still Water (V) = (D + U) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59707dc3411f383552a85a19521af22aa3b9ed35c67f64215ffd7a6d819e721e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Upstream Speed (U) = 2 ÷ 1 = 2 km/h

⇒ Downstream Speed (D) = 1 ÷ (1/6) = 6 km/h

⇒ Speed of Boat in Still Water (V) = (6 + 2) ÷ 2

⇒ V = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 km/h

⇒ Time required to travel 6 km in still water = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Time = 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 hours

⇒ 1.5 hours = 1 hour + 0.5 hour = 1 hr 30 min

**∴ The correct answer is 1 hr 30 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Stream

The speed of the current can be found by taking half the difference of the downstream and upstream speeds: Speed of Stream = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Effective Speed

When moving downstream, the flow of the river assists the boat, hence speeds are added (Boat + Stream). When moving upstream, the flow resists the boat, hence speeds are subtracted (Boat − Stream).
</p

Relative Speed

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, relative speed = a − b. When moving in opposite directions, relative speed = a + b.

When equal distances are covered at speeds a and b, Average Speed = (2 × a × b) ÷ (a + b). For varying distances, Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

question: In a circular race of 840 m, A and B start running in the same direction at the same time from the same point at the speeds of 6 m/s and 12 m/s, respectively. After how much time will they meet next?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two persons run in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their speeds.

Relative speed = 12 − 6 = 6 m/s.

Time to meet next = Track length ÷ Relative speed.

Time = 840 ÷ 6 = 140 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 140 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b79b7c70c3142a9947d29865cd34de0c1710c29b6dd3c67e79a8672f9be1b85c.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ Total length of the circular track = 840 m

⇒ Speed of runner A = 6 m/s

⇒ Speed of runner B = 12 m/s

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Time taken to meet = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Since both A and B are running in the same direction, their relative speed will be the difference between their speeds.

⇒ Relative Speed = Speed of B − Speed of A

⇒ Relative Speed = 12 − 6 = 6 m/s

⇒ Time taken to meet next = 840 ÷ 6

⇒ Time = 140 s

**∴ The correct answer is 140 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting Anywhere on Track (First Time)

Time = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed. If moving in the same direction, RS = |S₁ − S₂|. If opposite, RS = S₁ + S₂.

Meeting at the Starting Point (First Time)

Time = LCM of the individual times taken to complete one full round = LCM(L÷S₁, L÷S₂).

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

If the ratio of their speeds is a : b (in simplest form), they meet at |a − b| distinct points if moving in the same direction, and (a + b) points if moving in opposite directions.
</p

solution:

Relative speed (same direction) = 108 − 90 = 18 km/h

Time to meet = Distance ÷ Relative speed

Time to meet = 1635 ÷ 5 = 327 s

**∴ The correct answer is 327 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the circular track = 1635 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c9ae52f2f06fd1987c4e94a36dbf802929c1466ca3c897098f772c34b395131f.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time to meet for the first time = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed

Relative speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of Varun = 90 × (5/18) = 25 m/s

⇒ Speed of Sandeep = 108 × (5/18) = 30 m/s

⇒ Relative speed = 30 − 25 = 5 m/s

⇒ Time to meet = 1635 ÷ 5 = 327 s

**∴ The correct answer is 327 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting for the first time anywhere on the track

When moving in the same direction: Time = Distance ÷ (S₁ − S₂). When moving in opposite directions: Time = Distance ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Meeting at the starting point

The time taken to meet at the starting point for the first time is the LCM of the times taken by each individual to complete one full round.

Relative Speed

Relative speed is the speed of a moving object with respect to another. If they move in the same direction, speeds subtract; if opposite, speeds add.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
</p

subject: MATH
question: M and N walk along a circular track. They start at 5:00 a.m. from the same point in the opposite directions. M and N walk at a speed of 5 rounds per hour and 2 rounds per hour, respectively. How many times will they cross each other before 6.30 a.m. on the same day?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When bodies move in opposite directions on a circular track, they cross each other at a frequency equal to the sum of their speeds in rounds per unit time.

Relative speed = 5 + 2 = 7 rounds per hour.

This means they cross each other 7 times every hour.

Total time from 5:00 a.m. to 6:30 a.m. = 1.5 hours.

Total crossings = 7 × 1.5 = 10.5 crossings.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of M = 5 rounds/hr

Speed of N = 2 rounds/hr

Time interval = 5:00 a.m. to 6:30 a.m. = 1.5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed (Opposite direction) = Speed₁ + Speed₂

Total Crossings = Relative Speed × Total Time

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/58ad5c5b2300645c8384014a65f1ffbbe54b8621f6a764505a8b6d3ad6db460a.png] 

⇒ Relative speed = 5 + 2 = 7 rounds/hr

⇒ This means M and N jointly cover 7 complete laps of the track in 1 hour.

⇒ Hence, they cross each other 7 times in 1 hour.

⇒ In 1.5 hours, relative laps completed = 7 × 1.5 = 10.5 laps.

⇒ Since a crossing occurs for every fully completed relative lap, we take the integer value.

⇒ Number of times they completely cross each other = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meetings in Opposite Directions

When moving in opposite directions, the frequency of meetings per unit time is the sum of their individual speeds (rounds per unit time): S₁ + S₂.

Meetings in Same Direction

When moving in the same direction, the frequency of meetings per unit time is the difference of their individual speeds: |S₁ − S₂|.

Meeting at the Starting Point

Regardless of the direction, the time taken to meet for the first time at the starting point is the LCM of the individual times taken by each person to complete one full round.
</p

When two persons run in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Speed of P = 10 m/s

Speed of Q = 8 m/s

Length of the track (Total Distance) = 1620 m

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 10 + 8

⇒ Relative Speed = 18 m/s

⇒ Time taken to meet = 1620 ÷ 18

⇒ Time taken to meet = 90 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 90 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (v₁ + v₂).

Time to Meet at the Starting Point

Distinct Meeting Points

If two persons run at speeds 'a' and 'b' (where a and b are co-prime integers), they meet at (a + b) distinct points if moving in opposite directions, and |a − b| distinct points if moving in the same direction.
</p

question: Arvind and Chetan started running simultaneously from the same point in the same direction on a circular track of length 210 m. If Arvind takes 180 seconds to complete one round, and Chetan takes 420 seconds to complete one round, after how much time will they meet for the first time at the starting point on the track?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by Arvind to complete one round = 180 seconds = 3 minutes.

Time taken by Chetan to complete one round = 420 seconds = 7 minutes.

To find the time they meet for the first time at the starting point, we calculate the LCM of their individual lap times.

Meeting time = LCM(3, 7) = 21 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 21 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of circular track = 210 m

Time taken by Arvind (T₁) = 180 seconds

Time taken by Chetan (T₂) = 420 seconds

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d3f3d0dadcdbfb6f2f5ebccd64d5bb528d1c478001af304c84d8ffdbcc9c5153.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time to meet for the first time at the starting point = LCM of individual times taken to complete one round.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 180 = 2² × 3² × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 420 = 2² × 3 × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM(180, 420) = 2² × 3² × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM(180, 420) = 4 × 9 × 5 × 7 = 1260 seconds

⇒ Convert total seconds into minutes = 1260 ÷ 60

⇒ Time to meet = 21 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 21 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting First Time at Starting Point

When multiple people start from the same point simultaneously, they meet again at the starting point exactly at the LCM of the times taken by each to complete one full round independently.

Meeting First Time Anywhere on Track

If running in the same direction, Time to meet = Track Length ÷ (S₁ − S₂). If running in opposite directions, Time to meet = Track Length ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

If the ratio of their speeds is a : b in its simplest form, they will meet at (a − b) distinct points if running in the same direction, and at (a + b) distinct points if running in opposite directions.
</p

subject: MATH
question: Seema walks around a circular field at the rate of 3 rounds per hour, while Priya runs around it at the rate of 8 rounds per hour. They start in the same direction from the same point at 11:54 PM. They shall first cross each other at:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in the same direction = 8 − 3 = 5 rounds per hour.

This means Priya gains 5 complete rounds over Seema in 60 minutes.

They will cross each other when Priya gains exactly 1 complete round.

Time to gain 1 round = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 minutes.

Crossing time = 11:54 p.m. + 12 minutes = 12:06 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 12:06 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8598969b60a14b0eabd910dcbb69243baeb6e532e4055ce167129b3f1b4ec37f.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ Speed of Seema = 3 rounds/hr

⇒ Speed of Priya = 8 rounds/hr

⇒ Starting time = 11:54 p.m.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

⇒ Time to cross for the first time = 1 round distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since they are moving in the same direction, relative speed = 8 − 3 = 5 rounds/hr

⇒ They cross each other when the faster person (Priya) covers exactly 1 more round than the slower person (Seema).

⇒ Time taken to gain 1 round = 1 ÷ 5 hours

⇒ Time taken in minutes = (1/5) × 60 = 12 minutes

⇒ Crossing time = 11:54 p.m. + 12 minutes

⇒ 11:54 p.m. + 6 minutes = 12:00 a.m. (Midnight)

⇒ 12:00 a.m. + 6 minutes = 12:06 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 12:06 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circular Motion (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction on a circular track, the time taken to meet for the first time anywhere on the track is calculated as Track Length ÷ (Speed₁ − Speed₂).

Circular Motion (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed increases. The time taken to meet for the first time is Track Length ÷ (Speed₁ + Speed₂).

Meeting at the Starting Point

The time taken for both runners to meet exactly at the starting point is the LCM (Least Common Multiple) of the individual times taken by each to complete one full round.

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

If the ratio of their speeds is a:b (in simplest form), they will meet at exactly (a − b) distinct points if running in the same direction, and at (a + b) distinct points if running in opposite directions.
</p
