question: In a circular race of 1600 m in length, Bhaskar and Vinay start with speeds of 27 km/h and 45 km/h starting at the same time from the same point. When will they meet for the first time on the track when running in the opposite directions and the same direction, respectively?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speeds in m/s: Bhaskar = 27 × 5/18 = 7.5 m/s, Vinay = 45 × 5/18 = 12.5 m/s.

Relative speed (Opposite) = 7.5 + 12.5 = 20 m/s ⇒ Time = 1600 ÷ 20 = 80 s = 1 minute 20 seconds.

Relative speed (Same) = 12.5 − 7.5 = 5 m/s ⇒ Time = 1600 ÷ 5 = 320 s = 5 minutes 20 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 minute 20 seconds and 5 minutes 20 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the track = 1600 m

Speed of Bhaskar = 27 km/h

Speed of Vinay = 45 km/h

**Formulas Used:**

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × 5/18

Time to meet (opposite direction) = Distance ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

Time to meet (same direction) = Distance ÷ |S₁ − S₂|

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5054ecff9576e91156f6419e3fd8368b136d003d0114df6cde0187fe93d7df79.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of Bhaskar (S₁) = 27 × 5/18 = 7.5 m/s

⇒ Speed of Vinay (S₂) = 45 × 5/18 = 12.5 m/s

⇒ **Case 1: Running in opposite directions**

⇒ Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂ = 7.5 + 12.5 = 20 m/s

⇒ Time taken to meet = 1600 ÷ 20 = 80 seconds = 1 minute 20 seconds

⇒ **Case 2: Running in the same direction**

⇒ Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂| = 12.5 − 7.5 = 5 m/s

⇒ Time taken to meet = 1600 ÷ 5 = 320 seconds = 5 minutes 20 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 1 minute 20 seconds and 5 minutes 20 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting at the Starting Point

The time taken to meet at the starting point for the first time is the LCM of the times taken by each person to complete one full round independently: LCM(T₁, T₂).

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

If the ratio of their speeds is a : b (in its simplest form), they will meet at (a + b) distinct points when running in opposite directions, and at |a − b| distinct points when running in the same direction.

First Meeting Anywhere on Track

For meeting anywhere on the track for the very first time, use the relative speed directly. Opposite direction relative speed = S₁ + S₂ | Same direction relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|.
</p

⇒ 120/(x +y) = 30 - 24

⇒ (x +y) = 20 .......eq(4)

Solving both eq(3) and eq(4), we get:

question: A train is to cover 370 km at a uniform speed. After running 100 km, the train could run at a speed 5 km/h less than its normal speed due to some technical fault. The train got delayed by 36 minutes. What is the normal speed of the train, in km/h?
solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered by the train = 370 km 

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance/Speed

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the train = x km/h

As per the question;

[100/x + 270/(x - 5)] - 370/x = 36/60 

⇒270/(x - 5) - 270/x = 3/5

⇒ 1/(x - 5) - 1/x = 1/450

⇒ [x - (x - 5)]/(x - 5)x = 1/450

⇒ 5/(x - 5)x = 1/450

⇒ 5 × 450 = x² - 5x 

⇒ x2 - 5x - 2250 = 0

⇒x2 - 50x + 45x - 2250 = 0 

⇒ x(x - 50) + 45(x - 50) = 0

⇒ (x + 45)(x - 50) = 0

⇒ x ≠ 45, x = 50

**∴ The required speed of the train = 50 km/h**

⇒ D = (3 × 60) ÷ 5

⇒ D = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km.**

Inverse Relation of Speed and Time

When the distance is constant, Speed and Time are inversely proportional. A ratio of speeds = a : b means the ratio of time taken will be = b : a.

Average Speed (Same Distance)

If equal distances are covered at two different speeds S₁ and S₂, then the Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

If two bodies move in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

question: Two trains P and Q start from stations S and T towards each other. Train P takes 4 hours 48 minutes and train Q takes 3 hours 20 minutes to reach T and S, respectively, after they meet. If the speed of train P is 45 km/h, what is the speed of train Q?
solution:

After meeting, trains P and Q complete their journey in 4 hours 48 minutes and 3 hours 20 minutes respectively

After meeting each other, the time required by the trains to reach the destination

⇒ (45)/(S₂) = (5)/(6)

question: Places A and B are 20 km apart on the highway. A car starts from A and another from B at the same time. If the cars travel in the same direction at different speeds, they meet in one hour. solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in same direction (S₁ − S₂) = Distance ÷ Time = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 km/h

Relative speed in opposite direction (S₁ + S₂) = 20 ÷ (12/60) = 20 × 5 = 100 km/h

Speed of first car (S₁) = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (100 + 20) ÷ 2 = 60 km/h

Speed of second car (S₂) = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 = (100 − 20) ÷ 2 = 40 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 60, 40 km/h.**

Relative Speed (Same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Relative Speed (Opposite direction) = S₁ + S₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ S₁ − S₂ = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 km/h --- (Equation 1)

⇒ S₁ + S₂ = 20 ÷ (1/5) = 20 × 5 = 100 km/h --- (Equation 2)

Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ 2S₁ = 120

⇒ S₁ = 60 km/h

Substituting S₁ = 60 in Equation 2:

⇒ 60 + S₂ = 100

⇒ S₂ = 40 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 60, 40 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂.

Time & Distance Rule

The time taken for two objects to meet is calculated by dividing the initial distance between them by their relative speed: Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed.
</p

question: Akshara and Siddharth travel from point P to Q, a distance of 72 km at a rate of 8 km/h and 10 km/h, respectively. Siddharth reaches Q first and returns immediately and meets Akshara at R. Find the distance from P to R.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two persons start together from a point, and one reaches the destination and returns to meet the other, the total distance covered by both is 2 × Distance between the points.

Total distance covered = 2 × 72 = 144 km.

Ratio of distances covered = Ratio of their speeds = 8 : 10 = 4 : 5.

Distance covered by Akshara (PR) = (4 ÷ 9) × 144 = 64 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 64 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between P and Q = 72 km

Speed of Akshara = 8 km/h

Speed of Siddharth = 10 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2507102b4cea731c349014231d59dd099fe5d3fd04eab28fada62e62d30167fb.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Total distance covered by both = 2 × Distance between two points

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the time taken for them to meet at point R be 't' hours.

⇒ Distance covered by Akshara in t hours = PR = 8t km

⇒ Distance covered by Siddharth in t hours = PQ + QR = 10t km

⇒ The sum of the distances covered by both = PR + PQ + QR

⇒ Since PR + QR = PQ, the total distance covered = 2 × PQ = 2 × 72 = 144 km.

⇒ 8t + 10t = 144

⇒ 18t = 144

⇒ t = 8 hours

⇒ Distance from P to R = 8t = 8 × 8 = 64 km

**∴ The correct answer is 64 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting Point Concept

When two individuals start simultaneously from point A towards B, and the faster one returns immediately from B to meet the slower one at C, the total distance covered by both is exactly twice the distance between A and B (2D).

Direct Distance Ratio

Since the time of travel until they meet is constant for both, the distance covered is directly proportional to their respective speeds. Thus, Distance Ratio = S₁ : S₂.
</p

question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 200 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 9 km/h and that of the policeman 10 km/h, how far will the thief have to run before he is overtaken?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of speeds of Policeman to Thief = 10 : 9

Since the time taken is constant, ratio of distances covered = 10 : 9

Difference in distance ratio = 1 unit = 200 m = 0.2 km

Distance covered by thief = 9 units = 9 × 0.2 = 1.8 km

**∴ The correct answer is 1.8 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Policeman = 10 km/h

Speed of Thief = 9 km/h

Initial distance between them = 200 m = 0.2 km

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d9130cb192aad85372295fb97f65dbd03cc5122348146ef8fe519eb387a7a245.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = Speed of A − Speed of B (in same direction)

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = 10 − 9 = 1 km/h

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 0.2 km ÷ 1 km/h = 0.2 h

⇒ Distance covered by thief before being caught = Speed of Thief × Time

⇒ Distance = 9 km/h × 0.2 h = 1.8 km

**∴ The correct answer is 1.8 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their speeds (V₁ − V₂). When moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (V₁ + V₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert a speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5 ÷ 18. Conversely, to convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

Average Speed

When equal distances are covered at different speeds x and y, the average speed for the entire journey is given by (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).
</p

question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 195 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 22 km/h and that of the policeman is 27 km/h, then how far would the thief have run (in m) before he is overtaken?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the time taken by both to meet is the same, the ratio of distances covered is equal to the ratio of their speeds.

Ratio of speeds = Policeman : Thief = 27 : 22

Difference in ratio = 27 − 22 = 5 units

This 5 units represents the initial gap of 195 m ⇒ 1 unit = 195 ÷ 5 = 39 m

Distance covered by the thief = 22 units = 22 × 39 = 858 m

**∴ The correct answer is 858 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial distance between Policeman and Thief = 195 m

Speed of Policeman (SP) = 27 km/h

Speed of Thief (ST) = 22 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 27 − 22 = 5 km/h

⇒ Convert Relative Speed into m/s = 5 × (5 ÷ 18) = 25 ÷ 18 m/s

⇒ Time taken by Policeman to overtake = 195 ÷ (25 ÷ 18)

⇒ Time = (195 × 18) ÷ 25 = 140.4 seconds

⇒ Speed of Thief in m/s = 22 × (5 ÷ 18) = 55 ÷ 9 m/s

⇒ Distance covered by the Thief = Speed × Time = (55 ÷ 9) × 140.4

⇒ Distance = 55 × 15.6 = 858 m

**∴ The correct answer is 858 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). When moving in opposite directions, relative speed is their sum (S₁ + S₂).

Conversion of Units

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by (5 ÷ 18). Conversely, to convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by (18 ÷ 5).

Proportionality of Distance and Speed

If the time taken is constant, the distance traveled by an object is directly proportional to its speed (D₁ ÷ D₂ = S₁ ÷ S₂). This allows solving chase problems instantly using ratio methods.

question: Suppose P starts walking at a speed of 8 km/h. After 8 hours B started travelling on a bicycle at a speed of 24 km/h. The distance from the starting B can catch P is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Head start distance covered by P in 8 hours = 8 × 8 = 64 km.

Relative speed of B (moving in the same direction) = 24 − 8 = 16 km/h.

Time taken by B to catch P = 64 ÷ 16 = 4 hours.

Distance from the starting point = B's speed × time = 24 × 4 = 96 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 96 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of P = 8 km/h

Speed of B = 24 km/h

Head start time for P = 8 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/af7d8e12728f3fe71dd76a33d84aba3f0c7fff9aa670cc49bb917333ddd0f164.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed of B − Speed of P

Catch-up Time = Initial Gap Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by P before B starts = 8 × 8 = 64 km

⇒ This 64 km is the gap that B needs to cover to catch P.

⇒ Relative speed of B to P = 24 − 8 = 16 km/h

⇒ Time taken by B to close the gap = 64 ÷ 16 = 4 hours

⇒ Distance from the starting point = B's speed × Time taken

⇒ Distance = 24 × 4 = 96 km

**∴ The correct answer is 96 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects travel in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂.

Catch-up Time Formula

The time required to overtake or catch a head-start object is given by: Time = Initial Gap Distance ÷ Relative Speed.

Distance by Ratio Method

When the travel time is constant for two moving bodies, the ratio of the distances they cover is directly proportional to the ratio of their speeds: D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂.
</p

question: A thief takes off on his bike at a certain speed, after seeing a police car at a distance of 250 m. The police car starts chasing the thief and catches him. If the thief runs 1.5 km before being caught and the speed of the police car is 70 km/h, then what is the speed of thief's bike (in km/h)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the time of travel is constant, the ratio of speeds is directly proportional to the ratio of distances covered.

Ratio of distances = Distance of Police : Distance of Thief = (1.5 + 0.25) : 1.5 = 1.75 : 1.50 = 7 : 6

⇒ Speed of Police : Speed of Thief = 7 : 6

Given 7 units = 70 km/h ⇒ 1 unit = 10 km/h

⇒ Speed of Thief = 6 units = 60 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total distance covered by the police car = 1.5 km + 0.25 km = 1.75 km

⇒ Total distance covered by the thief = 1.5 km

⇒ Time taken by both the police car and the thief to reach the catch point is equal.

⇒ Distance of Police ÷ Speed of Police = Distance of Thief ÷ Speed of Thief

⇒ 1.75 ÷ 70 = 1.5 ÷ Speed of Thief

⇒ Speed of Thief = (1.5 × 70) ÷ 1.75

⇒ Speed of Thief = 105 ÷ 1.75 = 60 km/h

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Constant Time Concept

If two bodies travel for the exact same duration of time, the ratio of the distances they cover is directly proportional to the ratio of their speeds (D₁ / D₂ = S₁ / S₂).

Time taken to meet after 8:00 AM = 420 ÷ 150 = 2.8 hours = 2 hours 48 minutes.

Meeting time = 8:00 AM + 2 hours 48 minutes = 10:48 AM.

**∴ The correct answer is 10:48 AM.**

question: A boat covers a round trip journey between two points A and B in a river in T hours. If its speed in still water becomes 2 times, it would take (80)/(161) T hours for the same journey. Find the ratio of its speed in still water to the speed of the river.
solution:
**Given:** 

A boat covers a round trip journey between two points A and B in a river in T hours

**Formula used:**

Downstream = (u + v) km/hr

Upstream = (u – v) km/hr

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of boat in still water be xkm/hr

Speed of stream = y km/hr

Let the distance between them be d 

Downstream = (x + y) km/hr

Upstream = (x – y) km/hr

According to the question

⇒ d/(x + y) + d/(x – y) = 161T

⇒ d(x - y + x + y)/ x2 - y2 = 161T

⇒d(2x)/161(x2 - y2) = T ......... (1)

Again,

⇒ d/(2x + y) + d/(2x – y) = 80T

⇒d(2x - y + 2x + y)/(2x)2 - (y)2 = 80T

⇒d(4x) / 80(4x2 - y2) = T ..........(2)

Now equalling both the equations,

⇒d(2x)/161(x2 - y2) = d(4x) / 80(4x2 - y2) 

⇒1/161(x2 - y2) = 2/ 80(4x2 - y2) 

⇒1/(161x2 - 161y2) = 1/(160x2 - 40y2)

⇒160x2 - 40y2 = 161x2 - 161y2

⇒x2 = 121y2

⇒x/y = 11/1

∴ The required ratio is 11 : 1

⇒ d[(x – y) + (x + y)/(x² – y²)] = T

⇒ d[(2x/(x² – y²) = T

⇒ d/T = x² – y²/2x .....(1)

Again,

⇒ d/(2x + y) + d/(2x – y) = 80T/161

⇒ d(2x – y+ 2x + y)/4x² – y² = 80T/161

⇒ d(4x/4x² – y²) = 80T/161

Now, substituting both the equation, we get

d/T = x2 – y2/2x = 80(4x2 – y2)/4x × 161

⇒ (161x² – 160x²) = (161y² – 40y²)

question: A boat covers a certain distance against the stream in 9 hours 36 min and it covers the same distance along the stream in 6 hours. What is the ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream?
solution:
Given:

A boat covers a certain distance against the stream in 9 hours 36 min and it covers the same distance along the stream in 6 hours.

Concept used:

1. Distance = Speed × Time

2. While rowing upstream, the upstream speed is the difference between the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the flow.

3. While rowing downstream, the downstream speed is the addition of the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the flow.

Calculation:

Let the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the stream be S and R km/h respectively.

9 hours 36 minutes = 9 + 36/60 = 9.6 hours

Let the distance be D km.

Upstream speed = (S - R) km/h

Downstream speed = (S + R) km/h

​According to the question,

frac {D}{S - R} = 9.6 ....(1)

 frac {D}{S + R} = 6 ....(2)

(1) ÷ (2),

frac {S + R}{S - R} = frac {9.6}{6}

⇒ 6S + 6R = 9.6S - 9.6R

⇒ 3.6S = 15.6R

⇒ S/R = 15.6/3.6

⇒ S : R = 13 : 3

**∴ The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 13 : 3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

We know, 9 hours 36 min = 576 min and 6 hour = 360 min

Through upstream (U) and downstream(D) distance is constant, then time ∝ 1/speed

Time ratio of U : D = 576 : 360 = 8 : 5, then Speed ratio of U : D = 5 : 8

Speed of boat = (D speed + U speed)/2 = (8 + 5)/2 = 13/2 

Speed of stream = (D speed - U speed)/2 = (8 - 5)/2 = 3/2

So, Speed of boat : Speed of stream = 13/2 : 3/2 = 13 : 3

question: A bullet train covers a fixed distance in 30 minutes at an average speed of 240 km/h. Due to track maintenance, it needs to be diverted, increasing the distance by 20%. If the train needs to arrive at its destination on time (i.e., in 30 minutes), what should its new average speed be in km/h?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the travel time remains constant (30 minutes) in both cases, Speed is directly proportional to Distance.

Because the distance increases by 20%, the required average speed must also increase by exactly 20%.

New Speed = 240 + (20% of 240)

New Speed = 240 + 48 = 288 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 288 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Average Speed (S₁) = 240 km/h

Initial Time (T₁) = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours

New Time (T₂) = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 Initial Distance: 120 km
 Speed: 240 km/h | Time: 30 min
 
 
 New Distance: 144 km (+20%)
 New Speed: 288 km/h | Time: 30 min

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Distance (D₁) = 240 × 0.5 = 120 km

⇒ The distance is increased by 20% due to track maintenance.

⇒ New Distance (D₂) = 120 + (20 ÷ 100) × 120

⇒ D₂ = 120 + 24 = 144 km

⇒ The train needs to arrive in the same exact time window.

⇒ New Time (T₂) = 0.5 hours

⇒ New Speed (S₂) = D₂ ÷ T₂

⇒ S₂ = 144 ÷ 0.5 = 288 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 288 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct and Inverse Proportionality

When **Time is constant**, Distance and Speed are directly proportional (S₁ ÷ S₂ = D₁ ÷ D₂). When **Distance is constant**, Time and Speed are inversely proportional.

Unit Conversions for Speed

To convert an object's speed from km/h to m/s, multiply it by 5 ÷ 18. To change m/s back to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

Average Speed

Average Speed over an entire journey equals Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If two equal distances are traveled at speeds a and b, the Average Speed is 2ab ÷ (a + b).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered = S₁ × T₁ = 60 × 1.75 = 105 km

⇒ New speed (S₂) = Distance ÷ T₂ = 105 ÷ 2 = 52.5 km/h

⇒ Decrease in speed = S₁ − S₂ = 60 − 52.5 = 7.5 km/h

⇒ Fraction decrease = Decrease ÷ Original Speed

⇒ Fraction decrease = 7.5 ÷ 60 = 1/8 = 0.125

⇒ Percentage decrease = 0.125 × 100% = 12.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5% (0.125).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality of Speed and Time

When distance is kept constant, speed is inversely proportional to the time taken (S ∝ 1/T). If the time increases by a ratio of a : b, the required speed decreases by the ratio of b : a.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. It must be noted that it is strictly calculated using this formula and is not merely the simple arithmetic average of individual speeds unless the travel times are identical.

Percentage Change

Percentage Change = (New Value − Initial Value) ÷ (Initial Value) × 100. A negative end result simply indicates a percentage decrease.
</p

question: In a 1500 m race, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 200 m, then vehicle P wins the race by 8 sec. Alternatively, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 400 m, the race ends in a dead heat. How long does vehicle P take to run 1500 m?
solution:
**Given:**

Distance = 1500 m

Vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 200 m, and P wins the race by 8 sec

If vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 400 m, the race ends in a dead heat

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculations:**

For case 1:

Vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 200 m, and P wins the race by 8 sec

⇒ Distance travel by P = 1500 m

⇒ Distance travel by Q = 1500 - 200 = 1300 m

⇒ Speed of vehicle P = (1500)/(t)

⇒ Speed of vehicle Q = (1300)/(t+8)

Now for case 2:

If vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 400 m, the race ends in a dead heat

⇒ Distance travel by P = 1500 m

⇒ Distance travel by Q = 1500 - 400 = 1100 m

As the race is end at dead heat, they finish the race at tie or equal time

⇒ Time taken by vehicle P = Time taken by vehicle Q

⇒ (1500)/(frac{1500){t}}=(1100)/(frac{1300){t+8}}

⇒ t=(11(t+8))/(13)

⇒ 13t = 11t + 88

⇒ 13t - 11t = 88

⇒ 2t = 88

⇒ t = 44 sec

**⇒ ****Hence, The time taken by vehicle P is 44 sec**

Distance = speed × time

**Calculation **

Let’s assume speed of A as vₐ and speed of B as vb

Then, in a 200 M race distance run by A = 200 m

Distance run by B after getting head start of 25 M = 175 m

Time taken by A = 200/vₐ

if A gives B a start of 45 m, the race ends in a dead heat,

Time taken by A = 200/vₐ

Both finish at same time,

∴ 155/vb = 200/vₐ

⇒ vₐ = 40/31 × vb ----(2)

Putting (2) in (1) we get,

Vb = 2 

Time taken by B to complete 200M race would be 175 / 2 = 87.5 seconds

Thus time taken by A would be = 87.5 - 10 = 77.5 second

**A takes 77.5 seconds to run 200m.**

Vishu's speed = 54 ÷ 12 = 4.5 m/s.

Time taken by Vishu to cover 900 m = 900 ÷ 4.5 = 200 seconds = 3 minutes 20 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes 20 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance of the race = 900 m

In Case 1, Atul gives Vishu a head-start of 20 seconds and beats him by 135 m.

In Case 2, Atul gives Vishu a start of 189 m and beats him by 8 seconds.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

Let Atul's speed be vₐ and the time taken by Atul to cover 900 m be T seconds.

Let Vishu's speed be vv.

**Case 1:** Vishu runs for (T + 20) seconds but falls short by 135 m.

⇒ Distance covered by Vishu = 900 − 135 = 765 m

⇒ Time taken to cover 765 m = T + 20

⇒ 765 ÷ vv = T + 20 --- (Equation 1)

**Case 2:** Vishu gets a 189 m distance start, so he only needs to run 900 − 189 = 711 m.

Atul finishes in T seconds, but beats Vishu by 8 seconds.

⇒ Time taken by Vishu to cover 711 m = T + 8

⇒ 711 ÷ vv = T + 8 --- (Equation 2)

Subtracting Equation 2 from Equation 1:

⇒ (765 ÷ vv) − (711 ÷ vv) = (T + 20) − (T + 8)

⇒ (765 − 711) ÷ vv = 12

⇒ 54 ÷ vv = 12

⇒ vv = 54 ÷ 12 = 4.5 m/s

Time taken by Vishu to complete the full 900 m race:

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Time = 900 ÷ 4.5

⇒ Time = 200 seconds

⇒ 200 seconds = 3 minutes 20 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes 20 seconds.**

Head-start in Distance

When runner A gives B a start of x meters in a race of L meters, A covers the full L meters while B covers (L − x) meters.

Head-start in Time

When runner A gives B a head-start of t seconds, B begins running t seconds before A starts the race.

Beating by Distance or Time

If A beats B by x meters, B is x meters behind when A finishes. If A beats B by t seconds, B reaches the finish line t seconds after A.

Downstream speed = (x + y) km/h

Upstream speed = (x - y) km/h

Time = Distance/Speed

So, 24/(20 - x) = 24/(20 + x) + (1/2) [∵ 30 minutes = 1/2 hour]

⇒ 24/(20 - x) - 24/(20 + x) = (1/2)

⇒ (24(20+x)-24(20-x))/(400-x²)=(1)/(2)

⇒ (24(20+x-20+x))/(400-x²)=(1)/(2)

⇒ (24×2x)/(400-x²)=(1)/(2)

⇒ 400 - x² = 96x

⇒ x² + 96x - 400 = 0

⇒ x2 + 100x - 4x - 400 = 0

⇒ x (x + 100) - 4 (x + 100) = 0

⇒ (x + 100) (x - 4) = 0

⇒ x + 100 = 0 ⇒ x = -100 ["-" is neglacted]

question: A boatman can row his boat in still water at a speed of 9 km/h. He can also row 44 km downstream and 35 km upstream in 9 hours. How much time (in hours) will he take to row 33 km downstream and 28 km upstream?
solution:
**Given:**

The speed of the boat in still water = 9 km/h

Concept used:

If the speed of a boat in still water is x km/h and the speed of the stream is y km/h, then

Downstream speed = (x + y) km/h

Upstream speed = (x - y) km/h

Time = Distance/Speed

**Calculation:**

Let, the speed of the water = x km/h

Time to cover 44 km downstream = 44/(9 + x)

Time to cover 35 km upstream = 35/(9 - x)

so, [44/(9 + x)] + [35/(9 - x)] = 9

⇒ (44(9-x)+35(9+x))/(81-x²)=9

⇒ 396 - 44x + 315 + 35x = 729 - 9x²

⇒ 9x2 - 9x - 18 = 0

⇒ x2 - x - 2 = 0

⇒ x2 - 2x + x - 2 = 0

⇒ x (x - 2) + 1 (x - 2) = 0

⇒ (x + 1) (x - 2) = 0

⇒ x + 1 = 0 ⇒ x = - 1 ["-" is neglacted]

⇒ x - 2 = 0 ⇒ x = 2

∴ The speed of the water = 2 km/h

So, time is taken to row 33 km downstream and 28 km upstream = [33/(9 + 2)] + [28/(9 - 2)]

= (33/11) + (28/7)

= 3 + 4 = 7 hours

**∴ The boatman will take 7 hours to row 33 km downstream and 28 km upstream**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Here we can see that, 

The Downstream distance in both cases (44 km & 33 km) are divisible by 11

The Upstream distance in both cases (35 km & 28 km) are divisible by 7.

We can say that because the time required (Number of hours) is a complete number in both cases. (9 hrs & all options are complete numbers not in decimal)

Here, according to the question, 

x = 9 km/hr.

⇒ 44/(9 + y) + 35/(9 - y) = 9 hrs

Put y = 2, so that 9 + y will be 11 & 9 - y = 7

⇒ 44/11 + 35/7 = 4 + 5 = 9

y = 2 satisfies the given equation,

Now, 

⇒ 33/(9 + y) + 28/(9 - y) = 33/(9 + 2) + 28/(9 - 2) 

⇒ 33/11 + 28/7 = 3 + 4 = 7 hrs

∴ The boatman will take 7 hours to row 33 km downstream and 28 km upstream

⇒ Total time = 75 min 

⇒ Distance traveled in 72 min

question: A swimmer swims from a point P against the current for 6 min and then swims back along the current for next 6 min and reaches at a point Q. If the distance between P and Q is 120 m then the speed of the current (in km/h) is:
solution:
Given: 

A swimmer swims from point P against the current for 6 min and then swims back along the current for next 6 min and reaches at a point Q.

The distance between P and Q is 120 m.

Concept used:

1. 6 min = 360 seconds

2. While rowing upstream, the upstream speed is the difference between the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the flow.

3. While rowing downstream, the downstream speed is the addition of the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the flow.

4. 1 m/s = 18/5 km/h

5. Distance = Time × Speed

Calculation:

Let's suppose the swimmer started from P and swam 360 seconds to R against the current, then return to Q swimming for 360 seconds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7bcfe6a4dbdc137a2c61104611309129d86316219d60c66a455b9adfaf2a2ca6.png] 

Let the speed of the swimmer in still water and the current be U and V m/s respectively.

​According to the question,

PR = 360(U - V) ....(1)

QR = 360(U + V) ....(2)

So, PQ = QR - PR

⇒ 120 = 360(U + V - U + V) (From 1 and 2)

⇒ V = 1/6

So, the speed of the current = 1/6 m/s

Now, the speed of the current = 1/6 × 18/5 = 0.6 km/h

∴ The speed of the current is 0.6 km/h.

Speed ratio Downstream : Still water = 125% : 100% = 5 : 4

Stream speed ratio = 5 − 4 = 1 part, so Upstream speed ratio = 4 − 1 = 3 parts.

Speed in still water (4 parts) = 20 km ÷ 0.5 hr = 40 km/h.

Upstream speed (3 parts) = (40 ÷ 4) × 3 = 30 km/h.

Time for 15 km upstream = 15 ÷ 30 = 1/2 hour.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2 hour.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Speed downstream = 125% of speed in still water.

⇒ Time taken to cover 20 km in still water = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Speed = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ Downstream Speed (D) = Boat Speed (B) + Stream Speed (S)

⇒ Upstream Speed (U) = Boat Speed (B) − Stream Speed (S)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f3c23fec93def93e6ddefbd76678ec1169c82b5e14d8bcb2559847494062b6e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed in still water (B) = 20 km ÷ 0.5 hours = 40 km/h

⇒ Speed downstream (D) = 125% of 40 = 1.25 × 40 = 50 km/h

⇒ Speed of stream (S) = D − B = 50 − 40 = 10 km/h

⇒ Speed upstream (U) = B − S = 40 − 10 = 30 km/h

⇒ Time to cover 15 km upstream = Distance ÷ Upstream Speed

⇒ Time = 15 ÷ 30 = 1/2 hour

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2 hour.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed in Still Water

It is the average of downstream and upstream speeds: B = (D + U) ÷ 2

Speed of Stream

It is half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: S = (D − U) ÷ 2

Average Speed of Journey

If a boat goes a certain distance downstream and comes back upstream, the average speed is (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).

question: A boat can go 60 km downstream and 40 km upstream in 12 hours 30 minutes. It can go 84 km downstream and 63 km upstream in 18 hours 54 minutes. What is the speed (in km/h, to the nearest integer) of the boat in still water?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divide first case by 20: 3/D + 2/U = 0.625

Divide second case by 21: 4/D + 3/U = 0.90

Eliminate 1/D: 3 × (4/D + 3/U) − 4 × (3/D + 2/U) = 3(0.9) − 4(0.625)

1/U = 2.7 − 2.5 = 0.2 ⇒ Upstream speed (U) = 5 km/h

3/D + 2(0.2) = 0.625 ⇒ 3/D = 0.225 ⇒ Downstream speed (D) = 13.33 km/h

Boat speed = (13.33 + 5) ÷ 2 = 9.165 ≈ 9 km/h

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: Distance downstream = 60 km, Distance upstream = 40 km, Time = 12.5 hours

Case 2: Distance downstream = 84 km, Distance upstream = 63 km, Time = 18.9 hours (as 54/60 = 0.9)

**Formula:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed | Speed of boat in still water (x) = (D + U) ÷ 2

 Boat Speed (x) = (D + U) ÷ 2
 

 

 

 
• 
 

 Downstream: x + y (Speed D)
 
• 
 

 Upstream: x − y (Speed U)

⇒ Let 1/D = a and 1/U = b

⇒ 60a + 40b = 12.5 --- (i)

⇒ 84a + 63b = 18.9 --- (ii)

⇒ Multiply (i) by 1.4: 84a + 56b = 17.5

⇒ Subtracting from (ii): (84a + 63b) − (84a + 56b) = 18.9 − 17.5

⇒ 7b = 1.4 ⇒ b = 0.2

⇒ U = 1/b = 1/0.2 = 5 km/h

⇒ 60a + 40(0.2) = 12.5 ⇒ 60a + 8 = 12.5

⇒ 60a = 4.5 ⇒ a = 0.075

⇒ D = 1/a = 1/0.075 = 13.33 km/h

⇒ Speed of boat (x) = (13.33 + 5) ÷ 2 = 18.33 ÷ 2 = 9.165 km/h

⇒ Nearest integer = 9 km/h

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Speeds

If speed of boat is x and stream is y, then Downstream (D) = x + y and Upstream (U) = x − y.

Calculating Still Water and Stream Speed

Boat speed in still water x = (D + U) ÷ 2; Speed of stream y = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Time Conversion

To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60. Example: 54 minutes = 54/60 = 0.9 hours.</p

question: A thief is chased by a policeman and distance between them is 3 km. The speed of policeman is 75 km/h and the speed of the thief is 60 km/h. The policeman will be able to catch the thief when the thief would have covered the distance of ____________ km.

question: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 500 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the rate of 17 km/h and 20 km/h, respectively. What is the distance between them after 8 minutes?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in same direction = 20 − 17 = 3 km/h.

Convert relative speed to m/min = 3 × (1000/60) = 50 m/min.

Distance reduced in 8 minutes = 50 × 8 = 400 m.

Remaining distance = 500 − 400 = 100 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 
• 
 
 Policeman (P)
 20 km/h
 
 Thief (T)
 17 km/h
 

 Initial Gap = 500 m
 

 

 Relative Motion Diagram

Given:

Initial distance = 500 m

Speed of Policeman (Sₚ) = 20 km/h

Speed of Thief (Sₜ) = 17 km/h

Time (t) = 8 minutes

Formula used: Distance = Relative Speed × Time

Relative speed (same direction) = Sₚ − Sₜ

⇒ Relative speed = 20 − 17 = 3 km/h

⇒ Speed in m/min = (3 × 1000) ÷ 60 = 50 m/min

⇒ Distance covered in 8 minutes = 50 × 8 = 400 m

⇒ Distance between them after 8 minutes = Initial distance − Relative distance covered

⇒ Distance = 500 − 400 = 100 m

**∴ The correct answer is 100 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference (S₁ − S₂). In opposite directions, it is the sum (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert km/h to m/min, multiply by 1000/60 or 50/3.

Catching Time

Time to catch = Initial Distance ÷ Relative Speed. The distance covered by policeman until catching = Sₚ × Catching Time.</p

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/092ea22a3f1907faa90a5b0f256bb4a61651f22bebfa96459a6581118f1be98b.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in the same direction) = Sₚ − Sₜ

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 15 km/h − 12 km/h = 3 km/h

⇒ Time required to catch the thief = 0.6 km ÷ 3 km/h

⇒ Time = 0.2 hours

⇒ Time in minutes = 0.2 × 60 = 12 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 12 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
</p

question: A policeman noticed a thief at a distance of 500 metres. The policeman started running and the thief also started running at the same time. The thief is running at a speed of 15 km/h. It took 15 minutes for the policeman to catch the thief. Find the speed of the policeman (in km/h).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed = Distance gap ÷ Time taken to catch

Initial Distance gap = 500 m = 0.5 km, Time taken = 15 mins = 1/4 hour.

Relative speed = 0.5 ÷ (1/4) = 2 km/h.

Since both are moving in the same direction, Policeman's speed = Thief's speed + Relative speed.

Policeman's speed = 15 + 2 = 17 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 17 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Initial distance between the policeman and the thief = 500 m = 0.5 km

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed of Object 1 − Speed of Object 2

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the policeman be P km/h.

⇒ Distance covered by the thief before getting caught = Speed of thief × Time taken

⇒ Distance covered by the thief = 15 × (1/4) = 3.75 km

⇒ Total distance covered by the policeman = Initial gap + Distance covered by the thief

⇒ Total distance covered by policeman = 0.5 km + 3.75 km = 4.25 km

⇒ Speed of policeman (P) = Total Distance ÷ Time taken

⇒ P = 4.25 ÷ (1/4)

⇒ P = 4.25 × 4

⇒ P = 17 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 17 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies travel in the same direction, their relative speed is calculated as the difference between their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two bodies travel in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is calculated as the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion Trick

To quickly convert km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
</p

question: A thief pursued by a policeman was 150 m ahead at the start. If the ratio of the speed of the policeman to that of the thief was 5 : 4, then how far (distance in metres) could the thief go before he is caught by the policeman?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the time traveled is constant, the ratio of distances covered is directly equal to the ratio of their speeds.

Ratio of distances (Policeman : Thief) = Ratio of speeds = 5 : 4

Difference in distance ratio = 5 − 4 = 1 unit

This 1 unit difference corresponds to the initial gap of 150 m.

Distance covered by the thief = 4 units = 4 × 150 = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial distance between the policeman and the thief = 150 m

Ratio of speeds (Policeman : Thief) = 5 : 4

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f7c426194eb344902d1d5298451d3b3e2043f5b259ee938cc1b85a3bc9c3f17.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the speed of the policeman be 5x m/s and the thief be 4x m/s.

⇒ Relative speed = 5x − 4x = x m/s

⇒ Time taken by the policeman to catch the thief = Initial Distance Gap ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Catching Time = 150 ÷ x seconds

⇒ Distance covered by the thief before getting caught = Speed of thief × Catching Time

⇒ Distance = 4x × (150 ÷ x)

⇒ Distance = 4 × 150 = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects travel towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Constant Time Property

If two moving bodies travel for exactly the same amount of time, the distance covered by each is directly proportional to their respective speeds (D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂).

question: A boat can travel 78 km upstream and back in a total of 32 hours. It can travel 15 km upstream and 52 km downstream in a total of 9 hours. How much distance will the boat cover in 12 hours in still water?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By observing the downstream distances (78 km and 52 km), we can intuitively check their common factor 13 as the downstream speed (D).

If D = 13 km/h, time taken for 78 km downstream = 78 ÷ 13 = 6 hours.

Upstream time for 78 km = Total time 32 − 6 = 26 hours, giving upstream speed (U) = 78 ÷ 26 = 3 km/h.

Checking Case 2: (15 ÷ 3) + (52 ÷ 13) = 5 + 4 = 9 hours (Condition perfectly satisfied).

Speed in still water = (13 + 3) ÷ 2 = 8 km/h → Distance in 12 hours = 8 × 12 = 96 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 96 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total time for 78 km upstream and downstream = 32 hours

Total time for 15 km upstream and 52 km downstream = 9 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9369b76dbf0171d05d9ccff18f9a6fca5c9aa9eff88101135923badaab9ddfe0.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Speed in still water = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

**Calculation:**

Let upstream speed be U and downstream speed be D.

According to Case 1:

⇒ 78/U + 78/D = 32

⇒ 1/U + 1/D = 32/78 = 16/39 --- (1)

According to Case 2:

⇒ 15/U + 52/D = 9

Splitting 52/D into 15/D + 37/D to substitute equation (1) efficiently:

⇒ 15(1/U + 1/D) + 37/D = 9

Substituting the value of (1/U + 1/D) from equation (1):

⇒ 15 × (16/39) + 37/D = 9

⇒ (5 × 16)/13 + 37/D = 9

⇒ 80/13 + 37/D = 9

⇒ 37/D = 9 − 80/13

⇒ 37/D = (117 − 80) / 13 = 37/13

⇒ D = 13 km/h

Substitute D = 13 in equation (1):

⇒ 1/U + 1/13 = 16/39

⇒ 1/U = 16/39 − 3/39 = 13/39

⇒ 1/U = 1/3

⇒ U = 3 km/h

Now, finding the speed in still water:

⇒ Speed in still water = (13 + 3) ÷ 2 = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 km/h

Distance covered in 12 hours in still water:

⇒ Distance = 8 × 12 = 96 km

**∴ The correct answer is 96 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

Calculated by the formula v = (D + U) ÷ 2, where D is downstream speed and U is upstream speed.

Speed of Stream (Current)

Calculated by the formula s = (D − U) ÷ 2, representing the velocity of the flowing water.

Upstream & Downstream Rules

Downstream speed (D) = v + s (moving in the direction of the stream) and Upstream speed (U) = v − s (moving against the stream).
</p

question: A boatman rows to a place 30 km distant and back in 14 hours. He finds that he can row 10 km with the stream at the same time as 4 km against the stream. Find the speed (in km/h) of the stream.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Downstream speed (D) : Upstream speed (U) = Distance Ratio (in same time) = 10 : 4 = 5 : 2.

Let D = 5k and U = 2k. Total time = (30 ÷ 5k) + (30 ÷ 2k) = 14 ⇒ 6/k + 15/k = 14 ⇒ 21/k = 14 ⇒ k = 3/2.

Speed of stream = (D − U) ÷ 2 = (5k − 2k) ÷ 2 = 3k/2.

Substitute k = 3/2 ⇒ Speed of stream = (3 × 3/2) ÷ 2 = 9/4 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 9/4 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance for a one-way trip = 30 km.

Total time for the round trip = 14 hours.

Distance covered downstream in a given time = 10 km.

Distance covered upstream in the same time = 4 km.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3f50fad3d3aaed4e02ff02c8444806259d24dabbe910eafef567c9708eb33a04.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Speed of stream = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the boat in still water be u km/h and the speed of the stream be v km/h.

⇒ Downstream speed (D) = u + v

⇒ Upstream speed (U) = u − v

Since the time taken is the same for 10 km downstream and 4 km upstream:

⇒ 10 ÷ (u + v) = 4 ÷ (u − v)

⇒ (u + v) ÷ (u − v) = 10/4 = 5/2

Let Downstream speed D = 5k and Upstream speed U = 2k.

Total time taken for the round trip is 14 hours:

⇒ 30 ÷ D + 30 ÷ U = 14

⇒ 30 ÷ 5k + 30 ÷ 2k = 14

⇒ 6/k + 15/k = 14

⇒ 21/k = 14

⇒ k = 21 ÷ 14 = 3/2

Now, calculate the absolute speeds D and U:

⇒ Downstream Speed (D) = 5 × 3/2 = 15/2 = 7.5 km/h

⇒ Upstream Speed (U) = 2 × 3/2 = 3 km/h

Speed of the stream (v) = (D − U) ÷ 2

⇒ v = (7.5 − 3) ÷ 2 = 4.5 ÷ 2 = 9/4 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 9/4 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Speeds

When a boat moves with the stream, its effective speed increases (D = u + v). When it moves against the stream, its effective speed decreases (U = u − v).

Boat in Still Water

The speed of a boat in still water (u) can be calculated directly if downstream and upstream speeds are known: u = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of the Stream

The speed of the stream or current (v) is half the difference between the downstream and upstream speeds: v = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Constant Time Principle

If the time taken to travel two different distances is the same, the ratio of the distances is directly proportional to the ratio of their respective speeds (D₁ ÷ D₂ = S₁ ÷ S₂).
</p

question: A motorboat takes 18 hours to go downstream, and it takes 36 hours to return the same distance. Find the ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When distance is constant, Speed ratio is inverse of Time ratio.

Time Ratio (Downstream : Upstream) = 18 : 36 = 1 : 2 ⇒ Speed Ratio (D : U) = 2 : 1

Let Downstream Speed (D) = 2 and Upstream Speed (U) = 1

Speed of boat (B) = (D + U) ÷ 2 = 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5

Speed of stream (S) = (D − U) ÷ 2 = 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5

Ratio B : S = 1.5 : 0.5 = 3 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken downstream (Td) = 18 hours

Time taken upstream (Tᵤ) = 36 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Downstream Speed = Speed of Boat in still water (B) + Speed of Stream (S)

Upstream Speed = Speed of Boat in still water (B) − Speed of Stream (S)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4eb55c1b49218e453e18382e7ae9511f33dc760b4386bd9f011447a2cde32faf.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the speed of the boat in still water be B and the speed of the stream be S.

⇒ Downstream speed = B + S

⇒ Upstream speed = B − S

⇒ Since the distance is constant in both directions, we equate the distances:

⇒ Distance = Downstream Speed × Downstream Time = Upstream Speed × Upstream Time

⇒ (B + S) × 18 = (B − S) × 36

⇒ Dividing both sides by 18, we get:

⇒ B + S = (B − S) × 2

⇒ B + S = 2B − 2S

⇒ 2S + S = 2B − B

⇒ 3S = B

⇒ Ratio of B to S = 3 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

If Downstream Speed is D and Upstream Speed is U, then the Speed of the Boat in still water B = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

If Downstream Speed is D and Upstream Speed is U, then the Speed of the Stream S = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed

When traveling equal distances downstream and upstream, the Average Speed = (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).
</p

question: A man can row a distance of 6 km in 1 hour in still water. He can row the same distance in 45 minutes with the current. Find the total time taken by him to row a distance of 16 km with the current and to return to the starting point.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Downstream speed = Distance ÷ Time = 6 ÷ (45/60) = 8 km/h.

Stream speed = Downstream speed − Still water speed = 8 − 6 = 2 km/h.

Upstream speed = Still water speed − Stream speed = 6 − 2 = 4 km/h.

Total Time = Downstream Time + Upstream Time = (16 ÷ 8) + (16 ÷ 4)

Total Time = 2 + 4 = 6 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the man in still water (Vb) = 6 km/h

Distance covered downstream = 6 km

Time taken downstream = 45 minutes = 45 ÷ 60 = 3/4 hours

Distance for final trip = 16 km each way

**Formulas Used:**

Downstream Speed (Vd) = Vb + Speed of stream (Vₛ)

Upstream Speed (Vᵤ) = Vb − Vₛ

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b33f71d0e019c47f3066b65054d5f5b46a31a47cda8b07743a766f7bd255f2f1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream Speed (Vd) = Distance ÷ Time = 6 ÷ (3/4) = 8 km/h

⇒ We know Vd = Vb + Vₛ

⇒ 8 = 6 + Vₛ ⇒ Vₛ = 2 km/h

⇒ Upstream Speed (Vᵤ) = Vb − Vₛ = 6 − 2 = 4 km/h

⇒ Time taken to row 16 km downstream = 16 ÷ 8 = 2 hours

⇒ Time taken to row 16 km upstream = 16 ÷ 4 = 4 hours

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 4 = 6 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream Speed

When a boat moves in the direction of the stream, the effective speed is the sum of the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the current. Formula: D = Vb + Vₛ

Upstream Speed

When a boat moves against the direction of the stream, the effective speed is the difference between the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the current. Formula: U = Vb − Vₛ

Speed of Boat and Stream from D and U

Speed of boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2 | Speed of stream = (D − U) ÷ 2
</p

question: A motorboat, whose speed in 15 km/h in still water goes 50 km downstream and comes back in a total of 7 hours 30 minutes. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal distance upstream and downstream, Total Time = [Distance × (2 × Speed of Boat)] ÷ (Speed of Boat² − Stream Speed²)

⇒ 7.5 = [50 × (2 × 15)] ÷ (15² − s²)

⇒ 7.5 = 1500 ÷ (225 − s²)

⇒ 225 − s² = 200 ⇒ s² = 25

⇒ s = 5 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the motorboat in still water (v) = 15 km/h

Distance covered in each direction (D) = 50 km

Total time taken (T) = 7 hours 30 minutes = 7.5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Downstream Speed = v + s

Upstream Speed = v − s

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90d7d394c756d0fc671f442f987c0cb89eb4edd7960a13bb347a629a5b6a8a95.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the stream be s km/h.

⇒ Time taken downstream = 50 ÷ (15 + s)

⇒ Time taken upstream = 50 ÷ (15 − s)

Since the total time is 7.5 hours:

⇒ [50 ÷ (15 + s)] + [50 ÷ (15 − s)] = 7.5

Taking 50 common from the numerator:

⇒ 50 × [1 ÷ (15 + s) + 1 ÷ (15 − s)] = 7.5

⇒ 50 × [(15 − s + 15 + s) ÷ (15 + s)(15 − s)] = 7.5

⇒ 50 × [30 ÷ (225 − s²)] = 7.5

⇒ 1500 ÷ (225 − s²) = 7.5

⇒ 225 − s² = 1500 ÷ 7.5

⇒ 225 − s² = 200

⇒ s² = 225 − 200

⇒ s² = 25

⇒ s = 5 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

If the downstream speed is D and upstream speed is U, then the speed of the boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

If the downstream speed is D and upstream speed is U, then the speed of the stream = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Round Trip

When going downstream and returning upstream over the same distance, Average speed = (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).
</p

question: A boat covers a distance of 55 km downstream in 5 hours while it takes 11 hours to cover the same distance upstream. What is the speed of the boat?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Downstream Speed (D) = Distance ÷ Time = 55 ÷ 5 = 11 km/h

Upstream Speed (U) = Distance ÷ Time = 55 ÷ 11 = 5 km/h

Speed of boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2

⇒ (11 + 5) ÷ 2 = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 8 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/256189234a100c96ff91c781e37fe6cf5eae0715b3631818078a472ab0830db3.png] 

**Given:**

Distance covered = 55 km

Time taken downstream = 5 hours

Time taken upstream = 11 hours

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Speed of Boat in Still Water = (Speed Downstream + Speed Upstream) ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream Speed = 55 ÷ 5 = 11 km/h

⇒ Upstream Speed = 55 ÷ 11 = 5 km/h

⇒ Speed of Boat in Still Water = (11 + 5) ÷ 2

⇒ Speed of Boat in Still Water = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 8 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of the Stream

It is calculated as half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: Vₛ = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Relationship Between Speeds

Downstream Speed (D) = Speed of Boat (Vb) + Speed of Stream (Vₛ).

Upstream Speed (U) = Speed of Boat (Vb) − Speed of Stream (Vₛ).

Average Speed for a Round Trip

If a boat goes a certain distance upstream and returns downstream to the original point, its average speed is given by (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).
</p

question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 100 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. If the speed of thief and policeman are 21 km/h and 23 km/h, respectively, then how far will the thief have to run before he is over taken?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the time of running is constant for both, the ratio of distances covered is equal to the ratio of their speeds.

Ratio of speeds (Police : Thief) = 23 : 21

Difference in distance ratio = 23 − 21 = 2 units, which is equal to the initial gap of 100 m.

⇒ 1 unit = 100 ÷ 2 = 50 m

⇒ Distance run by the thief = 21 units = 21 × 50 = 1050 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1050 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2062327096b12fe8c1af981927f56f76f4a3fc2723f24933bbf907eb8fa1edf5.png] 

**Given:**

Distance between policeman and thief = 100 m

Speed of thief = 21 km/h

Speed of policeman = 23 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = 23 − 21 = 2 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 2 × (5 ÷ 18) = 5/9 m/s

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 100 ÷ (5/9) = 180 seconds

⇒ Distance covered by the thief = Speed of thief × Time taken

⇒ Distance covered = [21 × (5 ÷ 18)] × 180

⇒ Distance covered = 21 × 50 = 1050 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1050 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗₐₜᵢvₑ = |S₁ − S₂|.

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗₐₜᵢvₑ = S₁ + S₂.

Proportionality of Distance and Speed

When the time traveled is constant, the distance covered is directly proportional to the speed: D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂.
</p

question: A policeman is chasing a thief at a speed of 82 km/h. The thief is 1300 m away and is running at a speed of 64 km/h. In how much time will the policeman catch the thief if both are riding on bikes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since both the policeman and the thief are moving in the same direction, relative speed = 82 − 64 = 18 km/h.

Convert relative speed to m/s = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s.

Time required to cover 1300 m gap = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 1300 ÷ 5 = 260 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 260 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/459e8a3558179988894b40dc8d137de344ddb061ab6ac577bf8c6f0cd38428ab.png] 

**Given:**

Speed of Policeman (S₁) = 82 km/h

Speed of Thief (S₂) = 64 km/h

Initial distance between them (D) = 1300 m

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in the same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 82 − 64 = 18 km/h

⇒ Convert speed into m/s: 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken = 1300 ÷ 5 = 260 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 260 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ − S₂. When moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5.

Average Speed

Average speed is the Total Distance Covered divided by Total Time Taken. If a person covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).
</p

question: A policeman noticed a thief at some distance. The policeman started running to catch the thief and the thief also started running at the same time. The speed of both policeman and the thief was 12 km per hour and 10 km per hour, respectively. It took 30 minutes for the policeman to catch the thief. Find the initial distance (in metres) between them.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When running in the same direction, Relative Speed = SP − ST.

Relative speed = 12 − 10 = 2 km/h

Time = 30 minutes = 1/2 hour

Initial distance = Relative speed × Time = 2 × 1/2 = 1 km

Convert to metres: 1 km = 1000 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1000 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of policeman (SP) = 12 km/h

Speed of thief (ST) = 10 km/h

Time taken to catch the thief (t) = 30 minutes = 30 ÷ 60 = 0.5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed (same direction) = SP − ST

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e7fd881eb1c69088519f114b1cd3072592449ec397bd4274cb6a0cd636aea3e.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ The policeman and the thief run in the same direction, so we calculate their relative speed.

⇒ Relative speed = 12 − 10 = 2 km/h

⇒ Initial Distance = Relative Speed × Time taken to catch

⇒ Initial Distance = 2 km/h × 0.5 hours

⇒ Initial Distance = 1 km

⇒ Convert kilometers to meters: 1 km = 1000 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1000 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. When they move in opposite directions towards each other, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversions for Speed and Distance

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s back to km/h, multiply by 18/5. Always ensure units match before applying distance formulas.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If equal distances are covered at speeds S₁ and S₂, then Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).
</p

question: Two cars, X and Y, start from points 360 km apart and travel at constant speeds. If they move towards each other, they meet in 4 hours. If they move in the same direction, they meet in 12 hours. What is the speed of car X? (Assume X is the faster car).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in opposite direction = 360 ÷ 4 = 90 km/h

Relative speed in same direction = 360 ÷ 12 = 30 km/h

Speed of the faster car (X) = (Sum of relative speeds + Difference of relative speeds) ÷ 2

Speed of X = (90 + 30) ÷ 2 = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Case 1: Opposite Direction (X + Y)

 Case 2: Same Direction (X − Y)
 
•

**Given:**

Distance between X and Y = 360 km

Time to meet moving towards each other = 4 hours

Time to meet moving in the same direction = 12 hours

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Opposite Direction: Relative Speed = X + Y

Same Direction: Relative Speed = X − Y

**Calculations:**

⇒ X + Y = 360 ÷ 4

⇒ X + Y = 90 ... (Equation 1)

⇒ X − Y = 360 ÷ 12

⇒ X − Y = 30 ... (Equation 2)

⇒ Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ (X + Y) + (X − Y) = 90 + 30

⇒ 2X = 120

⇒ X = 60 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is calculated as the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is calculated as the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Distance Constant Rule

If the distance to be covered remains constant, the speed of an object is inversely proportional to the time taken: S₁ ÷ S₂ = T₂ ÷ T₁.
</p

question: Ajay and Vijay start from the same point and walk at 4 km/h and 5 km/h respectively, in the same direction. What will be the distance between them after 2 hours?

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds.

Distance gap after 2 hours = Relative speed × Time = 1 × 2 = 2 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km.**

Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance covered by Vijay in 2 hours = 5 × 2 = 10 km

⇒ Since they are walking in the same direction, the distance between them is the difference of distances covered.

question: A train without stoppage travels with an average speed of 50 km/h, and with stoppage, it travels with an average speed of 40 km/h. For how many minutes does the train stop on an average per hour?
solution:
Without stoppage average speed = 50 km/h

With stoppages average speed = 40 km/h

Time of rest per hour equal to the difference in average speed divided by the speed without stoppage.

Required time = [(50 – 40)/50] × 60 = 12

So, A train stops on an average 12 minute/hr

question: Two cyclists X and Y start at the same time from place A and go towards place B at a speed of 6 km/h and 8 km/h, respectively. Despite stopping for 15 minutes during the journey, Y reaches 10 minutes earlier than X. The distance between the places A and B is:
solution:
Speed of X = 6 km and speed of Y = 8 km

Speed ratio of X and Y = 6 : 8 = 3 : 4

Time ratio of X and Y = 4 : 3

As we know, Time is inversely proportional to speed.

The time difference = 15 min + 10 min = 25 min

4 – 3 unit = 1 unit

1 unit = 25 min

Time taking by X = 4 × 25 = 100 min = 100/60 hr

Distance covered by X in 100/60 hr = 100/60 × 6 = 10 km.

subject: MATH
question: Two trains of lengths 150 m and 250 m run on parallel lines. When they run in the same direction, they take 20 seconds to cross each other and, when they run in the opposite direction, they take 5 seconds to cross each other. What is the speed of the two trains?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 150 + 250 = 400 m.

Relative speed in same direction = S₁ − S₂ = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s.

Relative speed in opposite direction = S₁ + S₂ = 400 ÷ 5 = 80 m/s.

Solving, S₁ = (80 + 20) ÷ 2 = 50 m/s and S₂ = (80 − 20) ÷ 2 = 30 m/s.

Speeds in km/h = 50 × (18/5) = 180 km/h and 30 × (18/5) = 108 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 180 km/h and 108 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 150 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 250 m

Time taken to cross in same direction (T₁) = 20 seconds

Time taken to cross in opposite direction (T₂) = 5 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Total distance covered to cross each other = L₁ + L₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16430e557035d55fee350ec3e082cf14d0f49e9acdc012923f1823d994f2e282.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 150 + 250 = 400 m

⇒ Let the speed of the first train be u m/s and the second train be v m/s.

⇒ When running in the same direction, relative speed = u − v

⇒ u − v = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s ... (Equation 1)

⇒ When running in opposite directions, relative speed = u + v

⇒ u + v = 400 ÷ 5 = 80 m/s ... (Equation 2)

⇒ Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ 2u = 100 ⇒ u = 50 m/s

⇒ Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 2:

⇒ 2v = 60 ⇒ v = 30 m/s

⇒ Convert speeds to km/h by multiplying with (18/5):

⇒ Speed of first train = 50 × (18/5) = 180 km/h

⇒ Speed of second train = 30 × (18/5) = 108 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 180 km/h and 108 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). When moving in the same direction, it is the difference of their speeds (|S₁ − S₂|).

Distance While Crossing

When two trains cross each other, the total distance covered is always the sum of their lengths (L₁ + L₂), regardless of the direction they are moving.

Unit Conversion Trick

To rapidly convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5. To convert from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.
</p

question: A train 900 m long is running at 108 km/h. How long will it take to clear a 900 m long platform completely?
solution:

Speed of train = 108 km/hr

Length of platform = 900 meters

Formula Used:

Time = Distance/Speed

Calculation:

Speed of train in km/hr = 108 km/hr

Speed of train in m/sec = 108 × 5/18

⇒ 30 m/sec

Time taken by train to cross the platform:

As we know,

Time = Distance/Speed

⇒ (900 + 900)/30

⇒ 1800/30

⇒ 60 sec

∴ The train will cross the platform in 60 seconds.

question: A group of 5 friends went to a restaurant. If 4 of them paid Rs. 200 each and the fifth paid Rs. x, the average bill per person came out to be Rs. 210. What is the value of x?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Net Deviation Method:

The given average bill per person is ₹210.

4 friends paid ₹200 each, creating a deficit of ₹10 per person (−10 × 4 = −₹40).

To balance this deficit and maintain the average, the 5th friend must pay the average plus this deficit amount.

x = 210 + 40 = 250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of friends = 5

Amount paid by 4 friends = ₹200 each

Average bill per person = ₹210

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all values ÷ Total number of values

Sum of all values = Average × Total number of values

 Total Bill = 5 × 210 = ₹1050 4 Friends = ₹800 5th Friend = x 
• 
• x = 1050 − 800 = ₹250 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total bill amount = 210 × 5 = ₹1050

⇒ Total amount paid by 4 friends = 200 × 4 = ₹800

⇒ Amount paid by the 5th friend (x) = Total bill − Total amount paid by 4 friends

⇒ x = 1050 − 800

⇒ x = 250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Deviation Method

The sum of the deviations of all observations from their true average is always zero. This property helps find missing individual values rapidly.

Weighted Average

If two distinct groups have quantities n₁ and n₂ with their respective averages A₁ and A₂, the combined average is calculated as (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Constant Change Property

If every term in a series is increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided by a constant value 'k', the new average undergoes the exact same mathematical operation by 'k'.

question: Two pipes A and B can fill an empty tank in 10 hours and 16 hours respectively. They are opened alternately for 1 hour each, opening pipe B first, in how many hours, will the empty tank be filled?
solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A fills the empty tank in 10 hours

Pipe B fills the empty tank in 16 hours

**Concept Used:**

Total work = LCM of time taken by each pipe

**Calculation:**

LCM of 16 and 10 = 80

Let total work be 80 units

Pipe A does = 80/10 = 8 units per hour

Pipe B does = 80/16 = 5 units per hour

Now,

Pipe B & A fill the tank in two hour

⇒ (5 + 8) units

⇒ 13 units

Now,

Each B & A will keep filling the tank for = (80/13) ≈ 6 hours 

After (6 × 2) = 12 hours, the tank will be filled by (13 × 6) = 78 units. 

2 units are yet to be filled

On, 13th hour B will be opened. 

It will take 2/5 hour for B to fill the remaining tank entirely.

Total time = 12 + 2/5 = 12(2)/(5) hours 

**∴ The empty tank will be filled in 12(2)/(5) hours.**

question: Pipe X can fill a tank in 9 hours and Pipe Y can fill it in 21 hours. If they are opened on alternate hours and Pipe X is opened first, in how many hours shall the tank be full?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM of 9 and 21 = 63 units.

Efficiency of X = 7 units/hr, Y = 3 units/hr.

Work done in 1 cycle (2 hours) = 7 + 3 = 10 units.

In 6 cycles (12 hours), work done = 60 units, remaining = 3 units.

X fills the remaining 3 units in 3/7 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 ³/₇ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe X = 9 hours

Time taken by Pipe Y = 21 hours

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 X

 Y

 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work to be done = 63 units

⇒ Pipes are opened alternately starting with X.

⇒ Work done in 1st hour by X = 7 units

⇒ Work done in 2nd hour by Y = 3 units

⇒ Total work done in a 2-hour cycle = 7 + 3 = 10 units

⇒ In 6 cycles (12 hours), work done = 10 × 6 = 60 units

⇒ Remaining work = 63 − 60 = 3 units

⇒ In the 13th hour, it is Pipe X's turn.

⇒ Time taken by X to fill the remaining 3 units = 3 ÷ 7 hours

Alternate Working Rule

When entities work on alternate hours or days, calculate the work done in one complete cycle, multiply to get closest to the total work, and assign the remaining work to the entity whose turn is next.

Pipes & Cisterns

It operates similarly to Time and Work problems. The total capacity of the tank acts as Total Work (LCM of individual times) and the rate of filling is the Efficiency.

Emptying Pipes

If a pipe empties the tank instead of filling it, its efficiency is taken as negative, reducing the overall net work done per cycle.

question: A, B, and C are capable of completing a job in 30, 45, and 90 days, respectively. A works every day, while B and C join A every fifth day. How long will it take to finish the task?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(30, 45, 90) = 90 units.

Efficiencies: A = 3, B = 2, C = 1.

Work done in a 5-day cycle = (3 × 5) + 2 + 1 = 18 units.

Number of cycles = Total work ÷ Work per cycle = 90 ÷ 18 = 5 cycles.

Total days = 5 cycles × 5 days/cycle = 25 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Calculations:**

⇒ In 1 cycle of 5 days, A works for all 5 days, while B and C work only on the 5th day.

⇒ Work done by A in 5 days = 5 × 3 = 15 units

⇒ Work done by B and C on the 5th day = 2 + 1 = 3 units

⇒ Total work done in 5 days = 15 + 3 = 18 units

⇒ Number of 5-day cycles required to complete 90 units = 90 ÷ 18 = 5 cycles

⇒ Total time taken = 5 cycles × 5 days/cycle = 25 days

Total Work Concept

Total work is considered as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the days taken by individuals. Efficiency is the work done per unit time (Total Work ÷ Days).

Alternate or Cyclic Work

Find the work done in one complete cycle. Divide the total work by the work per cycle to find the number of cycles, then multiply by days per cycle to find the total time required.

Pipes and Cisterns

Works exactly on the same principle as Time and Work, but pipes that empty the tank are assigned a negative efficiency value.
</p

Total Work Rule

Total Work is often considered as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the days taken by different individuals to complete the given task.

Work Efficiency

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Total Days. It represents the units of work done by a person in a single day.

Alternate Day Work

When people work in a specific periodic pattern, sum their combined work into a cycle and find the total time by finding the number of full cycles needed.

Combined Efficiency

When individuals work together on any given day, their combined efficiency is simply the sum of their individual daily efficiencies.

question: A takes 4 times as much time as B or 5 times as much time as C to finish a piece of work. Working together, they can finish the work in 4 days. B can do the work alone in:

question: P and Q can do a job in 24 days, Q and R can do it in 30 days, while P and R can do it in 40 days. X is four times as efficient as P, Y is half as efficient as Q, and Z is 2.5 times as efficient as R. Determine the number of days required to complete the same job if X, Y and Z work together.
solution:
Given:

P and Q can do a job in 24 days, Q and R can do it in 30 days, while P and R can do it in 40 days. X is four times as efficient as P, Y is half as efficient as Q, and Z is 2.5 times as efficient as R. Determine the number of days required to complete the same job if X, Y and Z work together.

Concept used:

Efficiency = (Total work / Total time taken)

Efficiency = work done in a single day

Calculation:

Let total work is 120 units ( LCM of 24, 30 , and 40 and)

The efficiency of P+Q = 120 /24

⇒ 5 units

The efficiency of Q+R = 120 / 30

⇒ 4 units

The efficiency of P+R = 120 / 40

⇒ 3 units

Total efficiency of P + Q + R is (4+ 5 + 3) / 2 = 6

The efficiency of P is 6 - 4 = 2 units

The efficiency of X is 2 × 4 = 8 units

The efficiency of Q is 6 - 3 = 3 units

The efficiency of Y is 3 × .5 = 1.5 units

The efficiency of R is 6 - 5 = 1 unit

The efficiency of Z is 1 × 2.5 = 2.5 units

Total efficiency of X + Y + Z is (8+ 1.5 + 2.5) = 12 units

The number of days required to complete the same job if X, Y and Z work together is,

120 /12 = 10days

**∴ The correct option is 4**
